jobs.title: Country Safeguards Manager
jobs.description:
**Program Background**

Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across the Pacific and Timor-Leste. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of 17 years of Australian Government support for skills and training in the Pacific.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**The Role**
The Country Safeguards Manager is responsible for leading the implementation, coordination and continuous improvement of safeguarding systems across the Paciﬁc Australia Skills Solomon Islands program. The role provides strategic and technical leadership to ensure safeguarding is effectively integrated into program planning, procurement, partnership management, activity implementation and organisational operations. The position is accountable for ensuring compliance with DFAT safeguarding requirements, DT Global safeguarding policies, procedures and Paciﬁc Australia Skills safeguarding strategy through the delivery of safeguarding risk management, due diligence, incident management, monitoring, compliance and capacity strengthening activities. The Country Safeguards Manager also supports the development of a strong safeguarding culture by promoting accountability, prevention, respectful behaviours and continuous organisational learning.

**Reporting Relationship**

The Country Director provides overall leadership, operational oversight and performance management of the position, ensuring safeguarding is integrated into country operations and strategic priorities. The Regional Safeguards Manager provides specialist technical advice, professional supervision and quality assurance to ensure consistent implementation of safeguarding policies, procedures and standards across Pacific Australia Skills.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

## 1. **Strategic Safeguarding Leadership**

- Lead the implementation of the Pacific Australia Skills Safeguarding Strategy and annual country safeguarding workplan, ensuring safeguarding is embedded across all aspects of program delivery in Solomon Islands.
- Provide strategic and technical advice to the Country Director and Country Leadership Team on safeguarding risks, compliance obligations, emerging issues and continuous improvement initiatives.
- Champion a culture of safeguarding, accountability and respectful behaviours by promoting awareness, prevention and shared responsibility across the program.
- Ensure safeguarding considerations are integrated into program planning, activity design, procurement, partnership development and operational decision-making.
- Contribute to regional safeguarding priorities and support the consistent application of safeguarding standards across Pacific Australia Skills.

## 2. **Safeguarding Risk Management and Due Diligence**

- Lead the implementation of safeguarding due diligence processes for implementing partners, contractors, service providers and other stakeholders in accordance with DFAT and DT Global safeguarding requirements and procedures.
- Conduct Safeguards Risk and Capacity Assessments and develop practical safeguarding plans to strengthen organisational capability and compliance.
- Review and provide technical quality assurance of Activity Safeguards Risk Assessments, ensuring risks are appropriately identified, mitigated, monitored and documented.
- Monitor implementation of safeguarding mitigation measures and partner action plans, providing technical support to address identified gaps and strengthen safeguarding systems.
- Work collaboratively with procurement, partnerships and program teams to ensure safeguarding considerations are appropriately incorporated throughout the partnership lifecycle.

## 3. **Incident Management and Case Coordination**

- Ensure safeguarding incidents are reported, managed and escalated within required timeframes while maintaining confidentiality and appropriate information management.
- Coordinate survivor-centred and child-centred responses, including referrals to appropriate support services and monitoring implementation of agreed actions.
- Provide technical advice and support to managers and staff in responding to safeguarding concerns and implementing appropriate risk mitigation measures.

## 4. **Capacity Development and Technical Support**

- Coordinate and deliver safeguarding induction, briefings, awareness and capacity strengthening initiatives for Pacific Australia Skills staff, implementing partners, government stakeholders, contractors and service providers.
- Build safeguarding capability through coaching, mentoring and ongoing technical support to Safeguards Focal Points and key stakeholders.
- Support partners to strengthen safeguarding governance, policies, procedures, reporting mechanisms and organisational practices aligned with DFAT safeguarding requirements.
- Promote continuous learning by identifying emerging safeguarding issues, lessons learned and opportunities to strengthen organisational capability.

## 5. **Monitoring, Compliance and Quality Assurance**

- Monitor safeguarding implementation through regular field visits, compliance reviews, partner engagement and activity monitoring to assess the effectiveness of safeguarding measures.
- Track implementation of safeguarding action plans, recommendations and corrective actions, ensuring timely follow-up and continuous improvement.
- Prepare high-quality safeguarding reports, dashboards, risk analyses, briefing papers and technical updates for the Country Director, Regional Safeguards Manager and other stakeholders as required.
- Monitor compliance with DT Global safeguarding policies, Codes of Conduct, DFAT safeguarding requirements and contractual safeguarding obligations.
- Contribute to internal audits, assurance processes and organisational reporting to demonstrate safeguarding compliance and program performance.

## 6. **Stakeholder Engagement and Partnerships**

- Develop and maintain effective working relationships with government agencies, TVET institutions, employers, civil society organisations, implementing partners, contractors and development partners to strengthen safeguarding outcomes.
- Provide trusted technical advice to internal and external stakeholders on safeguarding policy, risk management and good practice.
- Work closely with Rural Training Centres (RTCs) in Solomon Islands to strengthen safeguarding practices through tailored assessments, training and technical support, with follow-up on agreed improvement actions that reflect their local contexts and training environments.
- Represent Pacific Australia Skills in safeguarding-related meetings, working groups, technical forums and partner consultations as delegated by the Country Director.
- Foster collaborative partnerships that strengthen safeguarding capability, promote organisational learning and support sustainable safeguarding systems across the program.

## 7. **Other Responsibilities**

- Contribute to regional safeguarding initiatives, Communities of Practice, cross-country learning and the continuous improvement of safeguarding systems across Pacific Australia Skills.
- Support the development, review and continuous improvement of safeguarding policies, guidance materials, tools, templates and training resources.
- Participate in organisational planning, learning and knowledge management activities to strengthen safeguarding practice across the program.
- Maintain professional knowledge of emerging safeguarding legislation, DFAT policies, international standards and best practice to ensure continuous improvement in safeguarding approaches.
- Undertake other duties consistent with the responsibilities, classification and level of the position, as reasonably directed by the Lead.
- This TOR may be revised or updated in the future as required.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference: [https://tinyurl.com/56xmkfm8](https://tinyurl.com/56xmkfm8)

**Selection Criteria**

**Essential Experience and Knowledge**

- A tertiary qualification in Social Work, Psychology, Law, Human Rights, International Development, Education, Gender Studies, Public Policy or another relevant discipline. Postgraduate qualifications are desirable.
- Demonstrated experience (minimum five years) in safeguarding, child protection, protection from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (PSEAH), gender equality, disability inclusion, protection or a related social development field.
- Demonstrated experience implementing safeguarding systems, policies and procedures within DFAT-funded or other donor-funded international development programs.
- Proven experience conducting safeguarding due diligence, organizational safeguarding assessments, safeguarding risk assessments and developing risk mitigation and capacity strengthening plans.
- Demonstrated experience managing safeguarding incidents in accordance with survivor-centered, child-centered and trauma-informed approaches, while maintaining the highest standards of confidentiality and professionalism.
- Experience designing, facilitating and evaluating safeguarding training, capacity strengthening initiatives and organizational learning programs for diverse stakeholder groups.
- Demonstrated ability to build safeguarding capability through coaching, mentoring and technical advisory support to staff, implementing partners and external stakeholders.
- Excellent analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to assess risk, exercise sound judgement and provide practical safeguarding solutions within complex operating environments.
- Highly developed written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare high-quality reports, technical guidance, briefing papers and presentations for senior management and development partners.
- Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain productive working relationships with governments, development partners, civil society organizations, contractors, service providers and other stakeholders.
- Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, work independently and deliver high-quality outcomes within agreed timeframes.

**Desirable**

- Experience working within the Pacific region, with an understanding of Pacific cultures, governance systems and development contexts.
- Knowledge of Solomon Islands's legislative, policy and institutional framework relating to safeguarding, child protection, gender equality and protection.
- Experience working with Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions, government agencies or education sector programs.
- Demonstrated experience supporting organisational safeguarding system strengthening, policy development or institutional capacity building.
- Experience working on Australian Government (DFAT) funded programs or with other bilateral or multilateral development agencies.
- DT Global strongly encourages applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds including first nations, diverse SOGIESC and people with disabilities.

jobs.title: RESPONSABLE PROGRAMME SMSP - RDC
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision du Coordinateur de Terrain, vous serez responsable de la qualité et de la pertinence de toutes les activités liées à la Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial (SMSP) à Bunia. Vous coordonnerez toutes les activités SMSP.
Dans ce cadre, votre rôle sera d'identifier et de mettre en oeuvre les interventions SMSP de qualité, pertinentes et innovantes dans le respect de la stratégie, des standards ACF, internationaux et des politiques nationales.
Plus précisément vous serez responsable de :
Contribuer à alimenter la réflexion sur la stratégie et les positionnements du département SMSP dans la zone d'intervention
Identifier les besoins et contribuer à la formulation des projets
Assurer la mise en oeuvre, le suivi et le reporting de projets SMSP
Contribuer aux processus qualité et redevabilité et à la mesure d'impact du programme
Participer à la coordination, à la représentation et aux partenariats ACF dans sa zone d'intervention
Encadrer et manager l'équipe SMSP
Contribuer à la capitalisation et au développement technique au sein de ce secteur
Garantir et assurer la confidentialité des données recueillies lors des activités SMSP de la mission

Profile :

Vous êtes titulaire d'un Master 2 en psychologie clinique et en psychopathologie sera exigée.
Vous avez au moins 2 ans d'expérience en tant que psychologue ou psychiatre.
Vous avez de l'expérience dans la prise en charge psychologique de traumatismes psychiques et de la détresse psychologique.
Vous avez au moins 1 an d'expérience dans le domaine de la solidarité internationale, dont au moins 1 an dans la gestion de projets humanitaires et/ou de développement dans le secteur de la SMSP
Vous êtes reconnu pour vos qualités managériales pour des équipes aussi à distance.
Vous avez d'excellentes qualités rédactionnelles en français écrit et oral.
Vous savez travailler et vous adapter à des situations complexes d'un point de vue sécuritaire.
Avoir de l'expérience avec Action Contre la Faim sera un atout.

Conditions d'emploi

La vaccination contre le Mpox est recommandée pour les salarié·e·s qui se rendent dans le pays.

Contrat à durée déterminée d'usage de droit français : 3 mois

Salaire mensuel brut : de 2130 euros à 2406 euros en fonction de l'expérience, incluant 13ème mois

Remboursement assurance retraite pour les citoyens non français : 16% du salaire mensuel brut

Augmentation du salaire de base : 6% tous les 12 mois de contrat continu

Per diem et frais de vie mensuels : 1105$ nets, versés sur le terrain

Allocation contexte mensuelle : 450euros

Allocation enfant : 1500euros par an et par enfant présent dans le pays d'origine (plafond de 6000euros/an)

Transport et logement : Prise en charge des déplacements et logement collectif

Couverture Médicale : 100% de la prise en charge des cotisations santé et assurance rapatriement, de vos frais médicaux et ce jusqu'à 1 mois après la fin de votre contrat

Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)Congés et RnR : 25 jours par an de CP et 20 RnR par an ; prise en charge du billet avec plafond pour se rendre sur la zone de break choisie, et 215euros d'indemnité forfaitaire par RnR

Accompagnement et formation
Suivi et accompagnement parcours professionnel
Accès illimité et gratuit à plateforme d'e-learning Talentsoft

jobs.title: Documentation Assistant
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Land Resources Division (LRD)** provides effective expert scientific advice, capacity building and services on conservation, development and utilization of plant genetic resources, forest and landscape management, resilient agricultural systems, diversification of livelihood strategies and access to markets to maintain ecosystem services and improve land productivity and the food, nutrition security and resilience of Pacific communities. LRD has expertise in genetic resource conservation, resilient agriculture, biosecurity, pest and disease management, agricultural extension, plant pathology, entomology and animal health. It collaborates with governments, regional organisations, civil society and other SPC divisions to pinpoint the needs and priorities of Pacific countries and communities and provide technical expertise to address them. This mission is realized through four main thematic work areas, or pillars, and a progressively integrated approach to programming that works towards achieving SPC’s development goals.

The role – **Documentation Assistant** will provide routine documentation, data-entry and records support for CePaCT. The purpose of the role is to strengthen the genebank's day-to-day documentation and data-entry capacity. The position will enter information only from validated source records, digitise files and documents, prepare routine records and labels, and check information for completeness. The position reports to the Curator, CePaCT, and will work closely with the Documentation & Database Technician for technical guidance on approved GGCE, database, data-standard and documentation procedures.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Routine CePaCT Data Entry and Records Maintenance**

- Enter or update routine records in GGCE and other approved systems from validated source records supplied by responsible staff.
- Process assigned records arising from acquisition, conservation, regeneration, characterisation/evaluation, health testing or diagnostics, inventory, distribution, safety duplication and other approved CePaCT activities.
- Enter legacy or backlog records using approved naming, coding and data-entry procedures.

**Documentation Digitisation, Filing and Records Support**

- Scan and digitise approved paper records and save them in the correct electronic location.
- Apply approved file names, folder structures and document-control conventions.
- Maintain orderly physical and electronic records and retrieve documents when requested.

**CePaCT Operational Documentation Barcode and Inventory Support**

- Prepare and print barcode labels from approved accession or inventory identifiers using established procedures.
- Carry out routine readability and identifier checks before labels are issued or applied.
- Support stock takes and inventory reconciliation by comparing approved lists or system records with information supplied by responsible technical staff.

**Documentation Quality, MS and User Support**

- Follow approved SOPs and work instructions for data entry, document control, confidentiality and record security.
- Assist with routine documentation checks, file retrieval and preparation of records for internal reviews or audits.
- Direct staff to current approved forms and routine documentation procedures and refer technical or procedural queries to the appropriate responsible staff.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- A diploma in library and information services, administration or a related field, or an equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 1 year of relevant experience in data entry, records, administration or information support.
- Good computer literacy, particularly Microsoft Excel, Word and routine electronic records systems.
- Accurate keyboard and data-entry skills with strong attention to detail.
- Ability to follow written procedures, maintain confidentiality and work within delegated authority.
- Good organisation, communication and teamwork skills.
- Ability to identify missing or inconsistent information and refer it appropriately.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **1 year** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration –** The **Documentation Assistant** is a band 5 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a commencing taxable salary range of FJD 1,636-2,045 per month, plus local staff benefits. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration being given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised locally (EPAL) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides medical and life insurance for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Recruitment principles** –SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**.

Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.description:
**Application deadline:** Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized. Follow up with any referrals made to other programs.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Case Coordination Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20.97/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Current Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

jobs.description:
**Información general sobre INSO**
Fundada en 2011, International NGO Safety Organisation (INSO) es una organización internacional no gubernamental sin ánimo de lucro que apoya a los trabajadores de ayuda humanitaria mediante el establecimiento de plataformas de coordinación de la gestión de riesgos en contextos inseguros. INSO ofrece a las ONG registradas una serie de servicios gratuitos, como seguimiento de situaciones en tiempo real, informes analíticos, datos y cartografía relacionados con la seguridad humanitaria, apoyo a la gestión de crisis, orientación y formación del personal. INSO presta apoyo diario a más de 1000 ONG en una veintena de países. INSO tiene su sede en La Haya (Países Bajos), la ciudad internacional de la paz y la justicia.

**INSO Colombia**

INSO Colombia inició operaciones en octubre de 2024. La oficina central está ubicada en Bogotá, con el objetivo de abrir sucursales en varias regiones del país en los próximos meses.

**Objetivo general del cargo**

El/la Oficial de Finanzas y Contabilidad apoyará la gestión financiera y contable de la organización, asegurando registros precisos y oportunos, cumplimiento de la normativa colombiana, políticas internas, requisitos de Casa Matriz y donantes. Bajo la supervisión del/la Finance Manager, colaborará con Finanzas, Operaciones, RR. HH. y programas en contabilidad general, cierres mensuales, conciliaciones, impuestos, nómina, tesorería, anticipos, reportes financieros, seguimiento presupuestal, control interno y auditorías, asumiendo responsabilidades delegadas o de sustitución cuando sea necesario.

**Principales deberes y responsabilidades**

- Realizar el cierre contable mensual, incluyendo registros, causaciones, provisiones, conciliaciones, ajustes y validación de saldos y cuentas de balance.
- Preparar y presentar los estados financieros, notas y demás reportes contables requeridos por la organización, la sede internacional y las autoridades competentes.
- Garantizar que los registros, estados financieros y reportes cumplan con la normativa contable colombiana y las NIIF para PYMES aplicables.
- Emitir y firmar estados financieros, certificaciones y demás documentos que requieran firma profesional, de acuerdo con la legislación vigente y los requisitos de la Junta Central de Contadores.
- Mantener registros contables completos, actualizados y debidamente soportados, asegurando la trazabilidad y consistencia entre los sistemas locales y los reportes de la sede.
- Gestionar y revisar pagos, conciliaciones bancarias y de cuentas, anticipos, depósitos, cuentas por cobrar y cuentas por pagar.
- Preparar y liquidar las obligaciones tributarias nacionales y distritales aplicables, incluyendo ICA y retención en la fuente, asegurando su presentación oportuna y el cumplimiento de los calendarios fiscales.
- Mantener actualizada la información fiscal de la organización y atender los requerimientos de las autoridades tributarias.
- Revisar y registrar mensualmente la información de nómina, seguridad social, prestaciones sociales y parafiscales antes de su contabilización.
- Revisar y gestionar la contabilización y archivo de legalizaciones de viajes, anticipos, reembolsos y gastos operativos, de acuerdo con las políticas internas y requisitos fiscales.
- Mantener el archivo contable físico y digital organizado, completo y disponible para auditorías y revisiones.
- Preparar información, reportes y documentación de soporte para auditorías internas, externas, de donantes, de la sede internacional y de las autoridades competentes.
- Elaborar y presentar reportes financieros periódicos a la Gerencia de Finanzas y la sede internacional, de acuerdo con los calendarios establecidos.

**Perfil requerido**

*Requisitos esenciales*

- Mínimo 4 años de experiencia en contabilidad, cierres contables, estados financieros, conciliaciones, impuestos, nómina y reportes financieros en Colombia.
- Sólidos conocimientos de normativa contable colombiana, NIIF para PYMES, obligaciones tributarias nacionales y distritales, nómina, seguridad social y controles internos.
- Manejo avanzado de Microsoft Excel y Microsoft Office, para análisis, conciliaciones, cierres y elaboración de reportes.
- Contador(a) Público(a) titulado(a), con tarjeta profesional vigente en Colombia y habilitado(a) para ejercer y firmar estados financieros y demás documentos que requieran firma profesional.
- La tarjeta profesional deberá estar vigente y en condiciones que permitan el ejercicio profesional conforme a los requisitos de la Junta Central de Contadores y demás normas legales aplicables en Colombia.
- Capacidad para gestionar altos volúmenes de información con precisión, confidencialidad, organización y atención al detalle.
- Buenas habilidades de comunicación, trabajo en equipo y coordinación con áreas operativas, oficinas de campo y sede internacional.

*Deseable*

- Experiencia en ONG, cooperación internacional, entidades sin ánimo de lucro o entornos con reportes a casa matriz, donantes o sedes internacionales.
- Experiencia con software contable local, preferiblemente Siigo, y conocimiento de sistemas corporativos como SUNSYSTEM u otros ERP financieros.
- Inglés intermedio, especialmente para lectura y redacción de reportes, comunicaciones financieras y documentación de la sede internacional.

**Competencias Clave**

- Comunicación – Transmite información de manera clara y efectiva, adapta su comunicación a diferentes interlocutores y mantiene relaciones de trabajo positivas con equipos internos y externos.
- Organización – Planifica, prioriza y coordina tareas de manera eficiente, gestionando múltiples actividades y plazos con precisión y atención al detalle.
- Autonomía – Trabaja de forma independiente, toma iniciativas y asume responsabilidades, manteniendo altos estándares de calidad y cumplimiento.
- Integridad – Actúa con ética, confidencialidad y transparencia, previniendo conflictos de interés y garantizando el manejo responsable de la información.
- Adaptabilidad – Mantiene un desempeño efectivo bajo presión y trabaja de manera respetuosa y colaborativa en entornos multiculturales y dinámicos.

**Política de protección de INSO**

INSO está plenamente comprometida con la contratación, selección e investigación de antecedentes seguras de todos los posibles nuevos miembros del personal, administradores y voluntarios, y garantizará el cumplimiento riguroso de nuestro Código de Conducta y nuestra Política de Salvaguardia a lo largo de todo el proceso de contratación.

**Condiciones de empleo**

- Fecha de inicio deseada: enero 2027
- Lugar de contrato: Bogotá D.C.
- Contrato: laboral, término fijo.
- Salario base mensual de $5.265.300 COP.
- 17 días laborales de vacaciones anuales.
- Puesto presencial, con 2 días de teletrabajo semanales.

jobs.title: Senior Analyst for Somalia
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
## **BACKGROUNG ON REACH AND IMPACT INITIATIVES**

REACH is an initiative of Acted whose purpose is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

**We are currently looking for a Senior Analyst to support our team in Somalia, based in Mogadishu.**

**Department**: REACH

**Position**: Senior Analyst

**Contract duration**: 4 months, with possibility of extension

**Location**: Mogadishu, Somalia

**Starting Date**: 1 January 2027

## **COUNTRY PROFILE**

Somalia remains within a complex and protracted crisis due to active conflict, the presence of non-state armed actors, the persistent presence of communicable diseases and climate-driven onset shocks – including droughts and flooding. Conflict and natural disasters continue to drive displacement and constrain the availability of resources, while the presence of armed groups severely impedes the level of access and support provided by humanitarian actors. The combination of restricted access to resources, drought, and flooding further exacerbates the possibility for outbreaks of communicable diseases like measles, cholera, and acute watery diarrhea (AWD).

Against this backdrop, REACH has developed a wide range of research cycles to provide an evidence base for the humanitarian community. This includes the Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessment (MSNA), the Acute Needs Analysis (ANA), the Area-Based Analysis Platform aimed at supporting Area-Based Coordination, support to the Somali Cash Consortium, among others.

## **FUNCTIONS**

Under the line management of the Deputy Country Representative, the Senior Analyst is responsible for overseeing the delivery of concise, actionable analysis on acute humanitarian needs at both national and sub-national levels, using REACH own data as well as secondary sources. At a time when the humanitarian system is facing unprecedented constraints, this role will be critical in ensuring that increasingly scarce resources are prioritised according to evidence of need.

The Senior Analyst will line manage two team members, including the Analyst who leads REACH Somalia’s Acute Needs Analysis (ANA) and the Analyst who supports the Area-Based Analysis Platform, providing them with technical oversight, quality assurance and day-to-day support. The Senior Analyst will also contribute to developing and maintaining the Area-Based Analysis Platform to support Area-Based Coordination, and help ensure that the extensive data collected by REACH in Somalia is translated into timely, decision-oriented insights.

The role offers a unique opportunity to shape analysis that directly informs humanitarian prioritisation and decision-making processes, including – but not limited to – the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP), the IPC, and donor resource allocation. The position is well suited to technically strong candidates who are comfortable working with large and complex datasets, while also able to situate their analysis within the broader humanitarian context to maximise operational relevance and impact. It involves close collaboration with GIS, data, and assessment colleagues to ensure that findings are communicated clearly and effectively, including through visual products where appropriate. The Senior Analyst should feel comfortable in front of a room: networking, socializing ideas, responding to questions, building and maintaining relationships, and positioning data in decision-making.

## **RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Senior Analyst’s responsibilities include:

***AREA-BASED ANALYSIS PLATFORM***

- Contribute to the continued design, development and maintenance of the Area-Based Analysis Platform to support Area-Based Coordination, including the synthesis of multiple data sources at sub-national level;
- Lead on the continued technical development of the platform’s analytical framework, including the selection, definition, calculation and validation of indicators and metrics drawn from a range of humanitarian data sources, ensuring they are methodologically sound, comparable across areas and fit for decision-making;
- Support joint analysis with Area-Based Coordination partners, ensuring outputs respond to the information needs of sub-national coordination structures.

***ACUTE NEEDS ANALYSIS***

- Oversee the delivery of the Acute Needs Analysis, ensuring that the Analyst leading it applies REACH’s global Acute Needs Analysis guidance and framework consistently;
- Review analysis, analytical outputs and products before they are submitted to HQ for validation, ensuring they are concise, high-impact and decision-oriented.

***NEEDS ANALYSIS WORKING GROUP***

- In coordination with OCHA, lead the set-up of a national-level Needs Analysis Working Group (NAWG) co-chaired by REACH, including drafting the NAWG ToR, defining its objectives, membership and workplan, and building buy-in from clusters, UN agencies, NGOs and donors;
- Lead the design of the NAWG’s analytical framework for regular intersectoral analysis, building on existing data sources such as the MSNA, the ANA, IPC analyses and cluster data, and work with Data staff to create the backend analysis system;
- Once a NAWG has been established:
- Co-chair the NAWG alongside OCHA, facilitating monthly meetings, including preparing agendas, presentations and minutes, and following up on action points with members;
- Facilitate joint analysis among NAWG members, including organising joint analysis sessions, harmonising indicators and thresholds, and consolidating inputs from clusters and partners;
- Ensure that NAWG outputs are concise, decision-oriented and timed to feed into the ICCG;
- Maintain an overview of planned and ongoing assessments and information gaps among NAWG members, promoting the coordination of assessments to avoid duplication;
- Present NAWG findings to the ICCG and other coordination fora and donors, as required.

***DATA REVIEW AND ANALYSIS***

- Review, synthesise, and assess secondary data from REACH, UN agencies, INGOs, and public sources, evaluating data quality and identifying data gaps;
- Ensure effective use of existing REACH data collected in Somalia, including the MSNA and other assessments, to produce timely, decision-oriented insights;
- Contribute to learning and methodological improvements for future analytical work in Somalia.
- Ensure that the production of analysis and outputs are aligned with key decision-making moments in the humanitarian response, including the HPC and donor allocation processes.

***STAFF MANAGEMENT***

- Line manage two team members, including the Analyst leading the Acute Needs Analysis, including setting work plans and objectives, conducting regular check-ins and appraisals, and supporting their professional development;
- Provide technical guidance, backstopping and quality assurance on analytical approaches, methods and outputs produced by the team;
- Support the capacity building of team members and the wider REACH Somalia mission in structured analysis, synthesis of multiple data sources, and drafting of decision-oriented outputs.

***DISSEMINATION MANAGEMENT***

- Ensure the drafting of timely and accurate analytical products, in collaboration with GIS, data, and assessment colleagues, which comply with REACH’s guidelines and quality standards;
- Ensure that products accurately reflect the information collected and that information is conveyed in a way that maximizes their impact for the intended audiences;
- Maintain regular communication with country management and HQ on progress and deadlines for deliverables, and ensure that all written products are validated by HQ before external release;
- After validation by the line manager, present findings to coordination fora and donors as required.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- Build contextual understanding and stakeholder networks at national and sub-national levels to ensure outputs are relevant, credible, and aligned with decision-making needs;
- Contribute to the Community Engagement and Accountability Taskforce (CEATF), including by sharing relevant REACH data and analysis on community perspectives and priorities, and integrating accountability considerations into REACH’s analytical work;
- Ensure that all partner engagement and external relations are clearly documented and communicated with the line manager and relevant colleagues;
- Lead in establishing a Needs Analysis Working Group (NAWG), and provide support to other national-level needs analysis processes with OCHA and partners, including contributing to analytical framework design for regular intersectoral analysis and decision-oriented outputs for the ICCG and HPC.

***DATA CONFIDENTIALITY AND PROTECTION***

- The Senior Analyst will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes, ensuring full compliance with REACH’s data protection policy and SOPs. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to REACH and its partners or collected during their assignment with REACH.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- **Academic qualifications** Excellent academic qualifications, preferably including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. international studies, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, statistics, etc).
- **Years of work experience** 3 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting, such as assessments, needs analysis, research design and analysis, etc.
- **Management experience** Experience managing or supervising staff, including providing technical guidance and quality assurance on analytical work.
- **Research skills** Strong quantitative and qualitative analysis skills, with experience interpreting large and complex datasets and the ability to evaluate the quality of different data sources.
- **Analytical skills** Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills, with a proven ability to identify trends, contextualise findings, and synthesise complex information into actionable insights for diverse humanitarian audiences. Very comfortable with the technical aspects of metrics and indicators across humanitarian data, including building and maintaining analytical frameworks.
- **Familiarity with the humanitarian and aid system** Understanding of the HPC and inter-agency needs analysis and assessments, and experience engaging with a variety of stakeholders (clusters, donors, UN agencies) across the humanitarian response.
- **Communication/reporting skills** Strong writing and speaking/presentation skills, with experience producing clear, concise outputs for humanitarian audiences which combine text and visuals for maximum impact.
- **Software skills** Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Skills in R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software are an advantage.
- **Multi-tasking skills** Proven ability to manage workflows and deliver high-quality outputs under tight deadlines.
- **Level of independence** Comfortable working autonomously and with limited direction, with sound judgment, emotional intelligence and the resilience to continue in difficult situations.
- **Experience in geographical region** Prior experience in Somalia would be a strong asset; past experience in the Horn of Africa region or any other emergency context where access is challenging is desirable.
- **Language skills** Fluency in English required, competency in Somali an asset.
- **Security environment** Openness to working in a high-risk security zone required. Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. Ability to prioritize self-care and well-being.

### **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 3’06**0 CHF** and **3’120 CHF** monthly (before income tax), as well as a monthly living allowance of **300 USD**
- NB - REACH salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in a guesthouse. REACH is hosted by Acted in Somalia.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered)
- R&R after 2 months (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in Acted HQ in Paris, including a 4-day in situ security training
- Enrolment in the Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract.
- REACH prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

jobs.description:
**DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS**

10 December 2026-23:59-GMT+05:00 Pakistan Standard Time (Karachi)

**ABOUT WFP**

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks.

At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

To learn more about WFP, visit our website: [https://www.wfp.org](https://www.wfp.org/) and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/c/worldfoodprogramme), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/unwfp/), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/worldfoodprogramme/), [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/WorldFoodProgramme/), [Twitter](https://twitter.com/WFP?ref_src=https://reliefweb.int/twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Eauthor), [TikTok](http://www.tiktok.com/@worldfoodprogramme?lang=en).

**WHY JOIN WFP?**

- WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.
- WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.
- WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.
- A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.
- We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the **Terms and Conditions** section of this vacancy announcement).

**ABOUT PROGRAMME AND POLICY AT WFP**

Pakistan faces a significant burden of maternal and child malnutrition. Stunting, wasting, anaemia and micronutrient deficiencies remain widespread, and are compounded by poverty, food insecurity, limited uptake of health services, inadequate maternal and young child feeding practices, and recurrent climate and economic shocks. The first 1,000 days, from conception to a child's second birthday, are therefore a critical window for preventing irreversible growth and development deficits.

In 2020, the Government of Pakistan, through the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), launched the Benazir Nashonuma Programme (BNP) with support from the World Food Programme (WFP), UNICEF and WHO. BNP is Pakistan's flagship nutrition-sensitive social protection programme and combines conditional cash transfers with specialised nutritious foods, maternal and child health services, social and behaviour change support, growth monitoring, immunisation promotion, and prevention and management of acute malnutrition for pregnant and breastfeeding women and children under two.

Since its launch, BNP has evolved from a pilot into a national delivery platform. By June 2026, the programme operated through more than 560 Facilitation Centres and had enrolled over 4.7 million pregnant women and children under two. Independent endline evidence confirms that the integrated BNP model can deliver measurable impact at scale, including substantial reductions in stunting, improved birth outcomes, and increased full immunisation coverage. These results support continuation of the combined cash, nutrition, health and counselling package, while programme learning highlights the need for earlier enrolment in pregnancy, stronger compliance and follow-up, improved coordination with provincial health systems, enhanced data interoperability, and sustained quality and accountability across the Facilitation Centre network.

The third phase of BNP, started in July 2026 for three years, is designed to consolidate these gains and expand services, including to the whole of Pakistan. The new phase places greater emphasis on data-driven and digitised service delivery, Facilitation Centre optimisation, supply-chain efficiency and traceability, coordinated beneficiary identification and case management, stronger national and provincial coordination, integration with health and social protection systems, climate-responsive operations, value for money, and a phased transition toward stronger government ownership and long-term sustainability.

As the programme evolves towards the next phase of implementation and scale, there is a need for dedicated project management leadership to strengthen governance, strategic oversight, performance management, risk management, stakeholder coordination, and delivery assurance across all BNP workstreams.

**THE ROLE**

The position is based in Islamabad and reports to Deputy Country Director.

Under the overall guidance of the Deputy Country Director and in close

collaboration with the Head of Programme, the incumbent will serve as the Project Manager for the Benazir Nashonuma Programme, providing end-to end management and oversight of programme governance, planning, implementation coordination, performance monitoring, risk management, business transformation initiatives, digital solutions, and stakeholder engagement.

The position will act as the central coordination and accountability function across Country Office units, Provincial Offices, Government of Pakistan, cooperating partners, UN agencies, and other stakeholders to ensure timely delivery of programme objectives and achievement of strategic outcomes.

This is a unique position that combines programme management, project governance, strategic coordination, business transformation, and performance oversight to ensure BNP remains effective, accountable, scalable, and aligned with national priorities and WFP strategic objectives.

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES** (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority):

1\. Programme Governance and Strategic Oversight : Serve as the central project management lead for the Benazir Nashonuma Programme; Establish and maintain programme governance structures, accountability mechanisms, and decision-making forums; Advise senior management on programme performance, implementation progress, strategic risks, and opportunities; Develop and oversee programme implementation roadmaps, milestone tracking frameworks, and annual work plans; Ensure alignment between programme activities, country strategic objectives, and government priorities; Support strategic planning for the future evolution and scale-up of BNP and related social protection initiatives.

2\. Stakeholder Coordination and Partnership Management: Lead coordination among WFP functional units, Provincial Offices, BISP Secretariat, government counterparts, UN agencies, and cooperating partners; Facilitate programme governance forums, steering committees, and coordination meetings; Develop and oversee stakeholder engagement plans and communication frameworks; Strengthen strategic relationships to support programme delivery and sustainability; Ensure effective information flow and collaboration across all levels of programme implementation

3\. Performance Management and Delivery Assurance: Establish programme performance management systems and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs); Monitor implementation performance against plans, targets, and commitments; Lead programme performance reviews and identify corrective actions where required; Prepare executive reports,

dashboards, and briefing materials for senior management and stakeholders; Ensure programme activities remain focused on achieving intended results and impact.

4\. Risk Management and Compliance: Establish and maintain a comprehensive programme risk register; Identify emerging strategic, operational, financial, and reputational risks; Develop mitigation measures and monitor implementation of agreed actions; Ensure compliance with WFP policies, procedures, donor requirements, and partnership agreements; Support audit responses and implementation of audit recommendations.

5\. Digital Solutions and Innovation: Lead the planning and implementation of the BNP digital transformation roadmap; Oversee initiatives related to beneficiary systems, digital monitoring tools, traceability solutions, and operational automation; Coordinate technical teams and stakeholders involved in digital initiatives; Identify innovative approaches to improve programme efficiency, accountability, and service delivery.

6\. Business Improvement and Change Management: Identify opportunities to strengthen programme governance, efficiency, and effectiveness; Lead business process reviews and continuous improvement initiatives; Drive change management efforts associated with BNP expansion, redesign, and future phases; Promote the adoption of best practices in programme and project management. Retrofit programme design based on evidence generated, feedback from beneficiaries, and recommendations from the Government.

7\. Cooperating Partner and Operational Excellence: Oversee the development of performance management frameworks for cooperating partners; Strengthen accountability and monitoring systems for implementing partners; Review operational delivery models and recommend improvements to enhance programme performance; Support development of future implementation models for BNP 3.0 and beyond.

8\. Supervise a team of 10-15 people, set priorities and performance expectations, clarify roles and accountabilities, promote collaboration, and support staff development and wellbeing.

9\. Lead cross-functional coordination within WFP and with other UN agencies, and with government at federal and provincial levels.

10\. Perform other related duties as required to support effective, accountable and sustainable delivery of the Benazir Nashonuma Programme.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

**Education**: Advanced University degree in Project Management, Public Policy, Development Studies, International Relations, Business Administration (MBA), Public Administration, Economics, Social Sciences, Nutrition, Public Health, or related fields or First University Degree with additional years of relevant professional experience and demonstrated project management expertise.

**Experience:**

- At least 8 years of progressively responsible professional experience in programme management, development programming, public sector reform, social protection, or humanitarian/development operations.
- Proven experience managing large and complex multi-stakeholder projects or programmes.
- Experience overseeing programme governance, implementation planning, performance monitoring, and risk management.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams across various functions and locations.
- Demonstrated experience supporting government systems and formulating and/or implementing solutions to reinforce them.
- Experience managing public health interventions at scale a plus.
- Experience managing digital solutions, or nutrition programme a plus\*\*.\*\*

**Knowledge &** **Skills**:

- Programme and Project Management methodologies and tools
- Programme governance frameworks
- Strategic planning and results-based management.
- Risk management and mitigation frameworks
- Performance monitoring and KPI management.
- Stakeholder engagement and partnerships management.
- Change management and business process improvement.
- Budget monitoring and resource management.
- Project lifecycle management.
- Monitoring, evaluation, learning, and reporting.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Experience utilizing data and analytics to support decision-making.

**Language**: Fluency (level C) in English language. Any other UN languages, a plus.

**TERMS AND CONDITIONS**

- This is an International Professional position and candidates must be a national of a country other than the country of assignment.
- The selected candidate will be employed on a limited fixed-term contract of 1 year renewable.
- Limited Fixed-Term Appointment (LFT) position is a non-mobile staff appointment in the international professional category for a limited period for up to 4 years.
- The position is based in **Islamabad, Pakistan** and the selected candidate will be expected to relocate.
- Incumbents of LFT positions are not eligible to apply for other mobile positions advertised internally through the Reassignment.
- WFP offers an attractive compensation and benefits package in line with ICSC standards ([http://icsc.un.org](http://icsc.un.org)) including basic salary, post adjustment, relocation entitlement, visa, travel and shipment allowances, 30 days’ annual leave, home leave, an education grant for dependent children, a pension plan, and medical insurance.

jobs.title: Procurement Associate
jobs.description:
## OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

WHO’s work in countries operationalizes the General Programme of Work (GPW14) and the European Programme of Work 2025-2029 (EPW2). GPW14 focuses on accelerating progress toward Health for All by strengthening systems for health, improving access to essential services, advancing preparedness and resilience, and reducing health inequalities. EPW2, endorsed at RC75 following extensive consultation with Member States, reaffirms WHO/Europe’s role in bringing unique value to countries through five core functions:
1\. International knowledge hub for health – providing authoritative evidence, norms, policies and best practices from across the Region and globally to inform national public health decision-making.
2\. Impartial coordinator for everyone’s health – convening national stakeholders and partners to align strategies and support coherent, multisectoral responses to shared health challenges.
3\. Leader in tracking and managing cross-border health threats – supporting surveillance, preparedness, and coordinated action on public health emergencies in line with the Preparedness 2.0 agenda.
4\. Driver of health system transformation – advising national authorities on evidence-informed reforms and policies that strengthen health systems and improve performance.
5\. Voice for health equity – helping countries identify who is being left behind and integrating equity considerations into health policies and strategies.

In this context, WHO Country Offices enable the translation of global and regional commitments into national action. They support Member States by providing strategic advice, convening dialogue across sectors and partners, connecting national authorities with WHO’s technical expertise, and facilitating the use of evidence and best practices to inform policy.

## DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

1\. Coordinate and manage assigned procurement activities involving more complex requirements, ensuring that procurement actions are undertaken in accordance with WHO rules, regulations and procedures and completed within established timelines. Identify operational challenges and recommend appropriate solutions, referring exceptional or policy-sensitive matters to the Procurement Officer.
2\. Review procurement requests and supporting documentation to ensure completeness, accuracy and compliance with WHO procurement requirements. Identify missing information or inconsistencies and liaise with requesting units to obtain the necessary clarifications before proceeding with procurement actions.
3\. Initiate and follow up purchase requisitions and other procurement transactions in WHO enterprise systems, ensuring complete and accurate procurement records and supporting documentation.
4\. Conduct market research and support the identification and maintenance of suitable suppliers for routine and recurring procurement requirements.
5\. Coordinate competitive procurement processes for assigned cases, including preparation and review of solicitation documents, obtain quotations or bids, administer tender and bidding processes, compile offers, support evaluation of commercial terms and prepare documentation supporting recommendations for award for review by the Procurement Officer and submission to the authorized approving officials.
6\. Provide administrative support to contract and purchase-order management, including monitoring contractual milestones, delivery status, supplier documentation, receipt of goods or services, invoices, payments and closure actions.
7\. Monitor supplier performance at the administrative level, maintain supplier and contract information, follow up delays or non-compliance and escalate material issues to the Procurement Officer.
8\. Coordinate with finance, logistics and requesting units on procurement status, funding or encumbrance issues, delivery, acceptance, customs-related documentation where applicable, payment and closure of procurement actions.
9\. Maintain procurement trackers, supplier databases, contract records and filing systems; produce regular and ad hoc procurement status information and reports and ensure records are complete and readily retrievable.
10\. Follow up implementation of decisions and recommendations arising from relevant procurement review and approval processes and maintain the associated documentation.
11\. Quality assure routine procurement work products and processes; identify recurring bottlenecks or control issues and propose practical process improvements to strengthen timeliness, efficiency and client service.
12\. Provide procedural guidance and briefings to staff on routine procurement procedures, documentation and systems, and support the sharing of good practices and continuous learning.
13\. As assigned, provide work coordination or functional guidance to procurement support staff, including allocation and follow-up of routine tasks, while escalating policy, exception and higher-risk matters to the responsible supervisor.
14\. Maintain accurate and complete procurement data in WHO enterprise resource planning (ERP) and procurement systems, ensuring procurement transactions are processed and updated promptly, supporting documentation is properly recorded, and procurement status can be effectively monitored and reported.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

### Education

**Essential:** Completion of secondary education. Training and certification in a relevant UN operational service area or system.
**Desirable:** University degree in business administration, procurement, supply chain, logistics or a related field. Professional procurement training or certification, such as CIPS or an equivalent qualification, is an asset.

### Experience

**Essential:** A minimum of eight years' experience relevant to procurement support services and transactions, including procurement administration, tender or bidding processes, purchase requisitions and supplier support.
**Desirable:** Experience in procurement support within WHO or another United Nations agency. Experience using Oracle-based systems or another enterprise resource planning system. Experience supporting procurement in an emergency or complex operating environment is an asset. Experience in technical medical procurement.

### Functional Skills

• Sound knowledge of procurement. Service-oriented, problem solving and analytical skills.
• Communication and negotiation skills.
• Ability to manage and prioritize own's work in a systematic way.
• Ability to manage emotions, remain objective and focused even in a changing environment.
• Promotes collaboration and open communication in the team.
• Emotional intelligence; Ability to identify and manage one's own emotions, as well as helping others to do the same.
• Good knowledge in use of an ERP system.
• Ability to use. IT tools to improve workflows, speed of service and reports. Knowledge of WHO and/or other UN systems is an asset

### Other Skills (e.g. IT)

Proficiency in computers and office software packages, web-based management systems and enterprise resource planning systems. Advanced spreadsheet and data-management skills are desirable for procurement planning, monitoring and reporting.

### WHO Competencies

• Teamwork
• Respecting and promoting individual and cultural differences
• Communication
• Producing results

### Use of Language Skills

**Essential:** Expert knowledge of English. Expert knowledge of Ukrainian.

**Desirable:** Intermediate knowledge of any other UN language.

## REMUNERATION

Remuneration comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 27,597 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable) and 30 days of annual leave.
