jobs.title: Contract Manager - Youth Inclusion and Employment Project / DAPP
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Contract Manager - DAPP.**

## **About the job**

The Contract Manager provides integrated project leadership and contractual, financial and compliance oversight for the Danish Arab Partnership Programme (DAPP) Youth Inclusion and Employment Project (YIEP) in Tunisia. The role is accountable for translating the project strategy and contractual commitments into high-quality, timely and cost-effective delivery, coordinating implementing partners, and ensuring that results, budgets, risks and client obligations are actively managed throughout the project cycle.

As the project’s senior day-to-day manager and budget holder, the Contract Manager leads implementation planning, partner and stakeholder coordination, performance monitoring, reporting, forecasting, contract administration and audit readiness. The role works closely with programme and support-service colleagues and draws on technical support from DRC’s HQ Commercial Contracts team.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

### **1. Project leadership and delivery**

- Lead the full project management cycle, from detailed planning to implementation, monitoring, adaptation and close-out.
- Develop, maintain and regularly review the consolidated work plan, implementation schedule, deliverables tracker and resource plan, ensuring clear sequencing, ownership and deadlines.
- Ensure timely and high-quality delivery of project activities, including entrepreneurship support, business-plan development, linkages to finance and employment opportunities, market assessments, and support to cooperatives and small businesses, implemented through a number of local partners.
- Monitor progress against outputs, outcomes, milestones and contractual deliverables; identify bottlenecks and agree corrective actions with project staff and partners.
- Lead regular project coordination and performance-review meetings and ensure decisions and action points are documented and followed through.
- Promote adaptive management by using monitoring data, market evidence, client feedback and lessons learned to adjust implementation while protecting agreed results and compliance.

### **2. Partner, subcontractor and stakeholder management**

- Manage relationships with implementing partners and subcontractors, ensuring shared understanding of scope, deliverables, budgets, quality standards and contractual obligations.
- Provide practical implementation support, maintain regular communication, convene coordination meetings and track completion of agreed partner actions.
- Oversee the development, review and amendment of subcontractor agreements so that they align with the prime contract, approved budgets and DRC requirements.
- Lead performance and compliance reviews of partners and subcontractors, including review of narrative and financial submissions, invoices and supporting documentation.
- Maintain constructive engagement with the client, public institutions, private-sector actors and other relevant stakeholders, and ensure responsiveness to agreed requirements.

### **3. Financial management and commercial performance**

- Act as Budget Holder, overseeing project budgets and financial systems in DRC Dynamics and ensuring expenditure is accurate, eligible, timely and aligned with implementation priorities.
- Lead financial forecasting, budget monitoring and variance analysis across DRC and subcontractors, including tracking burn rate, forecast accuracy, value for money, payment schedules and contractual milestones.
- Maintain the Contract Follow Up (CFU) and provide clear financial management information to project governance and relevant DRC stakeholders.
- Coordinate preparation and submission of compliant client invoices, with complete supporting evidence and documentation of deliverables.
- Prepare budget projections and lead budget amendments in coordination with partners, the Country Office, Regional Office and HQ.

### **4. Contractual compliance, risk and audit**

- Serve as the principal project focal point for compliance with client terms and conditions, including cost eligibility, safeguarding, security, code of conduct, reporting and documentation requirements.
- Maintain effective compliance and quality-assurance systems, including checklists, contract files, decision logs, document-control standards and archiving.
- Maintain the internal project risk matrix, escalate material risks, assign mitigation measures and monitor their completion with programme and support-service teams.
- Ensure project systems remain audit-ready through strong internal controls, complete documentation and timely follow-up of findings from internal or external reviews and audits.
- Coordinate with Finance, HR, Supply Chain, Logistics and other support functions to resolve operational or compliance issues that could affect delivery.

### **5. Monitoring, reporting, learning and communication**

- Ensure an effective system for monitoring activities, results, contractual milestones and data quality throughout implementation.
- Lead timely preparation of accurate, concise and evidence-based narrative, financial and operational reports, including Delivery Reporting Tools and client templates.
- Ensure reports and external communications meet contractual requirements, DRC quality standards and client expectations.
- Document case studies, good practices and lessons learned and ensure they inform project adaptation, future programming and stakeholder communication.
- Provide clear updates to project governance and act as the primary contact for operational, contractual and compliance queries.

### **6. Team coordination and management**

- Provide clear priorities, guidance and day-to-day coordination to project staff, fostering collaboration between programme, MEAL and support service functions.
- Ensure roles, decision-making responsibilities and internal workflows are understood and applied consistently.
- Supervise the DAPP Finance Officer, ensuring timeline work planning, as well as objective setting and monitoring.
- Perform other relevant duties assigned by the line manager.

## **About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have At least 7 years of progressively responsible experience in project delivery and management within the humanitarian, development or private-sector development field, including experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

- At least 2 years of experience in contract management, commercial contracts, framework contracts or comparable donor-funded contractual arrangements.
- Demonstrated experience managing budgets of at least USD 2 million, financial forecasts, invoices, audits and partner or subcontractor agreements.
- Proven ability to lead implementation planning, monitor delivery against milestones and results, manage risks and coordinate corrective action.
- Experience in economic recovery, youth employment, entrepreneurship, market systems or private-sector engagement is strongly desirable.
- Experience working with public institutions and maintaining partnerships with private-sector, finance or entrepreneurship actors is an asset.
- Strong knowledge of donor or client compliance; experience with commercial contracting is a distinct advantage.
- Excellent planning, analytical, problem-solving, negotiation and communication skills, with the ability to work across cultures and functions.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint; experience with ERP and project-management systems is desirable.
- Professional fluency in English is required. Working proficiency in French and/or Arabic is strongly desirable; fluency in both is an advantage.
- Advanced university degree in international development, business administration, economics, social sciences, project management or another relevant field. A bachelor’s degree combined with substantial relevant experience may be accepted.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- Striving for excellence: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- Collaborating: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- Taking the lead: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- Communicating: You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- Demonstrating integrity: You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

## **We offer**

- Contract length: Until Dec 31, 2027
- Band: MF2
- Designation of Duty Station: Tunis
- Suggested Start date: 01 Jan 2027

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Us.

### **Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

Closing date for applications:07 December 2026

jobs.title: Logistics Support Officer
jobs.description:
The Logistics Support Officer will assist the Logistics Coordinator in managing procurement activities, with a particular focus on complex purchases requiring the conduct of tendering processes, supplier pre-qualification procedures and the establishment of framework agreements in accordance with Concern’s procedures. He or she will help to strengthen compliance, quality and efficiency in the mission’s procurement processes. Other operations-related activities (stock management, fleet management, systems management, administration or emergency preparedness) may be carried out in a supporting capacity where necessary but will remain secondary to this primary responsibility. He or she will receive on-the-job support and will contribute to capacity-building for the staff that relate to this responsibility.

**Role title:** Logistics Support Officer – Procurement & Tendering

**Reports to:** Logistics Coordinator - and work closely with base managers, area coordinators, the Head of Human Resources and Administration, the Regional Logistics Adviser, and logistics, finance, human resources and programme staff, as appropriate.

**Terms:** *Fixed-term voluntary role for 6 months.*

**Grade:** Voluntary role – Annual allowance of €12,637

**Requirements:** *The post is based in Goma with travel to Concern’s areas of operation in the provinces of North and South Kivu, and Tanganyika.*

**Start date:** ASAP

**Please note that this role requires fluency in French.**

*Main responsibilities*

- Support the Logistics Coordinator in managing complex procurement procedures requiring national and international calls for tenders.
- Help prepare tender documents, publish them, receive tenders and collate the documentation in accordance with Concern’s procedures.
- Contribute to the preparation of the documents required for procurement committees and provide administrative support for the process.
- Support the coordination of tendering procedures by organising meetings for the preparation, opening and evaluation of tenders, and by ensuring that follow-up actions are carried out and that members related to the process participate.
- Support the implementation and monitoring of the mission’s framework agreements.
- Help organise supplier pre-qualification exercises and update the supplier database.
- Contribute to carrying out market analyses and identifying new procurement opportunities.
- Help review procurement files to ensure they comply with internal procedures and donors’ requirements.
- Support the monitoring of procurement plans and assist programme teams in anticipating their procurement needs.
- Contribute to the improvement of the mission’s procurement tools and processes.
- Take part in capacity-building activities for teams on procurement procedures, calls for tenders and framework agreements.

*Secondary responsibilities*

- Provide ad hoc support for stock and warehouse management activities where required.
- Help monitor transport and fleet operations in line with operational requirements.
- Support the logistical preparation of emergency responses where necessary.
- Take part in training and coaching teams on logistics tools and procedures.
- Carry out any other tasks assigned by the Logistics Coordinator in line with the mission’s operational priorities.

*Essential requirements*

- A bachelor’s degree that relates to a relevant field (logistics, supply chain management, business administration, etc.)
- Technical skills in at least one of the following areas: supply chain management, procurement and tendering
- Security awareness or experience of living in a non-secure environment
- Strong IT skills, including the use of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
- Fluency in French, both spoken and written, and a good command of English
- Ability to organise and prioritise workload, and ability to show initiative where required.
- Ability to work within a multicultural and multidisciplinary team, taking cultural differences into account
- Ability to communicate clearly, patiently and respectfully with colleagues
- Ability to manage stress and work under pressure
- Flexibility, adaptability and patience
- Willingness to live in basic accommodation and travel to remote work locations.
- Extremely detail-oriented and thorough

*Desirable requirements*

- Professional or voluntary experience in Central Africa
- Experience of emergency operations in logistics and supply chain management in humanitarian or development contexts
- Experience in the humanitarian sector or volunteering with an NGO in humanitarian contexts

*Special skills, aptitudes or personal qualities required*

- Good time management, the ability to structure processes and to respond positively and constructively to a rapidly changing operational environment are essential skills.
- Values: humanity, humility, humour
- Approaches: flexible, practical, inclusive
- Attitudes: collaborative, understanding/sensitive, committed

jobs.title: Human Resources Coordinator (F/M) - Afghanistan
jobs.description:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## MdM in Afghanistan

Médecins du Monde re-opened its mission in Afghanistan in 2021 and currently implements programmes in primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), nutrition and harm reduction through a combination of direct implementation and partnerships with local organizations. The mission operates in a complex environment marked by restrictions imposed by de facto authorities, constraints affecting women’s participation and access to services, evolving humanitarian needs and significant challenges for the health system. Current programmes are implemented in Wardak, Farah and Nimroz provinces and place a strong emphasis on community engagement, quality of care and access to essential health services.

In 2025 and 2026, the mission significantly expanded its operations through new funding secured from ECHO, CDCS, and GFFO. The current funding strategy focuses on diversifying the donor portfolio and securing additional funding sources to further expand programmatic coverage. To support this objective, a donor mapping tool has been developed and is regularly updated by the grants officer, in coordination with the deputy general coordinator, to ensure systematic monitoring and follow-up of potential funding opportunities.

## About the role

You will be responsible for defining, adapting, planning, and overseeing the implementation of the mission’s human resources framework, including internal policies and procedures, compensation and benefits, talent management, employee relations and disciplinary processes, career development, learning and development, and team-building initiatives. You will ensure that all HR practices are aligned with the local context and legislation, as well as with MdM’s policies and values.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the general coordinator, your main responsibilities are the following:

**Strategy & planning**

- Lead HR planning and budgeting to ensure adequate staffing capacity
- Maintain and update the mission organizational chart
- Contribute to HR planning for project proposals and amendments
- Monitor and report on key HR indicators
- Ensure compliance with local labor laws and MdM HR standards

**Administration & payroll**

- Oversee employee records and HR databases
- Supervise payroll, tax declarations, and HR reporting
- Ensure implementation of salary grids and compensation policies
- Manage HR administration for expatriate staff

**Team management**

- Recruit, supervise, and evaluate HR team members
- Build team capacity through coaching and training

**Policies & recruitment**

- Develop, update, and implement HR policies and procedures
- Ensure staff awareness and compliance with HR policies
- Lead national staff recruitment processes
- Monitor labor market trends and conduct salary benchmarking
- Support implementation of expatriate HR policies

**Capacity building & employees relations**

- Provide HR guidance and support to managers and field teams
- Coordinate performance management and staff development processes
- Lead training needs assessments and annual training plans
- Support conflict resolution and disciplinary processes
- Promote staff development and internal mobility

**Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH)**

- Ensure implementation of MdM's PSEAH policy and reporting mechanisms
- Raise staff awareness and train HR teams on PSEAH requirements

**Legal compliance**

- Ensure compliance with labor, tax, and immigration regulations
- Supervise visas, work permits, and legal documentation
- Support the renewal of registrations and agreements with authorities

**Who you’ll work with**

You will work closely with the HR advisor at HQ, technical coordinators and support coordinators in the field, among others.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Have at least 3 years of experience in a similar role
- Have demonstrated experience in interpreting and applying the legal and administrative framework of a mission in compliance with organizational policies and procedures
- Have a strong understanding of recruitment and training processes, with the ability to identify, analyze, and address the mission's workforce development and staffing needs
- Have a previous experience with Médecins du Monde (MdM) is a strong asset
- Are fluent in English

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Don't have experience in designing, adapting, and implementing HR procedures, standard operating procedures (SOPs), operational guidelines, and recommendations
- Don't have the ability to work under pressure, in insecure and fast-changing contexts, with sound judgment, diplomacy and adaptability
- You are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of November.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 392 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting in January 2027
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Kabul, Afghanistan
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility.

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Spécialiste Accès Humanitaire et sécurité - CDD 3 mois - H/F/X
jobs.description:
Vous souhaitez mettre vos compétences en accès et sécurité au service de nos programmes internationaux ? Rejoignez notre département Sécurité en tant que **Spécialiste Accès humanitaire et Sécurité.**

Humanité & Inclusion / Handicap International - corécipiendaire du prix Nobel de la paix, est une organisation indépendante et impartiale œuvrant dans des situations de pauvreté et d'exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Au travers de nos actions sur le terrain et de notre plaidoyer, nous répondons aux besoins essentiels des populations vulnérables, améliorons leurs conditions de vie et promouvons le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux. HI est présente dans 56 pays à travers le monde.

Handicap International est un employeur inclusif et offrant l'égalité des chances et accueille particulièrement les candidatures de personnes en situation de handicap.

N’hésitez pas à nous indiquer si vous avez eu besoin d'un aménagement spécial, même lors du premier entretien.

Sous la responsabilité du Global Manager Accès Humanitaire et Sécurité (AHS), le/la Spécialiste Accès Humanitaire et Sécurité (AHS) contribue à développer l'accès humanitaire et la capacité d’intervention de l'organisation.

Pour un portefeuille de pays donné, il/elle agit en tant que Référent technique/ Expert AHS et soutient la ligne managériale (siège, région et pays) et les équipes AHS sur le terrain dans la mise en œuvre des cadres AHS, la sécurité opérationnelle, la gestion des incidents/crises et la définition des stratégies d’accès.

Plus largement, il/elle participe à renforcer la culture de l'AHS au sein de l'organisation.

**Principales responsabilités:**

- Déployer et promouvoir les standards, politiques et outils AHS au sein des programmes.
- Assurer une veille contextuelle permanente et analyser les évolutions sécuritaires, politiques et opérationnelles susceptibles d'impacter les activités.
- Contribuer à l'élaboration, au suivi et à l'adaptation des stratégies d'accès humanitaire.
- Conseiller et accompagner les équipes de direction dans la gestion des enjeux de sécurité et d'accès.
- Fournir une expertise technique en matière d'analyse des risques, de gestion de la sécurité opérationnelle et de prise de décision.
- Garantir l'application des protocoles de gestion des incidents et des crises, et participer à la coordination des réponses lors d'événements majeurs.
- Renforcer les capacités des équipes à travers la formation, le partage de bonnes pratiques et le développement des compétences AHS.
- Participer au recrutement, à l'accompagnement et à l'évaluation des Managers AHS de la région.
- Contribuer à la préparation et à la réponse aux urgences humanitaires afin d'assurer une intervention rapide et efficace.

**Votre profil**

• Vous justifiez d’une expérience d’au moins 3 ans sur le terrain au sein d’ONG humanitaires à des postes de Manager sécurité/ accès humanitaire. Les expériences à des postes de coordination et de renforcement des compétences sont un plus.

• Vous avez vécu des expériences de terrain en contextes d’urgence, complexes et instables incluant des gestion d’incident/de crise.

• Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme universitaire ou certification équivalent en gestion de risques, relations internationales ou autres disciplines pertinente pour le poste, et avez suivi des formations en accès/négociation humanitaire et gestion de la sécurité humanitaire.

Par ailleurs, vous présentez de solides capacités d’analyse et de synthèse, et d'appréhension rapide de nouveaux contextes. Vous maitrisez les concepts, outils et processus liés à la gestion de la sécurité et de l’accès humanitaire et connaissez la pédagogie et techniques de formation / transfert de compétence.

Capables de travailler avec une grande variété de personnel d'origines culturelles différentes, vous êtes reconnu.e pour votre réelle gestion du stress et votre sens de l’humour.

**La maîtrise du Français et de l’anglais sont indispensables à ce poste. La connaissance de l'espagnol est un réel atout.**

**Accessibilité du lieu de travail:**

A Lyon, Les locaux sont facilement accessibles en transports en commun (bus, métro). Un parc à vélos est également à disposition. Au sein du bâtiment, des rampes d'accès et ascenseurs garantissent une meilleure circulation. Tous les postes de travail sont situés en Open Space mais des box sont disponibles à chaque étage pour travailler dans le calme si nécessaire. L’espace de travail est très lumineux.

Une référente handicap est présente pour répondre aux éventuelles questions et vous accompagner dans vos démarches. En fonction de vos besoins, le poste peut être aménagé.

**Conditions du poste:**

\- CDI à pourvoir dès que possible

\- Rémunération à partir de 2857€ mensuels bruts

\- Statut cadre : 34 de congés payés et 13 jours de RTT annuels

\- Accord télétravail avantageux,

\- De nombreuses activités sportives et sociales sont proposées dans nos locaux

jobs.title: Technical Advisor - Maternal and Newborn Health and Nutrition (MNHN)
jobs.description:
**Role**: Full Time

**Contract Duration**: 2 Years, Fixed Term and Contract Renewable

**Reports to**: Senior Technical Advisor - Maternal and Newborn Health and Nutrition (MNHN)

**Location**: Nairobi, Kenya or Dakar, Senegal or Lilongwe, Malawi or Addis Ababa, Ethiopia or Abuja, Nigeria or Dar es Salaam, Tanzania

*This role is open only to candidates who have the legal right to work in the country where the position is based (Kenya, Senegal, Malawi, Ethiopia, Nigeria, or Tanzania).*

**Deadline for submission**: 7 December 2026

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

**About Us**

Founded in 1992, Nutrition International is a global organization dedicated to delivering proven nutrition interventions to those who need them most. Working in partnership with countries, donors and implementers, our experts conduct cutting-edge nutrition research, support critical policy formulation, and integrate nutrition into broader development programs. In more than 60 countries, primarily in Asia and Africa, Nutrition International nourishes people to nourish life.

For more than 30 years now, Nutrition International has focused on delivering low-cost, high-impact, nutrition interventions to people in need, driven by our mission to achieve a world where everyone, everywhere, is free from malnutrition and able to reach their full potential. Nutrition International’s work is guided by a dedicated and talented team of experts working globally, regionally and within countries to end malnutrition worldwide.

**About the NOURISH Investment**

The NOURISH investment (Nurture the ecosystem, Optimize the market, Unlock financing, Reinforce ANC platforms, Integrate and Scale MMS and Calcium for Healthy Futures) is an exciting new multi-country investment designed to accelerate the sustainable scale-up of MMS and strengthen systems for the integration of calcium supplementation across Africa. NOURISH takes a comprehensive, systems-based approach that brings together expertise across the critical areas required for successful scale-up: strengthening health systems, improving local product quality, affordability and availability, advancing sustainable health financing, and fostering the enabling policy and implementation environment needed for long-term success.

At the heart of NOURISH is a commitment to placing women and their nutritional needs at the center of program design and implementation, while ensuring strong government leadership and ownership throughout the scale-up journey. NOURISH connects partners in a coordinated and complementary way, aligning technical expertise, implementation support, and country priorities to accelerate impact.

Funded by Children’s Investment Fund Foundation (CIFF) and led by Nutrition International, the NOURISH consortium brings together a unique combination of global and country-level expertise. Consortium partners currently include UNICEF Ethiopia, Sight and Life Rwanda, and CHAI Ghana, each contributing specialized technical and operational capabilities to support either country-led scale-up or regional efforts.

NOURISH is supporting Ethiopia and Rwanda as the first countries to receive support through the initiative. Over the coming years, up to six additional African countries are expected to benefit from NOURISH support, working alongside governments navigate the pathway from MMS introduction to sustainable national scale-up.

**About the role**

The Technical Advisor provides technical support to ensure NOURISH programming is evidence-informed, high quality, and contributes to achieving intended outcomes. The role works closely with consortium partners and Nutrition International teams to provide technical input into programme implementation, support knowledge generation and learning, contribute to reporting and performance monitoring, and facilitate collaboration to strengthen programme impact.

**Key Duties and Responsibilities:**

**1. Technical Advisory and Programme Support**

Provide technical support to NOURISH by reviewing partner workplans and implementation approaches, applying evidence and programme data to strengthen programme quality, and contributing to technical problem-solving and evidence-informed decision-making.

**2. Knowledge Translation and Learning**

Support knowledge management and learning by synthesizing programme evidence and lessons learned into technical briefs, reports, guidance documents, presentations, and other knowledge products, while contributing to the implementation of the NOURISH learning agenda.

**3. Representation and Stakeholder Engagement**

Represent NOURISH in selected technical meetings, working groups, and partner engagements, build and maintain effective working relationships with consortium partners, government counterparts, and other stakeholders, and provide technical support during country and regional coordination meetings.

**4. Collaboration and Partnership**

Collaborate across the NOURISH team, Nutrition International technical teams, and consortium partners to deliver high-quality programme outputs, provide technical support for workplan implementation, and promote lessons learned and cross-country learning.

**5. NOURISH Reporting and Performance Management**

Contribute technical inputs to partner reports to ensure reporting reflects programme progress and technical achievements, support the review of programme performance data to identify opportunities to strengthen implementation, and assist with documenting technical progress against programme deliverables and results frameworks.

Any other related duties as assigned by the Senior Technical Advisor - Maternal and Newborn Health and Nutrition (MNHN).

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

- No direct supervisory responsibility.
- May provide technical guidance and mentorship to consultants, implementing partners, and junior staff as required.

## **Requirements**

**Education/Professional Designations/Experience**

- Master's degree (or higher) in nutrition, public health nutrition, maternal health and nutrition, nutrition and international development.
- Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible technical experience in international development, public health, nutrition, health systems strengthening, or a related field.
- Over 5 years of experience supporting nutrition programmes in international development, NGO, or public health settings, with demonstrated technical knowledge of maternal nutrition interventions for a healthy pregnancy, including multiple micronutrient supplementation (MMS) and calcium supplementation.
- Experience supporting maternal nutrition programmes at national level in at least two African countries.
- Experience supporting implementation of large-scale nutrition and health systems strengthening programmes.
- Experience contributing technical advice and translating evidence into programme implementation.
- Experience reviewing technical documents, implementation plans, and programme deliverables.
- Experience supporting monitoring, evaluation, learning, and use of programme data.
- Demonstrated experience in market shaping initiatives and approaches.
- Experience working within a consortium.

**Other Specific Skill Requirements:**

**Skills**

- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint.
- Demonstrated understanding of results-based management, performance measurement frameworks and fundamentals of program monitoring and donor reporting.
- Demonstrated understanding and/or experience operationalizing child safeguarding principles and policy.
- A working knowledge of French is an asset.

**Competencies**

- **Organization**: Exceptional organizational and planning skill with a proven ability to prioritize and work in a dynamic fast paced environment.
- **Leadership**: Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively, provide technical guidance, and contribute to successful team performance.
- **Communication**: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate with internal teams and external stakeholders.
- **Relationship Building**: Ability to build and maintain strong relationships with team members, project stakeholders and partner organizations.
- **Cultural Sensitivity**: Ability to navigate diverse cultural environments and tailor solutions to country and regional contexts.

jobs.title: MEAL Officer - Hasaka
jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer is responsible for implementing a functional MEAL system at the field level. He/she supports the programmes and operations departments in designing, monitoring and evaluating all projects’ interventions. Moreover, he/she works with the direct supervisor in the coordination and/or the implementation of projects’ baseline and evaluations and the implementation of standardized MEAL processes and tools for all sectors at the field level. The position is based in Hasska and reports to the Senior MEAL Officer.

**Major Responsibilities:**

1\. **Program Design**

- Support MEAL Senior MEAL Officer as requested (One Syria Response, strategy, sectoral frameworks, EBP (based on Regional and Global strategic priorities for Evidence Building), overall MEAL system set-up, ad-hoc requests)
- Support MEAL Senior MEAL Coordinator in leading the proposal development process regarding MEAL input (logframe, budgeting for MEAL activities and staffing, MEAL narrative plan, etc.)
- Develop project-specific MEAL frameworks in coordination with project staff

2\. **Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting**

- Develop methodology, sampling, and tools for the outcome and process monitoring studies, including pre/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, FGDs, KIIs, etc.
- Plan, lead and oversee the implementation of outcome monitoring studies for grants such as PIMs/PDMs, midline and endline studies, pre/post-tests, FGDs, KIIs, etc. (coordinate, follow up, and review the outcome monitoring methodology, tools and reports for grants
- Lead project-specific evaluations and baselines at the field level (development of ToR, select and short-list consultants, coordinate with the consultant, review of design methodology and tools, review final reports, attend interpretation workshops, etc. if externally led; and conduct data analysis and report writing if internally-led)
- Implement field-level tasks for the outcome and process monitoring of grants, including pre/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, midline and end-line studies, FGDs, KIIs, etc. (training of casual workers, planning field data collection, coordination of data collection, supervising, facilitating, coding tools, developing datasets, data cleaning, analysis, reporting)
- Implement field-level tasks for the Syria strategy Impact Assessment (casual training workers, ensuring the quality of data collection through supervision, data cleaning)
- Responsible for the coordination of projects’ baselines and evaluation studies (coordination at field level with consultants, beneficiaries and partners/stakeholders if externally led and methodology, development of tools, data collection, and cleaning if internally led)
- Provide support in training project staff and partners on reporting requirements, core humanitarian standards, output level monitoring and conduct regular training for Operations staff on data collection and data entry for pre-post tests
- Contribute to the MEAL-related component of the Child Well-Being Report (a requirement by GC for Response Offices to also submit a CWBR - as per frequency set by GC)
- Conduct ITT verifications of projects in coordination with project staff every month and ensure project level ITT are updated with accurate data monthly, and key findings are shared with management at the program review meetings
- Conduct project site visits regularly and monitors partner & direct implementation for quality standards through scheduled visits, data quality audits, and spot checks.
- Ensure that critical MEAL findings and recommendations are discussed and addressed by management

**3. Accountability to Children & Communities**

- Assess community preferences and needs to inform the design of contextually-appropriate accountability processes and share outcomes/results with communities, colleagues and partners
- Implement the accountability plan/design developed based on the community preferences on providing information, consulting with communities, promoting participation and collecting & acting on feedback and complaints
- Receive, process and respond to feedback and complaints and communicate progress back to the children, communities and stakeholders
- Implement the plan for sharing information according to the information needs and preferences of community stakeholders and adjust accordingly and collaborate with colleagues to collect relevant and accurate organizational and programme information that will be shared openly with communities, stakeholders and partners
- Ensure that all the feedback & complaints received from communities are recorded/updated timely and accurately in the system and loops closed within the timeline
- Sensitize community members about their right to information, to be consulted, participate and provide feedback and complaints, balanced with a responsibility to support solutions
- Support investigating allegations of irregularities, fraud, corruption or other forms of misconduct by directly liaising with the affected communities, according to guidelines and promptly that promotes trust and safety
- Engage community members in measuring the effectiveness of Accountability practices and, provide recommendations for and address areas that need improvement in coordination with the accountability core team, conduct other consultation activities which can support the design of new programmes
- Conduct exit interviews, observation and reporting

1. **Research and Learning**

- Co-lead lessons learned events for projects with project managers and technical staff (preparation, facilitation and report writing)
- Implement any potential research studies/EBP at the field level (data collection, cleaning) - (based on Regional and Global strategic priorities for Evidence Building)

**5. Miscellaneous**

- Complete Horizon tasks relevant to assigned projects (uploading MEAL plans and monitoring data) - (a requirement by GC to roll out Horizon at the Office level)
- Attend internal and external meetings relevant to assigned projects
- Attend internal and external training, workshops, events, etc.
- Manage and follow up on P&C and financial-related matters for casual workers and conduct performance agreement and review with direct supervisor

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**

- Minimum one to two years of experience in working in a relief or development NGO with a focus on MEAL processes

1. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- BS Degree in international development, international relations, public health, nutrition, statistics, community development, or other relevant discipline is required

1. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Experience in the design and implementation of MEAL systems, including qualitative and quantitative approaches to baselines, monitoring and evaluations, is required
- Good understanding of international standards in humanitarian and accountability (i.e. CHS, SPHERE and Red Cross Code of Conduct)
- Good working knowledge of statistical packages (Excel, etc.) is required
- Excellent knowledge of ODK database/SMAP server
- Expert data handling skills (classification, categorizing, tabulation etc.) and demonstrates diligence in data management
- Good knowledge of information presentation techniques (graphing, charting, tabling etc.) and interpreting them
- Information dissemination skills are required
- Good knowledge of and experience with humanitarian guidelines and principles.
- Ability to work effectively under pressure
- Organization, planning, and time management skills
- Detailed oriented and able to verify data quality
- Stays open to internal and external feedback
- Good contextual knowledge of the local community and social/cultural constraints, realities and organizational relationships
- Ability to understand, explain and contextualize MEAL tools
- High-level communications skills
- Ability to build positive relationships in a cross-cultural environment
- Preferred working knowledge of advanced statistical packages (SPSS etc.)
- The position requires the ability to attend and participate in capacity-building opportunities, training and meetings locally and internationally as required by the organization

1. **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

- The position requires 80% of the time to be field-based and 20% at the office level
- Position requires willingness and ability to continue functioning during a crisis, including during a World Vision response to an artificial or natural disaster.
- The position requires availability and willingness to work outside regular office hours occasionally.

1. **Physical Requirements**

Non

jobs.title: Global Platform Network Coordinator
jobs.description:
ActionAid Denmark is looking for a Global Platform Network Coordinator to strengthen participation, peer learning and collective action across the Global Platforms network, starting on 1 February 2027.

The Global Platforms network connects locally rooted youth spaces and partners, enabling young people and youth-led organisations to learn, organise, lead and act together across countries and regions. As part of ActionAid International, ActionAid Denmark supports strong communities and collective action for sustainable development, democratic participation and a fair distribution of power and resources.

## **About the role**

Join the Global Platforms (GP) Secretariat to help young people and partners connect, learn and act together. You will facilitate inclusive online spaces, coordinate gatherings and exchanges, and keep Global Platforms engaged between activities. Working with Secretariat colleagues, you will connect Global Platforms and young people with expertise, learning resources, capacity support, and exchange and grant opportunities. You will also coordinate shared resources, communication, planning, monitoring and evaluation, helping Global Platforms document change and use feedback to improve their work. The role combines relationship-building, practical coordination, confident use of digital tools and clear follow-up.

**Your main responsibilities will be:**

Participation, peer connections and collective action across Global Platforms

- Facilitate online peer connections, seminars and activities across countries and regions, helping young people and partners share experience, learn from one another and develop solidarity activities and collective action.
- Coordinate shared gatherings, network-wide peer exchanges and annual network festivals, with accessible preparation, meaningful youth and partner participation, effective facilitation and follow-up.
- Connect Global Platforms with methodological expertise, partner capacity support, digital learning, and exchange and grant opportunities across the Secretariat, ensuring clear referrals and follow-up.
- Sustain engagement between activities through online discussion, clear communication and storytelling, working with digital learning and media colleagues.
- Work with Global Platforms and Secretariat units to coordinate contributions to the shared GP resource library, keeping resources organised, accessible and easy to use.
- Use digital tools, including artificial intelligence (AI) where appropriate, to support coordination, resource organisation and communication in line with organisational guidance.

Network planning, monitoring, evaluation and learning

- Work with Global Platforms and the three Secretariat units to coordinate network-wide planning, monitoring, evaluation and learning, including the GP results framework, shared evidence collection and reporting schedules.
- Support Global Platforms to use practical, participatory approaches and storytelling to document young people’s ability to act and influence decisions, sustained organising, collective influence and sustainability. Ensure appropriate consent, privacy and data protection.
- Analyse evidence and feedback from Global Platforms, facilitate learning reviews and help translate findings into agreed improvements in network priorities, participation and support.
- Bring verified evidence and perspectives from Global Platforms into reporting, proposals, communication and agreed advocacy priorities.

## **About you**

We expect that you have:

- Relevant education or equivalent practical experience in youth engagement, community development or a related field.
- Experience engaging young people or civil society partners in networks, facilitating inclusive online sessions and sustaining participation and shared action across countries.
- Experience contributing to shared planning, results frameworks, participatory evidence collection, analysis and reporting.
- Strong coordination skills, including planning gatherings and exchanges, organising shared resources and following up across teams while managing priorities independently.
- Practical understanding of youth-led organising, local ownership, feminist leadership, inclusion, accessibility and safeguarding.
- Basic AI literacy: recognising suitable uses and limitations, checking accuracy and bias, and protecting personal and confidential information. No technical development skills are required.
- Clear written and spoken English, strong listening skills and the ability to build trust across cultures and organisations, adapting communication to local contexts and connecting Global Platforms with relevant support.

**It is an advantage if you also have:**

- Experience with international youth organising, movement building or participatory network governance, including membership and resource decisions.
- Experience coordinating shared resource libraries or contributing evidence to proposals, donor reporting, communication or advocacy.
- Additional languages relevant to the Global Platforms network.

We place particular emphasis on network facilitation, alongside planning, evidence and learning. In your application, interview and any practical exercise, and invite examples of how you enable equal participation and shared action, coordinate work, use digital tools responsibly, assess evidence and learn from feedback. It is also central to the role, that you are capable of practicing cross-cultural communication, show awareness to barriers to participation, power imbalances, safeguarding, consent, confidentiality and appropriate referrals.

## **Practical Information**

The position is placed in the ActionAid Denmark Youth Engagement Team, GP Network Unit, reporting to Camilla Holm-Jensen, with a target **start date of 1 February 2027**.

As a starting point, **applicants should be based in, or willing to relocate at their own expense to, Kenya, Nepal, Uganda, Zimbabwe, Nigeria or South Africa**. If you are based elsewhere, please state clearly in your application where you are based and explain why it would make sense for the position to be based there. In all cases, applicants must already have the right to work in the country where they will be based.

The position is full time, with working hours governed by local legislation and standard NGO-sector practice in the country. Salary will be according to the relevant AADK/AAI salary grade for international staff. The contract will run for the duration of the funding period for the position. International travel should be expected. There is no on-call requirement.

Global Platform Digital Learning Specialist
jobs.description:
ActionAid Denmark is looking for a Global Platform Digital Learning Specialist to develop digital courses, training tools and learning materials that are easy to find and use across the Global Platforms (GP) network and the Danish Training Unit.

The Global Platforms network connects locally rooted youth spaces and partners, enabling young people and youth-led organisations to learn, organise, lead and act together across countries and regions. As part of ActionAid International, ActionAid Denmark supports strong communities and collective action for sustainable development, democratic participation and a fair distribution of power and resources.

## **About the role**

You will join the Youth engagement team and support the DK training unit as well as the Global Platforms Secretariat and MOVE, deliver youth-led methodologies and learning through digital learning journeys. Around 70 percent of your role will focus on digital learning, learning management system (LMS) administration, user interface and user experience, with a central priority of developing online learning courses, training tools and materials. You will develop mobile-first solutions with clear navigation, taking account of the different devices, languages, accessibility needs and low-bandwidth connections of our diverse target groups. You will work closely with subject matter specialists to develop engaging and effective learning formats that support different target audiences and learning needs. The remaining 30 percent will focus coordination and practical user support.

### **Your main responsibilities will be:**

Digital learning system, user experience and mobile-first website integration

- As an instructional designer, collaborate with global subject matter experts to translate storyboards into digital learning and create engaging modules or bite-sized learning.
- Plan and coordinate digital learning systems development and website integration.
- Administer TalentLMS by setting up user groups and branches, managing enrolments, automating notifications, building learning paths and certification systems, and generating completion reports.
- Maintain appropriate user permissions and privacy settings, and improve interfaces and navigation, including integration with the Global Platforms website.
- Manage, organise and maintain courses, training tools and learning materials, and respond to learners’ day-to-day challenges.
- Proactively identify new technical solutions and AI features that enhance the learner experience, accessibility and workflow efficiency.
- Apply basic web and media formatting skills, including HTML/CSS basics for customising TalentLMS portal themes and emails, and optimising video (MP4), audio and PDF files for smooth use on the web.
- Apply considerable API literacy, including an understanding of how REST APIs and webhooks pass data between the website and TalentLMS.
- Adapt learning content to different languages, accessibility needs, internet connections and devices.
- Verify that portal navigation, uploaded media, captions and third-party SCORM packages function properly with keyboard navigation and screen readers, in line with WCAG standards.
- Use usability testing, participation and completion data, learner feedback and learning evidence to continuously improve learning resources, accessibility and LMS performance.
- Translate learner data and evidence into practical recommendations for subject matter specialists on course content, delivery methods and assessment.

Coordination, collaboration og practical user support

- Coordinate digital production with colleagues in the Global Platforms Secretariat, agreeing on digital requirements, content inputs, responsibilities and delivery plans.
- Proactively engage relevant colleagues, thematic specialists and local partners to identify and gather materials, knowledge and input that support the development of learning content and activities.
- Provide practical guidance and support in the use of the learning platform.
- Develop, test and document digital learning tools.

### **About you**

You can demonstrate how you meet the essential requirements through relevant examples from paid work, volunteering, youth organising or community leadership.

Essential requirements

- Expertise in managing and improving learning management systems, including website integration.
- Strong user interface and user experience skills, including organising content, designing clear navigation and testing usability. You can make resources easy to find and use on mobile phones and other devices, taking account of different languages, accessibility needs and low-bandwidth connections.
- Basic understanding of didactics and learning principles, and the ability to apply this understanding to relevant learning formats in collaboration with colleagues, ensuring that learning activities meet the needs of different target audiences.
- Ability to support colleagues, trainers and partners with different levels of digital confidence. You can produce clear user guides, provide practical guidance and help resolve technical problems.
- Practical experience using AI critically and responsibly to support digital learning, content production, accessibility or collaboration. You can assess its usefulness and limitations, check outputs for accuracy and bias, protect sensitive information and provide basic guidance to colleagues and partners.
- Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to explain digital systems clearly and communicate across organisations, cultures and professional backgrounds.
- Ability to work independently, manage subscriptions and payments, balance competing priorities and collaborate in an international network, with a commitment to local ownership, inclusion, feminist leadership and safeguarding.

The desirable qualifications below are an advantage rather than a requirement. They do not replace the essential technical skills.

Desirable qualifications

- A background in training, education or participatory learning, particularly experience with pedagogical design for digital or blended learning.
- Experience applying digital learning in youth engagement, civil society, international development or movement-building contexts.
- Proficiency in additional languages relevant to the Global Platforms network, such as Arabic, French, Spanish or Bangla.

Selection will reflect the balance of the role: around 70 percent will focus on digital learning, LMS administration, user interface and user experience, including mobile-first website integration, and the remaining 30 percent on practical user support. We will look for concrete, user-friendly digital solutions, effective coordination with specialists and partners, and improvements informed by user testing and feedback.

Your examples should also show clear communication and sound judgement on privacy, safeguarding and inclusion.

## **Practical information**

The position is placed in the ActionAid Denmark Youth Engagement Team, GP Network Unit, reporting to Camilla Holm-Jensen, with a target **start date of 1 February 2027**.

As a starting point, **applicants should be based in, or willing to relocate at their own expense to, Kenya, Nepal, Uganda, Zimbabwe, Nigeria or South Africa**. If you are based elsewhere, please state clearly in your application where you are based and explain why it would make sense for the position to be based there. In all cases, applicants must already have the right to work in the country where they will be based.

The position is full time, with working hours governed by local legislation and standard NGO-sector practice in the country. Salary will be according to the relevant AADK/AAI salary grade for international staff. The contract will run for the duration of the funding period for the position. International travel should be expected. There is no on-call requirement.

jobs.title: Digital Platforms and Design Officer
jobs.description:
ActionAid Denmark is looking for a **Digital Platforms and Design Officer** to support the Global Platforms (GP) network of locally rooted youth spaces across the world. These spaces enable young people and youth-led organisations to learn, organise, lead and act together, with support from the GP Secretariat. Headquartered in Denmark, ActionAid Denmark is part of the ActionAid International Federation.

## **About the role**

Based in the GP Network Unit of the Global Platforms Secretariat, you will help network members access information, resources and support, collaborate across countries and communicate their work to wider audiences. Around 70 percent of the role focuses on leading the design, development and day-to-day management of the GP website, maintaining shared digital tools and spaces, and producing publications, donor materials, presentations and digital visuals. Working with Global Platforms, Secretariat colleagues and the ActionAid Denmark communications team, you will make content easy to find and use, maintain accessible and consistent design, and strengthen the network’s visibility, credibility and donor engagement.

The remaining 30 percent focuses on managing social media, newsletters and digital outreach, building relationships that extend the reach of learning opportunities, and providing practical coordination support for network sessions and learning activities. You will also help Global Platforms use artificial intelligence (AI) safely for communication and learning, and use audience feedback and channel data to improve outreach and participation. Across the role, you will support youth-led storytelling that respects young people’s ownership and control over their stories, applying responsible communication practices on accuracy, consent, safeguarding and privacy.

### **Your main responsibilities will be:**

- GP website, shared digital spaces, design and communication production
- Lead the design, development and ongoing updating of the GP website. Use network feedback to make information, opportunities and Secretariat support easy to find, while presenting the network’s work to external audiences to strengthen visibility, credibility and donor engagement.
- Manage the website’s technical setup, publishing arrangements and accessibility.
- Assess unmet communication needs against existing channels, available resources and maintenance requirements. Select, introduce and maintain shared digital tools, including calendars and online spaces for collaboration and peer learning, and help colleagues use them. If a complementary solution is agreed, establish and manage it.
- Design and produce publications, donor materials, PowerPoint presentations and digital visuals using content agreed with relevant colleagues. Adapt materials for different audiences and formats, maintaining agreed visual standards and accessible formats, with clear language, readable layouts, image descriptions and captions.
- Support youth-led storytelling, with young people retaining ownership of their stories and control over how they are represented, adapted and shared. Check accuracy and informed consent before publication, apply safeguarding, privacy and data protection requirements, and refer concerns to responsible colleagues.
- Share responsibility with Global Platforms and Secretariat colleagues for keeping the GP resource library current and well organised, with materials easy to find through the website and appropriate access restrictions where needed.
- Coordinate design briefs, contributions and production schedules with Global Platforms, Secretariat colleagues and the ActionAid Denmark communications team to meet agreed publication dates.
- Digital outreach, network learning and responsible digital practice
- Manage content planning, publishing and audience engagement across the GP network’s social media, newsletters and other public digital channels, connecting audiences with opportunities to learn, participate and act.
- Build relationships with relevant networks, non-governmental and civil society organisations, partners and media to extend the reach of learning materials, webinars and other learning opportunities beyond the GP network. Coordinate this external outreach with communications and advocacy colleagues.
- Provide practical coordination support for network sessions, seminars, camps and learning activities, working with colleagues responsible for GP methods and learning standards.
- Support Global Platforms in safe, practical use of AI for communication and learning through guidance and peer exchange.
- Use channel data and audience feedback to improve content and outreach, considering both reach and participation in learning and action opportunities.

## **About you**

### **We expect that you have:**

- Relevant education or equivalent practical experience in digital communication, graphic design, media or a related field.
- Experience developing and maintaining accessible websites and resource libraries using content management tools, including technical setup and publishing. You can meet network members’ and external audiences’ needs through clear navigation and useful content, coordinating technical support where needed.
- Ability to select, set up and maintain shared calendars and online collaboration and peer-learning spaces, and help colleagues use them, accounting for accessibility, data protection and different connectivity needs.
- Strong writing and editing skills in English, with the ability to turn complex information into clear, accurate and engaging content.
- Strong design and layout skills using relevant tools to produce publications, donor materials, PowerPoint presentations, digital visuals and multimedia content. You can adapt materials across formats while maintaining accessibility and consistent visual standards.
- Experience in collaborative storytelling that respects contributors’ ownership and control over representation and sharing. You understand responsible publication, including accuracy, informed consent, safeguarding, privacy and when to seek specialist advice.
- Practical AI literacy and ability to guide Global Platforms in safe use for communication and learning, applying responsible publication principles and recognising AI limitations, bias and copyright risks.
- Experience managing social media and digital outreach that connects audiences with learning, participation and action.
- Strong coordination and collaboration skills across cultures and organisations. You can work independently, manage competing priorities and publication schedules, and support network learning activities.

### **It is an advantage if you also have:**

- Experience in communication for youth networks, civil society organisations or international cooperation.
- Experience facilitating structured practical sessions or peer learning on accessible content, shared design standards or responsible AI use.
- Knowledge of additional languages relevant to the Global Platforms network.

Selection will prioritise the primary responsibilities in website management, shared digital spaces and design. We will assess applications, interviews, work samples and any practical exercise against the following criteria:

- ·Quality and usability: Ability to build and maintain accessible websites and shared digital spaces, produce effective design, and write and edit clear English content for different audiences.
- ·Responsible communication: Sound judgement on accuracy, story ownership, consent, safeguarding, privacy and AI use.
- ·Delivery and collaboration: Effective prioritisation, planning and project management, cooperation and support for colleagues, using data and feedback to improve outreach and participation.

## **Practical information**

The position is placed in the ActionAid Denmark Youth Engagement Team, GP Network Unit, reporting to Camilla Holm-Jensen, with a target **start date of 1 February 2027.**
