jobs.title: Operations Officer (part time) – National Position
jobs.description:
Malteser International (MI) is the international humanitarian relief agency of the Sovereign Order of Malta. For over 60 years we provide relief and recovery for people during and following conflicts and disasters around the world. Christian values and humanitarian principles form the foundations of our work. In over 30 countries in Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe and the Middle East, we support people in need – regardless of their religion, origin or political convictions.

In the Middle East Region, MI is operating in the context of the humanitarian crisis in Syria since 2012 implementing emergency relief measures in Turkey, Syria, and Lebanon and since 2014 in Iraq. Malteser International’s programs cover needs mainly in the health sector and are mostly partner implemented. In Lebanon, Malteser International works in partnership with the “Order of Malta Lebanon (OML)” to implement a multi-annual program funded by the German Federal Foreign Office to strengthen health, social and agro- humanitarian services provided by OML across Lebanon.

**To support the implementation of its partner programme in Lebanon and to strengthen operational compliance, documentation and procurement processes, Malteser International is looking for an experienced Compliance Officer (part time).**

As Compliance Officer, you will support overall operations with a strong focus on operational compliance and partner coordination with the Order of Malta Lebanon (OML). You will help ensure that finance, procurement, administration, logistics and documentation processes follow MI and donor guidelines, support audits and project closures, and contribute to accurate filing, procurement tracking, asset management and payment processes.

## **Your responsibilities:**

- Ensure that partner expenditure reporting, supporting documents and voucher verification processes comply with MI and donor requirements
- Follow up with OML on compliance recommendations, corrective actions and agreed improvements in operational processes
- Document and maintain compliance-related communication, records and filing systems between MI and the implementing partner
- Conduct field compliance visits and support regular compliance monitoring of partner activities and operations
- Manage MI procurement processes, including purchase requests, purchase orders, procurement tracking and payment requests
- Support contract follow-up, deliverables monitoring, due payments and asset/inventory documentation in line with MI procedures
- Contribute to monthly financial closure, audit preparation and project closure processes by ensuring complete and accurate documentation
- Support administrative and logistics arrangements for the Country Office, including preparation of delegation visits and other operational needs

## **Your profile:**

- University degree or relevant professional qualification in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Procurement, Logistics or a related field
- At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in operations, compliance, finance administration, procurement or partner support, preferably in the humanitarian or development sector
- Good understanding of financial documentation, voucher verification, procurement processes and basic internal control requirements
- Experience in supporting partner coordination, compliance follow-up or documentation processes is an asset
- Familiarity with donor requirements and audit preparation, particularly for institutional donors such as GFFO, BMZ, ECHO, EU or UN agencies, is an advantage
- Strong organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records, trackers and filing systems
- Good communication and coordination skills, with reliability, integrity and a service-oriented working style
- Strong commitment to humanitarian principles, safeguarding and accountability
- Fluent in English, French and Arabic, additional languages (German) are an asset

## **What we offer:**

- Start date: ASAP
- Duty Station: Beirut, Lebanon
- Duration of contract: 1 year, part time (50 %)
- Salary according to qualification and experience, insurance package

## **Working for Malteser International**

Malteser is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all people, regardless of gender, confession or origin.

Malteser International is committed to safeguarding people within our programmes from exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment and has specific policies on this commitment (including a Code of Conduct) which outlines the expected behaviour and the responsibility of all staff, consultants and other organisational representatives. Malteser International conducts reference and background checks for all staff (including criminal records check for specific roles). Any candidate offered a job with Malteser International will be expected to sign MI’s Code of Conduct as an appendix to their contract of employment and agree to conduct themselves in accordance with the provisions of these documents.

Whether you work as a specialist on overseas service or in one of our regional offices - we offer you a challenging working environment in an experienced international team. More than 1,000 national and international staff are currently deployed in various crisis and disaster areas around the world as well as in our regional offices in Cologne and New York City. For more information please click [here](https://www.malteser-international.org/en/jobs.html).

jobs.description:
**Remote · Europe Contract · Full Time**

We have more than 40 projects running at the same time, from ERPs and grants platforms to data tools and information management systems. Our team is remote and works across Europe, Africa and Latin America.

## **About the role**

From the first workshop to handover and support. You will be the client's main contact and keep developers, designers and sector experts working to one plan.

## **Key responsibilities**

### **Delivery**

- Plan each project in phases and sprints, with working versions the client can test

jobs.title: Senior Programme officer - Macroeconomic Policy
jobs.description:
The African Economic Research Consortium (AERC) seeks an experienced and results-oriented macroeconomist to contribute to its macroeconomic policy fellowship and institutional capacity-development portfolio under the Department of Research and Capacity Development. The position combines substantive economic policy expertise with the design and delivery of demand-driven technical assistance and fellowship support to African governments which are beneficiary of the new, flagship and ambitious African Growth Fellowship (AGF) Program implemented in partnership with the African Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF).

The Senior Programme Officer will work with government counterparts, fellows, host institutions, technical experts and development partners to translate priority policy and institutional needs into practical assignments, high-quality analytical products and sustained institutional capability. The postholder will be expected to deliver technically credible advice, manage policy advisory activities effectively, track results of AGF and help ensure that skills, processes and knowledge are embedded within beneficiary institutions in a coordinated manner with regular follow up meetings.

The position does not allow for remote working and will be based in Nairobi, Kenya, on a fixed-term three-year contract, renewable subject to the availability of funds. The Senior Programme Officer will report to the Director of Research and Capacity Building in the AERC and work closely with the programme team within ACBF and AERC and other AERC departments.

## **Duties and responsibilities**

### **Programme Design and country engagement**

- Engage Ministries of Finance, Central Banks, Economic Planning Agencies and other host institutions to identify priority macroeconomic and fiscal policy challenges, assess institutional capacity gaps and define feasible areas for fellowship and technical assistance support.
- Translate country requests and diagnostic findings into clearly scoped programme interventions, including objectives, technical requirements, deliverables, implementation arrangements, budgets, risks and measurable capacity-development outcomes.
- Prepare and quality-assure concept notes, programme documents, annual work plans, results frameworks, budgets and procurement inputs, ensuring alignment with AERC strategies (e.g. the 10-year Strategy 2025-2035), operating procedures and government priorities.
- Contribute technical content and evidence to partnership development, funding proposals and resource mobilization efforts for the macroeconomic policy and fellowship portfolio.

### **Fellowship selection, placement and performance**

- Support transparent, merit-based recruitment and technical assessment of mid-career and senior fellows, closely working with the Programme Coordinator based in ACBF, Advisory Panel and relevant stakeholders. This involves spending 2 days a week in ACBF Nairobi office.
- Match fellows to institution-specific requirements and agree with host institutions on terms of reference, expected policy outputs, supervision, milestones and indicators of institutional benefit before deployment.
- Coordinate the technical aspects of induction, deployment and ongoing placement support; maintain a qualified network of African macroeconomic policy practitioners and potential fellows. Note AGF is implemented by closely working with ACBF. Therefore, there is close coordination with programme staff of both institutions.
- Regularly review fellowship performance with host supervisors and fellows, troubleshoot delivery constraints and document outputs, policy contributions and improvements in institutional practice.
- Ensure each placement includes a practical knowledge-transfer and exit plan, including mentoring of counterparts, documentation, handover of tools and continuity arrangements.

### **Macroeconomic and fiscal policy advisory support**

- Provide rigorous, context-sensitive analysis and practical policy advice on macroeconomic management, fiscal policy, public financial management, economic growth and structural reform priorities.
- Prepare, review and quality-assure macroeconomic projections and frameworks, medium-term fiscal strategies, fiscal risk and debt sustainability assessments, domestic resource mobilisation options and other decision-oriented policy products, as relevant to country demand.
- Support government counterparts, when requested, with analytical briefs, scenarios, policy options, position papers and technical preparations for dialogue with the IMF, World Bank, African Development Bank and other partners.
- Critically assess proposed policy measures, explain trade-offs and implementation implications, and translate complex economic evidence into concise, actionable advice for senior officials.
- Identify emerging countries or regional economic risks and opportunities that merit targeted analysis, expert assistance or new programme interventions.

### **Technical assistance, institutional learning and partnerships**

- Convert requests for technical assistance into precise terms of reference and work plans; identify and coordinate suitably qualified experts and technical partners, as needed.
- Oversee the technical quality, relevance, timeliness and usability of expert and fellowship deliverables through structured review and feedback.
- Design and facilitate applied policy dialogues, mentoring, peer exchanges, workshops and learning activities that directly strengthen the work of participating institutions.
- Promote joint production of research, policy notes, analytical tools and practical guidance with fellows and government counterparts, fostering ownership and use of outputs.
- Capture, synthesize and share lessons, effective practices and reusable knowledge products across participating countries and AERC programmes.

### **Programme delivery, results and accountability**

- Manage assigned activities against approved work plans, budgets, procurement plans, milestones and AERC procedures; proactively identify delays, delivery risks and corrective actions.
- Coordinate with monitoring, evaluation and learning colleagues to establish baselines, track outputs and outcomes, and verify evidence of strengthened institutional capabilities and policy uptake.
- Monitor the quality and utilisation of policy products, fellows’ contributions to reform processes, counterpart mentoring and post-placement sustainability, not only the number of activities completed.
- Prepare accurate, timely technical progress reports, donor inputs, management updates, case studies and evidence of results, supported by reliable programme records.
- Support country supervision, programme reviews, evaluations, financial and procurement documentation, and orderly closure of fellowships and technical assistance assignments.

## **Qualifications and experience**

- A postgraduate degree in Economics, Macroeconomics, Public Finance, Development Economics, Econometrics, Public Policy or a related discipline; a PhD is preferred and is an advantage.
- At least eight years of progressively responsible professional experience in macroeconomic and fiscal policy analysis, economic management, development economics or a closely related field.
- Demonstrated applied experience with macroeconomic frameworks, fiscal policy analysis, economic reform or public financial management in African country contexts; experience working with ministries of finance, central banks or planning institutions is highly desirable.
- Proven ability to produce technically sound, decision-ready policy advice and communicate complex findings to senior government audiences.
- Experience designing and delivering technical assistance, capacity development or multi-stakeholder programmes, including work planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting.
- Knowledge of IMF-supported programmes, debt sustainability analysis or engagement with international financial institutions is an advantage.
- Strong collaboration, stakeholder-management, analytical writing and presentation skills, with the ability to work across countries and disciplinary teams.
- Excellent written and spoken English is essential; working knowledge of French is an advantage, and bilingual proficiency is particularly valued.
- Advanced competence in Excel and standard office applications; familiarity with statistical/econometric tools and programme management systems is an asset.
- Willingness and ability to travel frequently within Africa.

### **Core competencies and personal attributes**

Sound judgement and analytical rigour; results orientation and accountability; diplomacy and ability to engage senior officials; partnership-building and collaborative working; integrity and discretion; adaptability, initiative and commitment to African-led institutional capacity development.

### **Compensation**

The AERC offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience. Under the AGF funding, the Consortium provides a very generous package of benefits.

jobs.title: Independent Evaluation Expert Consultancy Services
jobs.company: Center for Operational Analysis and Research
jobs.description:
**Scope of Services**

**Nature of Services:** Independent Evaluation Expert Consultancy Services

**Type of Contract:** Services will be provided on a day-rate basis against specific project assignments, with the applicable scope, deliverables, estimated level of effort, and fees agreed in writing between COAR and the Consultant.

**Level of Effort:** Assignment-based and strictly as mutually agreed in writing for specific tasks and deliverables. No minimum number of days, fixed working hours, or continuing level of effort is guaranteed or required.

**Place of Performance:** Such location as determined by the Consultant when performing the Services subject to any location-specific requirements expressly agreed in writing for a particular assignment. Any travel, in-person attendance, location-specific requirements and associated expenses shall be agreed in advance.

**Timeframe:** The anticipated term of this consultancy is from 01 January 2027 to 31 March 2027, subject to execution of the applicable agreement. The term establishes the period during which assignments may be agreed. This timeframe does not create any obligation on COAR to provide work or on the Consultant to maintain continuous availability or perform Services other than under an accepted assignment. Any extension shall be subject to mutual written agreement.

**Primary Point of Contact:** COAR's designated \[Syria Country Manager\] acting as the contact for agreeing assignment requirements, coordinating necessary project inputs, clarifying deliverables, addressing technical queries and reviewing completed outputs against the agreed scope.

**Overview:** This Scope of Services (SoS) outlines the services that may be provided by an Independent Evaluation Expert Consultant to the Center for Operational Analysis and Research (COAR). The consultant is expected to lead the design and delivery of an independent final evaluation of a multi-agency, multi-sectoral programme focused on urban and rural resilience and recovery in Syria. The consultancy will cover the evaluation process from inception through data collection, analysis, reporting and dissemination. The Consultant will provide specialist evaluation expertise and assume responsibility for the technical quality, methodological rigour and timely delivery of the agreed evaluation outputs.

**Nature of the consultancy:** This is an independent, non-exclusive, project-based consultancy engagement and not a position of employment with COAR. Services will be commissioned through specific assignments agreed between COAR and the Consultant, setting out the relevant scope, deliverables, estimated level of effort, timeframe and applicable day rate.

COAR does not guarantee any minimum number of assignments or consultancy days, and the Consultant will remain free to accept or decline proposed assignments and to provide services to other clients, subject to confidentiality, conflicts of interest and the timely delivery of any assignment accepted.

The Consultant will determine independently the professional approach, methods, sequencing, working time and place of performance of the Services, subject to agreed deliverables, deadlines, applicable legal, contractual, client, security, safeguarding, confidentiality, data-protection, and other project-specific requirements, and reasonable project coordination. The Consultant will ordinarily use their own equipment and working facilities and will be responsible for their own tax, social insurance and other statutory obligations arising from the consultancy. The consultancy does not carry employee benefits.

The Consultant will coordinate their own activities and agreed project inputs but will not occupy a position within COAR’s organisational structure, exercise employment or line-management authority over COAR personnel, or have authority to bind COAR, except where expressly authorised in writing for a defined project purpose.

COAR may specify the scope, required outputs, deadlines, quality standards, project requirements, and information required for an agreed assignment, but will not direct the Consultant as to the manner or means of performing the Services.

The Consultant will not be required to work fixed hours, maintain continuous availability, attend COAR premises on a regular basis, or participate in COAR’s internal management or personnel processes, except where specific attendance or participation is reasonably necessary for an agreed assignment.

Fees will be payable only for Services performed under an agreed assignment and against submission of appropriate invoices. No minimum volume of work or continuing retainer is guaranteed.

**Activities**

Activities may include, as agreed between the parties:

**Evaluation Design and Inception**

- Review relevant programme documents, including the Theory of Change, results framework and progress reports.
- Develop the evaluation methodology, evaluation matrix, sampling approach and data collection tools, in line with OECD-DAC criteria.
- Ensure appropriate consideration of gender equality, disability inclusion and conflict sensitivity.

**Evaluation Coordination and Data Collection**

- Provide technical coordination for the evaluation process, including coordination with the multidisciplinary evaluation team.
- Coordinate data collection with participating organisations, government counterparts, local authorities, partners and affected communities.
- Conduct or coordinate interviews, consultations and site visits, as agreed, to assess programme activities and verify relevant results.
- Ensure data collection is conducted ethically and in a conflict-sensitive manner.

**Analysis and Reporting**

- Assess programme achievements, outcomes and contribution to resilience and recovery, including in basic services, livelihoods and social cohesion.
- Identify key findings, lessons learned and practical recommendations.
- Prepare and present evaluation findings, including recommendations with proposed responsibilities and timelines.

**Deliverables**

The Consultant will be responsible for producing the following deliverables:

- Inception report, including the methodology, evaluation matrix and data collection approach.
- Preliminary findings and debriefing presentation.
- Draft evaluation report in English.
- Final evaluation report incorporating agreed feedback.
- Final presentation of evaluation findings to relevant stakeholders.
- The format, length and submission dates of each deliverable will be agreed at the start of the assignment.

**Required Professional Experience and Expertise**

- Demonstrable experience leading or conducting complex programme evaluations.
- Experience with OECD-DAC evaluation criteria and mixed-methods research.
- Strong analytical, report-writing and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Fluency in English. Arabic language skills and substantial knowledge of the Syrian context are desirable.

**Assignment Management**

The Consultant will coordinate with the designated COAR focal point on deliverables, access to information and technical feedback. COAR may provide comments on draft deliverables and assess their compliance with the agreed requirements. The Consultant will remain responsible for the independent analysis, findings and professional conclusions.

Any material changes to the scope, deliverables, timeline or level of effort will be agreed in writing, including any related fee adjustments.

jobs.title: Project Manager and Technical Advisor for Protection
jobs.description:
**Duty station:** Caracas or La Guaira, with regular travel to project locations
**Contract type:** Consultancy contract (100%)

**Contract duration:** 1.1.2027 – 31.12.2027
**Reporting to:** Humanitarian Desk, Solidar Suisse Headquarters, Switzerland
**Eligibility:** Open to Venezuelan nationals and other applicants who are legally authorised to work in Venezuela and are currently residing in the country (no relocation support)

**Background**

Solidar Suisse is a Swiss non-governmental organisation founded in 1936, formerly known as Swiss Labour Assistance. The organisation is committed to promoting social justice, decent work and equal opportunities and implements humanitarian and development programmes across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Europe.

Following the earthquake that struck Venezuela in June 2026, Solidar Suisse launched an initial humanitarian response to support affected communities. Building on this first intervention, Solidar Suisse is now preparing a new humanitarian project focusing on WASH and Protection in Caracas and La Guaira.

In line with Solidar Suisse’s commitment to locally led humanitarian action, the project will be implemented in close partnership with two Venezuelan organisations with strong expertise in WASH and Protection respectively. Each partner will lead implementation in its core sector, while contributing complementary expertise to the overall response. Solidar Suisse will retain overall responsibility for the project and provide oversight, coordination and quality assurance through a lean in-country structure.

**Position Purpose**

Solidar Suisse is seeking a qualified and adaptable Project Manager and Technical Advisor for Protection to oversee the effective implementation of its humanitarian project in Venezuela.

The position is responsible for the overall management, coordination, monitoring and quality assurance of the project, as well as for providing technical guidance on Protection. The position holder will supervise two Solidar Suisse project staff and will work closely with both local partner organisations, supporting them in planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, compliance and organisational coordination.

The successful applicant must be comfortable working across different areas of responsibility and responding flexibly to changing project needs. The position requires a hands-on professional who can combine project management, partner accompaniment, technical guidance, team supervision, external coordination and field-level problem-solving.

**Main Responsibilities**

**Project Management and Implementation**

- Lead and oversee the overall implementation of the humanitarian project in accordance with the approved proposal, budget, workplan and partnership agreements.
- Ensure that project activities are implemented on time, within budget and in accordance with agreed objectives, indicators and quality standards.
- Coordinate implementation across the Protection and WASH components of the project.
- Maintain a comprehensive overview of project progress, challenges, risks, expenditure and required follow-up.
- Identify implementation gaps or delays and work with the partner organisations and Solidar Suisse Headquarters to develop practical solutions.
- Ensure that project implementation complies with donor requirements, Solidar Suisse policies, humanitarian principles and applicable standards.
- Coordinate project revisions and adjustments when required.
- Ensure that appropriate project documentation and records are maintained.

**Partner Coordination and Support**

- Serve as the principal operational focal point for the two local implementing partners.
- Maintain regular communication and coordination with partner management and project teams.
- Guide and support the partners throughout project planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting.
- Review partner workplans, activity plans, reports and other project documentation.
- Support partners in meeting agreed programme, financial, safeguarding, accountability and compliance requirements.
- Facilitate joint planning, reflection and problem-solving processes.
- Identify partner support and capacity-strengthening needs and coordinate appropriate follow-up.
- Promote a respectful, transparent and collaborative partnership approach.
- Ensure that roles, responsibilities, expectations and communication channels between Solidar Suisse and the partners remain clear throughout implementation.

**Technical Guidance on Protection**

- Provide technical guidance and oversight for the project’s Protection component.
- Support the Protection partner in developing and adapting technically sound implementation approaches.
- Review Protection activities, tools and project documentation and provide practical recommendations for improvement.
- Ensure that Protection activities are implemented in line with humanitarian principles, relevant Protection standards, safeguarding requirements and the do-no-harm approach.
- Support the integration of protection principles across the wider project, including the WASH component.
- Promote safe, inclusive and accessible programming for different population groups.
- Support appropriate accountability, participation, confidentiality and referral practices.
- Identify technical quality concerns and work with the partner to establish and monitor corrective actions.

**Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Reporting**

- Monitor project performance against the approved results framework, indicators, targets, workplan and budget.
- Conduct regular monitoring visits to project locations and partner activities.
- Assess the quality and relevance of implementation and agree on follow-up actions with the respective partner.
- Support the collection, verification and analysis of project monitoring information.
- Ensure that monitoring processes consider programme quality, accountability, safeguarding and protection-related risks.
- Review narrative reports and supporting documentation submitted by the partners.
- Prepare accurate and timely internal updates and contribute to donor reporting.
- Document implementation challenges, lessons learned, good practices and recommendations.
- Promptly report significant programme, financial, operational, compliance, safeguarding or security concerns to Solidar Suisse Headquarters.

**Financial and Compliance Oversight**

- Monitor project expenditure in cooperation with the relevant partner and Solidar Suisse finance colleagues.
- Follow up on expenditure against the approved budget and flag potential over- or underspending.
- Support partners in understanding and meeting financial, procurement and documentation requirements.
- Review the consistency between implemented activities, reported results and related expenditure.
- Contribute to budget forecasting, financial planning and project revisions.
- Support compliance with contractual obligations, donor conditions, partnership agreements and internal control requirements.

**Team Management**

- Directly supervise two Solidar Suisse staff members.
- Establish clear roles, priorities and performance expectations.
- Provide regular guidance, feedback, coaching and practical support.
- Ensure effective coordination and information-sharing within the project team.
- Promote a professional, respectful, accountable and collaborative working environment.
- Support staff development and address performance or operational challenges in a timely manner.

**Coordination and Representation**

- Represent Solidar Suisse in relevant coordination meetings, technical working groups and consultations.
- Maintain professional relationships with local authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, civil society organisations and other relevant stakeholders.
- Participate in relevant Protection and humanitarian coordination mechanisms.
- Coordinate with relevant WASH actors when required to support coherent implementation across both project components.
- Monitor contextual and humanitarian developments that may affect the project.
- Provide Solidar Suisse Headquarters with regular updates on the operating context, implementation environment, risks and emerging needs.
- Contribute to strengthening Solidar Suisse’s presence, relationships and understanding of the humanitarian context in Venezuela.

**Risk Management, Safeguarding and Accountability**

- Monitor contextual, operational, programme, safeguarding and security risks affecting project implementation.
- Support the development and application of practical risk mitigation measures.
- Ensure that partners understand and apply relevant safeguarding and accountability requirements.
- Promote accessible and confidential feedback and complaints mechanisms.
- Escalate serious concerns or incidents through the appropriate reporting channels.
- Support safe and conflict-sensitive implementation across all project activities.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Contribute to organisational learning and the further development of Solidar Suisse’s humanitarian engagement in Venezuela.
- Undertake other reasonable duties necessary for the effective implementation of the project and humanitarian response.
- Respond flexibly to changing project priorities and operational needs.

**Candidate Profile**

- Full professional proficiency in Spanish and English, both written and spoken.
- University degree in humanitarian action, international development, social sciences, human rights, law, social work or another relevant field.
- At least five years of progressively responsible professional experience in humanitarian or development programming.
- Demonstrated experience managing humanitarian or development projects, including workplanning, monitoring, budget follow-up and reporting.
- Relevant experience in Protection programming and a sound understanding of protection principles, safeguarding, accountability and the do-no-harm approach.
- Experience working with and supporting national or local civil society organisations.
- Experience guiding partners and strengthening programme implementation through practical accompaniment, mentoring and constructive follow-up.
- Previous staff supervision or team management experience.
- Experience with donor-funded projects and related quality, reporting and compliance requirements.
- Ability to coordinate different technical and operational components within one project.
- Strong analytical, organisational and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities and respond constructively to changing circumstances.
- Willingness and ability to undertake regular field travel.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to work respectfully with diverse partners and stakeholders.
- Good command of Microsoft Office applications.
- Good knowledge of the Venezuelan humanitarian and institutional context.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.description:
**Role:** Full Time

**Number of positions**: 2

**Contract Duration:** 2 Years, Fixed Term and Contract Renewable

**Reports to:** Consortium Director

**Salary:** Annual Gross KES 6,749,952 -KES 8,200,000

**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya

**Deadline for submission:** 3 December, 2026

**This position is open to Kenyan nationals only**

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

**About Us**

Founded in 1992, Nutrition International is a global organization dedicated to delivering proven nutrition interventions to those who need them most. Working in partnership with countries, donors and implementers, our experts conduct cutting-edge nutrition research, support critical policy formulation, and integrate nutrition into broader development programs. In more than 60 countries, primarily in Asia and Africa, Nutrition International nourishes people to nourish life.

For more than 30 years now, Nutrition International has focused on delivering low-cost, high-impact, nutrition interventions to people in need, driven by our mission to achieve a world where everyone, everywhere, is free from malnutrition and able to reach their full potential. Nutrition International’s work is guided by a dedicated and talented team of experts working globally, regionally and within countries to end malnutrition worldwide.

**About the NOURISH Investment**

The NOURISH investment (Nurture the ecosystem, Optimize the market, Unlock financing, Reinforce ANC platforms, Integrate and Scale MMS and Calcium for Healthy Futures) is an exciting new multi-country investment designed to accelerate the sustainable scale-up of MMS and strengthen systems for the integration of calcium supplementation across Africa. NOURISH takes a comprehensive, systems-based approach that brings together expertise across the critical areas required for successful scale-up: strengthening health systems, improving local product quality, affordability and availability, advancing sustainable health financing, and fostering the enabling policy and implementation environment needed for long-term success.

Funded by Children’s Investment Fund Foundation (CIFF) and led by Nutrition International, the NOURISH consortium brings together a unique combination of global and country-level expertise. Consortium partners currently include UNICEF Ethiopia, Sight and Life Rwanda, and CHAI Ghana, each contributing specialized technical and operational capabilities to support either country-led scale-up or regional efforts. NOURISH is supporting Ethiopia and Rwanda as the first countries to receive support through the initiative. Over the coming years, up to six additional African countries are expected to benefit from NOURISH support, working alongside governments navigate the pathway from MMS introduction to sustainable national scale-up.

Employing a unique partnership approach with a consortium of partners, Nutrition International, together with the donor, is delivering a five-year pan-African initiative – NOURISH – focused on Strengthening Maternal Nutrition Platforms for MMS & Calcium across 8 countries. As the project scales, the volume and complexity of partner-facing delivery, sub-grant management and country-level coordination necessitates project management oversight.

**About the Role**

The **Senior Program Manager** is accountable for the delivery of an assigned portfolio within the NOURISH initiative. This portfolio will be made up of a defined group of countries, technical assistance partners and regional technical assistance partners who each own a scope of work, workplan and budget. The role translates the approved consortium strategy, workplan and budget into executed country and regional workplans, and holds assigned implementing partners to account for scope, timeline, budget, quality and compliance.

The role carries delegated authority for decisions within the approved workplan and budget, and escalates matters of consortium strategy, donor relations, partner agreements and material budget or scope change to the Consortium Director. The job holder works closely with the Consortium Director, the adjacent Senior Program Manager, a Senior Technical Advisor, a Senior MEAL Advisor and the Finance Manager, who provide technical, monitoring and financial management support across NOURISH.

The Senior Program Manager will be a delivery-focused Manager with a proven ability to run complex, multi-country, multi-partner programs, to hold partners to account constructively in a respectful and inclusive environment.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- **Program Delivery and Project Management:** Translate the approved NOURISH consortium strategy, annual workplan and budget into coordinated country and regional workplans, collaborating with partners, government stakeholders and Nutrition International country offices. Oversee day-to-day portfolio implementation, monitor activities, milestones and deliverables, lead annual planning and consolidate partner inputs into the consortium-wide plan. Maintain delivery trackers and risk logs, provide regular progress reports to the Consortium Director, resolve operational bottlenecks and escalate issues affecting scope, timelines, budgets or donor commitments.
- **Partner Management and Performance:** Serve as the primary management liaison for regional and country implementing partners, leading stakeholder engagement and co-creation workshops. Coordinate the onboarding and orientation of Technical Assistance Partners, ensuring clear scopes of work, budgets, annual workplans, milestone tracking and alignment with NOURISH’s technical, programmatic, MEAL, data systems and governance requirements.
- **Monitoring, Reporting and Learning:** Collaborate with the Senior MEAL Advisor to strengthen monitoring, evaluation and data quality across the portfolio, ensuring consistent application of tools and indicators, timely and accurate partner reporting, and data-driven performance reviews to identify gaps and drive continuous improvement.
- **Budget and Sub-Grant Management:** Manage the approved portfolio budget, including partner sub-grants; review financial reports and expenditure, investigate variances, prepare cash flow forecasts and budget realignment proposals, and ensure partner compliance with Nutrition International and donor financial procedures and requirements.
- **Technical Coordination and External Engagement:** Ensure alignment of portfolio workplans and partner delivery with consortium technical guidance, strengthen engagement with government stakeholders and national coordination platforms, and represent the project at relevant country and regional technical, coordination and partner forums as delegated by the Consortium Director.
- **Consortium Collaboration and Upward Reporting:** Provide the Consortium Director with timely, accurate and comprehensive updates on portfolio delivery, risks and expenditure to support evidence-based decision-making and fulfilment of donor commitments. Participate in consortium leadership and management meetings, contributing to strategic discussions and decision-making, while collaborating with Nutrition International teams, including Monitoring, Data and Learning, People and Culture, Corporate Services, Partnerships and Growth, and Communications, to support effective programme delivery.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

- The position holds delivery oversight – not line management – of the teams of assigned regional and country-level implementing partners.
- The position also coordinates the contribution of shared project functions (technical, financing, monitoring and finance) to the assigned portfolio on a matrix basis.

## **Requirements**

**Education/Professional Designations/Experience:**

- A Master’s degree or equivalent experience in public health, nutrition, international development, project management and/or a related field.
- At least 10 years of experience in health, nutrition or development programming, including at least 5 years managing multi-country or multi-partner programs, with a significant portion of this experience in Africa.
- Demonstrated track record of managing sub-grants or sub-awards and holding implementing partners to account for delivery, compliance and reporting.
- Proven experience managing project budgets, including expenditure tracking, forecasting, variance analysis and donor compliance requirements.
- Experience managing the full project cycle – work planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting and close-out – in complex, multi-stakeholder settings.
- Demonstrated track record of working directly with government leadership and national coordination structures in the health or nutrition sector.
- Demonstrated experience line managing and developing staff, including remote and multi-country teams.

**Other Specific Skill Requirements:**

**Skills**

- Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and competence with project management and workplan tracking tools.
- Strong communication skills (oral and written), including report writing for donor audiences.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent country workstreams and competing deadlines.
- Fluency in English - both reading and writing – is essential.
- A working knowledge of French is an asset.

**Competencies**

- **Delivery Focus**: Drives work to completion, anticipates obstacles, and holds self, team and partners to agreed commitments and timelines.
- **Partner Management**: Builds productive working relationships with partners while maintaining clear performance standards and accountability.
- **Project Management**: Strong planning, coordination and organisational skills across multiple concurrent country and regional workstreams.

**Personal Attributes**

- **Results-Oriented:** Focused on achieving measurable outcomes and maximising impact through efficient program delivery.
- **Collaborative**: Works constructively across teams, partners, units and offices to achieve shared objectives.
- **Integrity**: High ethical standards with a commitment to transparency, accountability and social impact.

jobs.title: Technical Manager - PPRD-Med II
Communications Officer
jobs.description:
## OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

WHO’s work in countries operationalizes the General Programme of Work (GPW14) and the European Programme of Work 2025-2029 (EPW2). GPW14 focuses on accelerating progress toward Health for All by strengthening systems for health, improving access to essential services, advancing preparedness and resilience, and reducing health inequalities. EPW2, endorsed at RC75 following extensive consultation with Member States, reaffirms WHO/Europe’s role in bringing unique value to countries through five core functions:
1\. International knowledge hub for health – providing authoritative evidence, norms, policies and best practices from across the Region and globally to inform national public health decision-making.
2\. Impartial coordinator for everyone’s health – convening national stakeholders and partners to align strategies and support coherent, multisectoral responses to shared health challenges.
3\. Leader in tracking and managing cross-border health threats – supporting surveillance, preparedness, and coordinated action on public health emergencies in line with the Preparedness 2.0 agenda.
4\. Driver of health system transformation – advising national authorities on evidence-informed reforms and policies that strengthen health systems and improve performance.
5\. Voice for health equity – helping countries identify who is being left behind and integrating equity considerations into health policies and strategies.

In this context, WHO Country Offices enable the translation of global and regional commitments into national action. They support Member States by providing strategic advice, convening dialogue across sectors and partners, connecting national authorities with WHO’s technical expertise, and facilitating the use of evidence and best practices to inform policy.

## DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

The incumbent will perform all or part of the following, and other related responsibilities as required by the needs of the office.

• In coordination with the regional and/or headquarters communication focal points, develop and guide the implementation of communication strategies and plans to support awareness of the programmes and achievements of WHO at country level. Ensure the implementation of the WHO corporate (global and regional) communication strategy.
• Identify marketable subjects/success stories and develop communications and advocacy products including for partnerships’ initiatives.
• Establish office processes for content identification.
• Ensure optimal and timely outreach and dissemination to target audiences in suitable media channels and platforms, including social media.
• Organize media events, campaigns and media technical briefings, coordinating between media and WHO experts, as required.
• Build and maintain productive networks and contacts with the press/media and key, national
communication counterparts to ensure positive and optimal coverage of WHO’s work.
• As a national of the country or territory, apply knowledge of the cultural norms of diverse, national stakeholders and audiences to (i) manage the development/updating of content and stakeholder linkages for the WHO country office website and (ii) the sensitive design and delivery of effective social-media engagements.
• Ensure regular media monitoring, tracking audience/target group perceptions of the organization. Identify information deficits and develop strategies to address these deficiencies; manage risk-mitigation communications.
• Collaborate with national stakeholders, development and other strategic partners and United Nations Information Officers, to encourage the production and dissemination of information on national health strategies. Advocate for organizational priorities, foster related initiatives, and represent WHO in the United Nations Communication Group.
• Deliver and/or support specialized emergency or multi hazard risk communications, social mobilization and advocacy plans, during public health crises, emergencies, and outbreaks.
• Advise country office leadership on strategic, external and internal communications and support country office staff on communications with sensitivity to national cultural norms, where required.
• Coordinate and deliver communication and media-sensitization-related training for WHO country office staff.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

### Education

**Essential:** First university degree (Bachelor's level) in communications, journalism, marketing, political or international relations, health communications or related fields.
**Desirable:** A Master’s degree in one of the above areas. Formal qualification in public health; courses in communication techniques and/or graphic design, visual language in the use of social media. Training in risk communication.

### Experience

**Essential:** A minimum of five years' experience overseeing and delivering communications services and products at the national level. A minimum of 2 years in communications strategy development at the international level.
**Desirable:** Demonstrated experience in the management communication/PR projects. Experience in team supervision. Relevant work experience with(in) UN, NGOs or similar international organizations/institutions.

### Functional Skills

**Essential:**
• Thorough understanding of public health and international development issues
• Proven skills in the development and implementation of communication/media products and approaches including solid writing skills
• Excellent interpersonal and networking skills
• Ability to represent and promote the WHO brand in virtual communities and networks
• Ability to develop messaging and positioning for an international organization
• Ability to elicit and communicate success stories
• Ability to transform technical information for different target audiences.

**Desirable:**
• Knowledge of WHO /United Nations agencies programmes and practices
• Knowledge and understanding of WHO mandate and goals in the emergency incident management context.

**Other Skills (e.g. IT)**

• Computer literacy and knowledge of office software packages, handling of web-based management systems, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems and Cloud Management Enterprise System such as Workday.

### WHO Competencies

1\. Teamwork
2\. Respecting & promoting individual and cultural differences
3\. Communication
4\. Creating an empowering and motivating environment
5\. Building and promoting partnerships across the organization and beyond

### Use of Language Skills

**Essential:** Expert level of English and Ukrainian**.**
**Desirable:** Intermediate knowledge of another United Nations language.

## REMUNERATION

Remuneration comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 64,825 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable) and 30 days of annual leave.

**Link to apply:** [**Job Description - Communications Officer (2605086)**](https://careers.who.int/careersection/ex/jobdetail.ftl?job=2605086&tz=GMT%2B02%3A00&tzname=Europe%2FKiev)

jobs.title: Branding & Communications Manager
jobs.description:
Job Title: Branding and Communications Manager

Organization: Greenpeace MENA

Department: GP MENA Engagement Department

Reports to: Engagement Director

Grade: F

Location: The job is based in the MENA region.

**OVERALL PURPOSE**
The Branding and Communications Manager is responsible for enhancing Greenpeace MENA's public image, reputation, and brand presence in the region. The role involves developing and implementing comprehensive branding and communications strategies, managing key influencer relationships, and ensuring cohesive organizational branding to expand awareness, engage new audiences, increase engagement, and maximize the impact of campaigns and projects.

**SCOPE**
Reporting to the Engagement Director, the postholder will contribute to the development and implementation of Greenpeace MENA’s Engagement Strategy, leading the branding, communications, media relations, and creative functions in support of its objectives.

The role oversees a multidisciplinary team, providing strategic direction, people management, and oversight of priorities and delivery. It requires independence, initiative, and strategic vision, with responsibilities extending to global projects and collaborations across multiple Greenpeace offices. The post holder will also oversee budgets, ensuring alignment with the organization’s objectives and priorities.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**BRANDING, COMMUNICATIONS & MARKETING STRATEGY**

- **Lead** the formulation and implementation of GP MENA’s branding and communications strategies as an integral part of the wider engagement strategy, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and contributing to audience growth, supporter engagement, and campaign impact.
- **Develop** campaigns that strengthen Greenpeace’s brand identity and visibility across the MENA region, focusing on positioning GP MENA as a leading environmental organization by integrating innovative storytelling techniques to effectively communicate its impact and initiatives.
- **Ensure** consistent and effective messaging across all internal and external communications channels, in alignment with the branding and communications strategy and guidelines.
- **Develop** and implement a strategy to enhance the public profile of the Executive Director (ED) as a leading voice in environmental advocacy.
- **Provide** strategic oversight of media relations and external communications, strengthening Greenpeace MENA's visibility, credibility, and positioning across regional and international media.
- **Guide** proactive media engagement, thought leadership, and strategic communications opportunities to amplify Greenpeace MENA's perspectives and campaign priorities.
- **Work** closely with the Engagement Director to ensure integrated planning, consistent audience experiences, and coordinated communications that support supporter acquisition, engagement, and long-term relationship building.

**INFLUENCER MARKETING & BRAND AMBASSADORSHIP**

- **Design** and execute strategies for engaging key influencers to amplify GP MENA’s messaging and campaigns.
- **Oversee** outreach and partnerships with influencers, ensuring alignment with branding objectives and organizational values.
- **Track** and analyze influencers' performance to refine engagement strategies.
- **Lead** on managing GP MENA branding events, in collaboration with partners and suppliers, and support in managing other departments' events to ensure proper branding of the organization.

**MESSAGE DEVELOPMENT & NARRATIVE BUILDING**

- **Create** and refine key messages for the organization, campaigns, public speaking engagements, and organizational updates.
- **Ensure** messaging is tailored to diverse audiences within the MENA region and fits different personas while considering local context and cultural sensitivity, taking into account political, social, and cultural contexts, audience perceptions, and potential sensitivities.
- **Exercise** sound editorial and strategic judgment to proactively identify and assess potential sensitivities and reputational risks in communications, campaigns, partnerships, and public positioning, advising teams on appropriate approaches.
- **Oversee** the creation of high-quality, brand-aligned content, including annual reports, newsletters, campaigns, and strategic messaging for stakeholders.
- **Work** with campaign teams to ensure messages are compelling, impactful, resonate with target audiences, and align with the branding messages and guidelines.

**MARKET & AUDIENCE RESEARCH**

- **Lead** audience and market research projects to identify trends, measure brand perception, and guide strategy development.
- **Utilize** data analysis to provide actionable recommendations for enhancing branding, communications, and marketing outcomes.

**PROJECT MANAGEMENT**

- **Lead** branding and communications components of cross-departmental projects, ensuring seamless integration of communications and engagement strategies.
- **Support** campaign teams by providing branding insights and communication expertise to maximize campaign reach and effectiveness.

**CRISIS COMMUNICATIONS**

- **Support** the Engagement Director in crisis communication planning and execution, as needed, ensuring clear, timely, and effective responses to reputational risks.

**INTERNAL COMMUNICATIONS**

- **Develop** internal communication plans in collaboration with the People & Culture team to safeguard the brand and to keep staff informed and engaged with organizational updates, campaigns, and milestones.

**MONITORING, EVALUATION & REPORTING**

- **Establish** key performance indicators (KPIs) for branding, communications, and marketing initiatives.
- **Monitor** and evaluate campaigns' success, reporting progress and incorporating lessons learned into future strategies.

**BUDGET MANAGEMENT**

- **Develop** and manage the budget for branding, ensuring cost-effectiveness and alignment with organizational priorities.

**TEAM LEADERSHIP & MANAGEMENT**

- **Manag**e the Branding and Communications team, including media relations, communications, creative, and editorial functions, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities.
- Establish clear team objectives and performance expectations, monitor progress, and ensure accountability for agreed deliverables.

**OTHER DUTIES**

- **Perform** additional tasks delegated by the Engagement Director to support GP MENA’s branding and communications goals.

**QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND EXPERIENCE**

**Educational Qualifications**

- Graduate or postgraduate degree (master's preferred) in communications, marketing, or a related field.

**Experience & Skills**

- At least 7-10 years of professional experience in marketing, branding, or communications, preferably in a non-profit organization.
- Proven success in designing and implementing branding, communications, and marketing strategies.
- Expertise in influencer marketing
- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English and Arabic, with experience in creating diverse content formats.
- Knowledge of market research methods and public relations strategies, with established connections in the MENA region.
- Demonstrated experience in project management and cross-cultural collaboration.

**Organizational Competencies**

- Exceptional relationship-building and interpersonal skills, particularly in multicultural and global settings.
- Strong planning, organizing, and time management abilities.
- Ability to lead and inspire teams, fostering collaboration and creativity.
- Self-driven, flexible, and capable of adapting to dynamic environments.
- Strong understanding of the political, social, and cultural landscape across the MENA region, with demonstrated ability to anticipate sensitivities, assess reputational risks, and exercise sound judgment in complex environments.

**Behavioral Competencies**

- Persistent, assertive, and capable of driving initiatives from concept to completion.
- Integrity and accountability in all professional interactions.

jobs.title: Program Manager CRCSU
jobs.description:
Canberra based (embedded within DFAT), with some possible travel required.

**Eligibility:**

Candidates must hold Australian citizenship and have or be willing to obtain a baseline or higher security clearance.

**Program Background**

Climate Resilient Communities (CRC) supports implementation of the Australian Government's climate change commitments under *Australia's International Development Policy*, in line with partner government priorities.

CRC supports the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to increase climate investments, drive climate integration, and better address climate change and disaster risk across Australia’s development portfolio.

CRC incentivises funding towards gender-responsive, inclusive climate and disaster resilience programming, particularly in the water, food, nature-based solutions, and energy sectors.

DFAT has engaged DT Global to support the implementation of CRC through a Support Unit.

For further information about CRC, visit the [**DFAT website**](https://www.dfat.gov.au/international-relations/themes/climate-change/supporting-indo-pacific-tackle-climate-change/climate-resilient-communities).

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [**www.dt-global.com**](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**The Role**

The Program Manager will support the Climate Change Division within DFAT to deliver Australia’s flagship climate program, the Climate Resilient Communities program (CRC), and its associated co-funded investments across the Pacific. Embedded within DFAT, the role will primarily support the effective management and delivery of DFAT’s climate investments, including liaising with investment managers at DFAT posts, providing program performance inputs to briefing products, and responding to program enquiries. The Program Manager will assist DFAT staff to use departmental development management systems effectively, support the collection, analysis and consolidation of program performance reporting, including Tier 2 and Tier 3 reporting and annual Investment Monitoring Reports, and provide back-up support to the Climate Adviser responsible for climate integration in the Pacific. The role will also coordinate and facilitate technical advice and capability-building on climate change integration across DFAT programs and implementing partners.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position:

[**https://tinyurl.com/mtd89cdf**](https://tinyurl.com/mtd89cdf)

**About You**

You are a proactive and well-organised program management professional with at least three years of experience managing or supporting development programs, preferably in the Indo-Pacific. You bring sound judgement, strong attention to detail and a systematic approach to managing competing priorities, deadlines and emerging issues, and you prepare clear and concise advice, briefs and reports. You are a collaborative relationship builder who is confident working across government and with implementing partners, technical advisers and partner governments. Experience within DFAT, the Australian Public Service or a comparable government environment, or supporting climate or development programs in the Pacific, will be highly regarded. You are committed to gender equality, disability and social inclusion, child protection, PSEAH and other DFAT safeguarding priorities in your day-to-day work.

**Why join CRC?**

This is an opportunity to work from within DFAT’s Climate Change Division and contribute directly to Australia’s flagship climate program, supporting increased climate investment and stronger climate integration across the Pacific. You will gain first-hand experience of how government development investments are managed, while helping DFAT staff and implementing partners strengthen how climate change and disaster risk are addressed across Australia’s development portfolio. You will join a collaborative team advancing gender-responsive and inclusive climate and disaster resilience programming, and play a central role in turning strategic priorities into well-coordinated, high-quality results.

jobs.title: Gerente de Proyecto
jobs.description:
**DATOS GENERALES**

- *Sede de Trabajo: San Lorenzo, Valle*
- *Mes de inicio: Diciembre 2026*
- *Plazas Disponibles: 1*
- *Reportará a: Directora de Programas*
- *Unidad a la que pertenecerá: Programas*

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL PROGRAMA:**

Con financiamiento de Blue Action Fund, GOAL implementará el proyecto “Aumentar la resiliencia de comunidades y ecosistemas mediante una mejor gestión de las AMP y los medios de vida en el Golfo de Fonseca, Honduras” en consorcio con COODDEFFAGOL, Ilili y la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de Honduras (UNAH). Y tiene como objetivo fortalecer la conservación de la biodiversidad marino-costera y mejorar la resiliencia socioeconómica de las comunidades que dependen de estos ecosistemas. Contempla una intervención en las nueve áreas marinas protegidas del Subsistema de Áreas Protegidas de la Zona Sur de Honduras (SAPZsurH), que abarcan 806,15 km².

La intervención se estructura en tres componentes estratégicos complementarios: i) orientado al fortalecimiento de la gobernanza y gestión efectiva de las áreas protegidas, mediante mecanismos de coordinación interinstitucional, participación comunitaria, actualización de instrumentos de planificación, vigilancia y sostenibilidad financiera; ii) promueve una gestión adaptativa basada en evidencia científica y monitoreo comunitario, fortaleciendo los sistemas de generación, análisis y utilización de información sobre biodiversidad, recursos pesqueros y condiciones ambientales. Ambos componentes buscan mejorar la capacidad de las instituciones, los cogestores y las comunidades para enfrentar amenazas como la degradación de manglares, la sobrepesca, la contaminación, la pérdida de biodiversidad y los efectos del cambio climático; iii) fortalecer medios de vida sostenibles, inclusivos y resilientes, mediante la diversificación económica, el desarrollo de emprendimientos vinculados a la economía azul y verde, el fortalecimiento de capacidades empresariales y el acceso a mercados y oportunidades de financiamiento. Se contempla apoyar mediante medidas específicas de medios de vida sostenibles, promoviendo especialmente la participación económica de mujeres y jóvenes. A través de un enfoque integrado de conservación, gobernanza y desarrollo económico local, el proyecto busca reducir las presiones sobre los ecosistemas, mejorar el bienestar de las comunidades costeras y consolidar un modelo de gestión territorial que contribuya a la sostenibilidad ambiental y económica del Golfo de Fonseca a largo plazo.

**OBJETIVO DE LA POSICIÓN:**

Asegurar la implementación integral, eficiente y oportuna del proyecto BAF en el Golfo de Fonseca, mediante la planificación, dirección técnica y operativa, gestión presupuestaria, seguimiento de resultados y articulación efectiva del consorcio, las instituciones y los actores territoriales, garantizando el cumplimiento de los objetivos, indicadores, compromisos contractuales y estándares de calidad de GOAL y del donante\*.\*

**RESPONSABILIDADES/FUNCIONES PRINCIPALES**

- Liderar la planificación, organización, implementación y seguimiento técnico, operativo y presupuestario del proyecto, garantizando el cumplimiento de los resultados, productos, indicadores y compromisos establecidos.
- Elaborar, actualizar y dar seguimiento a los planes operativos anuales, cronogramas, presupuestos y herramientas de gestión, en coordinación con los socios del consorcio y las áreas de soporte de GOAL.
- Coordinar la ejecución del proyecto, asegurando su integración, complementariedad y coherencia con los objetivos de conservación, gobernanza y desarrollo de medios de vida sostenibles.
- Identificar oportunamente riesgos, desviaciones y desafíos de implementación, proponiendo y gestionando medidas correctivas para garantizar el cumplimiento de los resultados.
- Supervisar y orientar al equipo técnico y operativo asignado al proyecto, promoviendo una gestión basada en resultados, el trabajo colaborativo y el cumplimiento de estándares institucionales.
- Coordinar técnica y programáticamente con la Coordinación del Programa Regional de Economía Azul de GOAL LATAM la planificación estratégica, implementación, seguimiento y revisión de los avances y resultados del proyecto.
- Responsable del seguimiento a la implementación técnica y operativa con CODDEFFAGOLF, Ilili y UNAH/FUNDAUNAH, asegurando la articulación de responsabilidades, cronogramas, productos ycompromisos establecidos en los acuerdos de asocio.
- Coordinar reuniones periódicas de planificación, coordinación y seguimiento con los socios del consorcio, promoviendo una gestión integrada, transparente y orientada al cumplimiento de resultados.
- Mantener relaciones de coordinación y cooperación con instituciones nacionales y locales, especialmente ICF, SERNA, DIGEPESCA, gobiernos municipales, organizaciones comunitarias y demás actores vinculados a la gestión de las áreas marinas protegidas.
- Representar técnicamente al proyecto en espacios de coordinación, diálogo y articulación institucional, de acuerdo con las delegaciones y lineamientos establecidos por GOAL.
- Promover alianzas estratégicas y mecanismos de participación entre instituciones públicas, comunidades, academia, sector privado y organizaciones de la sociedad civil que contribuyan a la sostenibilidad de las intervenciones.
- Velar por el cumplimiento de los procedimientos administrativos, financieros, contractuales y de adquisiciones establecidos por GOAL y Blue Action Fund.
- Otras funciones que le sean asignadas por el Director de Programas, en el marco de los objetivos y necesidades del programa.

**PERFIL MÍNIMO REQUERIDO**

***Estudios Profesionales:***

- Título universitario en Ciencias Ambientales, Biología, Ingeniería Forestal, Ingeniería Ambiental, Gestión de Recursos Naturales, Administración de Proyectos o carreras afines.
- Deseable posgrado en Administración de Proyectos, Gestión Ambiental, Conservación de Recursos Naturales, Desarrollo Sostenible o áreas relacionadas.

**Experiencia Profesional:**

- Experiencia mínima de seis (6) años en coordinación, gestión o implementación de proyectos de desarrollo sostenible, conservación ambiental, gestión de recursos marinos costeros o desarrollo económico territorial.
- Experiencia comprobada en planificación operativa, gestión presupuestaria, seguimiento de indicadores y elaboración de informes técnicos y financieros para proyectos financiados por cooperación internacional.
- Experiencia en coordinación de equipos multidisciplinarios, organizaciones socias y procesos de articulación con instituciones públicas, organizaciones comunitarias y actores del sector privado.

- Liderazgo y capacidad para coordinar equipos multidisciplinarios y socios estratégicos.

- Habilidades de negociación, articulación institucional y construcción de alianzas.

Asimismo, coordinará con los socios del consorcio, las áreas técnicas y de soporte de GOAL, instituciones gubernamentales, gobiernos locales, organizaciones comunitarias, academia, sector privado y demás actores estratégicos vinculados a la gestión de las áreas marinas protegidas y al desarrollo sostenible del Golfo de Fonseca.

jobs.title: Oficial de Seguridad y Acceso Humanitario
jobs.description:
**DATOS GENERALES**

- ***Sede del Puesto:** Caracas, Venezuela*
- ***Duración del Contrato:** 5 meses inicialmente*
- ***Supervisor***\*\*:\*\* *Asesor Regional de Seguridad y Acceso y Coordinará con el Director de Proyecto MIHR*

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL PROGRAMA:**

VENGOAL está implementando un programa multianual para apoyar y fortalecer la capacidad de las ONG locales en Venezuela para brindar servicios de salud materna, neonatal e infantil (MNCH) de calidad y mejorar el conocimiento, las prácticas y los resultados de la salud MNCH, incluyendo en comunidades indígenas, mineras y/o afectadas por la minería. Este cargo está abierto solo a residentes y ciudadanos venezolanos.

**PROPÓSITO DEL PUESTO:**

El Punto Focal de Seguridad y Acceso Humanitario de MIHR ELLA - VENGOAL es responsable de facilitar y garantizar un entorno seguro y el acceso sin obstáculos para las operaciones humanitarias en el proyecto MIHR ELLA. Esto incluye monitorear el contexto de seguridad, analizar riesgos, desarrollar estrategias de mitigación y mantener relaciones clave con actores relevantes para asegurar la entrega efectiva de asistencia humanitaria a las poblaciones necesitadas.

Además, MIHR ELLA - VENGOAL reconoce que los pueblos indígenas son titulares de derechos colectivos, poseen sistemas de conocimiento propios, estructuras de gobierno y cosmovisiones que deben ser respetados y comprendidos para establecer cualquier tipo de colaboración. En el marco de presencia en el país, es fundamental garantizar que todas las acciones se realicen con el consentimiento libre, previo e informado (CLPI) de los pueblos indígenas involucrados, asegurando la pertinencia cultural y el respeto a sus derechos y autonomía.

**RESPONSABILIDADES CLAVE**

**Análisis y Monitoreo de Seguridad:**

- Monitorear y analizar continuamente el contexto de seguridad y acceso humanitario en el país, incluyendo tendencias políticas, sociales, económicas y de conflicto.
- Apoyar al Asesor expatriado de Seguridad y Acceso Humanitario de VENGOAL en la producción de informes regulares y análisis de riesgo para informar la toma de decisiones estratégicas y operativas.
- Mantenerse al tanto del derecho internacional humanitario y los derechos humanos, y su impacto diferenciado en las poblaciones afectadas.
- Actuar como punto focal de comunicación principal entre la organización y las autoridades, líderes y miembros de las comunidades indígenas.
- Asesorar al equipo del proyecto sobre protocolos culturales, tiempos y formas adecuadas para el relacionamiento y la toma de decisiones según los usos y costumbres locales.
- Participar en el diseño e implementación de un sistema de monitoreo y evaluación participativo que incorpore indicadores y métodos culturalmente pertinentes.

**Estrategia y Gestión de Seguridad:**

- Desarrollar, implementar y actualizar planes y procedimientos de seguridad y acceso adaptados al contexto local.
- Asesorar a la dirección del país y al personal sobre las mejores prácticas de seguridad y acceso.
- Coordinar la respuesta a incidentes de seguridad y garantizar la gestión adecuada de la información.
- Facilitar y fortalecer la relación de confianza, comunicación y colaboración efectiva entre el Proyecto MIHR ELLA - VENGOAL y los pueblos, comunidades y/u organizaciones indígenas en el área de influencia del proyecto, asegurando que los principios de respeto, interculturalidad y pertinencia cultural guíen todas las fases del proyecto (diseño, implementación, monitoreo y evaluación).

**Coordinación y Enlace:**

- Establecer y mantener una red de contactos con autoridades locales, actores armados (cuando sea apropiado y seguro), líderes comunitarios, organizaciones humanitarias y otras partes interesadas.
- Participar activamente en foros de seguridad y acceso humanitario a nivel nacional y subnacional.
- Promover la concientización sobre los principios humanitarios (humanidad, imparcialidad, neutralidad e independencia) entre todos los actores relevantes.
- Apoyar en la mediación y resolución de posibles conflictos o malentendidos que puedan surgir, siempre desde un enfoque de respeto y construcción de consensos.
- Facilitar procesos de diálogo intercultural, asegurando que los mensajes se transmitan de manera clara, respetuosa y en los idiomas pertinentes (cuando sea posible).
- Alertar al equipo sobre posibles riesgos culturales, sociales o espirituales asociados a las intervenciones y proponer medidas de mitigación adecuadas.

**Capacitación y Desarrollo:**

- Identificar las necesidades de capacitación en seguridad y acceso para el personal MIHR ELLA y para los socios locales
- Organizar y facilitar sesiones de capacitación y talleres sobre seguridad y acceso humanitario.

**Reporte:**

- Elaborar informes periódicos sobre la situación de seguridad y acceso, incidentes y acciones tomadas.
- Contribuir a los informes internos y externos según sea necesario.

**PERFIL MÍNIMO REQUERIDO**

- Nacional Venezolano

***Formación Profesional:***

- Título universitario en seguridad, estudios de conflicto, relaciones internacionales, ciencias políticas, desarrollo o un campo relacionado.

***Experiencia Profesional***

- Mínimo de 2 años de experiencia relevante en seguridad y acceso humanitario, preferiblemente en contextos complejos o de emergencia.

***Habilidades:***

- Excelentes habilidades de análisis, comunicación y negociación.
- Capacidad probada para trabajar bajo presión y tomar decisiones rápidas.
- Conocimiento profundo de los principios humanitarios y el derecho internacional humanitario.
- Conocimiento profundo del enfoque sensible al conflicto, acción sin daño, enfoque diferencial y edad.
- Fluidez en español oral y escrito. Dominio del inglés será altamente apreciado.
- Habilidades informáticas avanzadas (MS Office, herramientas de mapeo, etc.).

***Competencias:***

- Liderazgo y trabajo en equipo.
- Comunicación efectiva.
- Planificación y organización.
- Toma de decisiones y resolución de problemas.
- Adaptabilidad y flexibilidad.
- Sensibilidad cultural.

***Condiciones de Trabajo:***

- El puesto puede requerir viajes frecuentes a áreas de alto riesgo dentro del país.
- Disponibilidad para trabajar fuera del horario laboral habitual en situaciones de emergencia.

**COORDINACIÓN**

El profesional reportará al Director de Proyecto MIHR ELLA, y coordinará con el Asesor de Seguridad y Acceso.

**SALVAGUARDIA**

Los niños, niñas y los adultos en situación de vulnerabilidad deben estar protegidos en la mayor medida posible de acciones deliberadas o inadvertidas y fallas que los ponen en riesgo de abuso, explotación sexual, lesiones y cualquier otro daño. Una de las formas en que VENGOAL muestra este compromiso continuo con la protección es incluir rigurosos antecedentes y verificaciones de referencia en el proceso de selección para todos los candidatos.

**RESPONSABILIDAD DENTRO DE VENGOAL**

Junto con nuestra política de protección, VENGOAL es un empleador que ofrece igualdad de oportunidades y tiene un conjunto de políticas de integridad. Se espera que cualquier candidato que ofrezca un trabajo con VENGOAL se adhiera a las siguientes áreas clave de responsabilidad:
