jobs.title: Human Resources Officer - Damascus
jobs.description:
The HR Officer ensures that HR administration at DCA Syria is accurate, timely, confidential and compliant with DCA policies, staff regulations and applicable national labour law. Reporting to the HR Coordinator, the position covers personnel files, recruitment support, contract administration, onboarding and offboarding, and leave and attendance for all staff across the country office and its field locations. It acts as the first point of contact for line managers on HR matters, prepares documents for the HR Coordinator’s approval, escalates complex or sensitive cases, and handles confidential data under strict access and retention rules.

**Functional Responsibilities**

- Acts as first point of contact for line managers on HR administration of their teams, escalating complex or sensitive cases to the HR Coordinator when necessary.
- Ensures HR practice complies with DCA policies, staff regulations, HR procedures and applicable national labour law, including social security requirements.
- Contributes to drafting local HR policies, procedures and tools (such as salary scales, promotion procedures and personnel file standards) and implements them once approved.
- Contributes to implementing the country office’s HR priorities and annual HR strategy so that HR supports operational needs.
- Creates and maintains complete, confidential personnel files (physical and digital) for all staff: contracts, ID copies, certificates, performance evaluations, training records, and disciplinary or grievance documents.
- Runs quarterly file audits against a standard checklist and follows up on missing or expired documents.
- Keeps the HRIS and staff lists up to date with new hires, changes and separations.
- Applies data-protection and confidentiality rules, including access control, retention and archiving.
- Supports recruitment by screening applications, preparing shortlists, arranging interviews and conducting reference checks, in line with DCA procedures.
- Prepares contracts, amendments, extensions, transfers, acting-up arrangements and separation documents for approval by the HR Coordinator.
- Confirms with line managers and Finance that contract terms match approved job descriptions, grades, budgets and donor funding.
- Maintains a contract tracker and alerts line managers at least 60 days before contract end dates, and ahead of probation reviews and renewals.
- Prepares employment, salary and other HR letters on request, for approval by the HR Coordinator.
- Ensures onboarding (induction documentation, policy acknowledgements) and offboarding (clearance, final entitlements, exit documents) are completed and filed.
- Follows up probation evaluations with line managers and files the DCA form signed by staff and line manager.
- Supports the performance management cycle with reminders, collection of evaluations and filing.
- Maintains training records for all staff and ensures training logistics are in place to support learning and development.
- Maintains accurate records of all leave types (annual, sick, maternity and paternity, unpaid, special) and up-to-date leave balances.
- Verifies timesheets, attendance and overtime against leave records, and advises staff and managers on leave entitlements on request.
- Provides Finance with verified monthly HR inputs for payroll (contract changes, leave, attendance).
- Prepares monthly or quarterly reports (headcount, turnover, contract expiries, leave liabilities) and supports audits and donor verification.
- Maintains and improves HR forms, templates and filing systems, and supports HR projects.

**Minimum qualifications and experience**

- Bachelor’s degree in human resources, business administration or a related field.
- At least 4 years of HR experience covering HR administration, recruitment and personnel management, and payroll support.
- Working knowledge of Syrian labour law and social security procedures.
- Fluent written and spoken Arabic and English.
- Good command of MS Office (especially Excel), and experience with HRIS or HR databases.
- High level of discretion, attention to detail and ability to work to deadlines.

jobs.title: Compliance and data security analyst
jobs.description:
**We're hiring**

**Compliance and data security analyst**

**LOCATION: Amsterdam, Netherlands**
0.8 FTE / 32 hours per week

**GROSS SALARY RANGE: EUR 33,446-38,275**

Laterite is looking for a Compliance and Data Security Analyst to help our research teams meet privacy, information-security and client obligations. You will improve how we manage compliance, set up missing processes and work with colleagues across our country offices to put agreed actions into practice.

**This position is open to candidates of all nationalities who have the legal right to work in the Netherlands. Please note that we are unable to provide sponsorship.**

**WHO WE ARE**

Laterite is a data, research, and analytics firm working on complex international development challenges. We partner with universities, global think tanks, international NGOs, multilateral donors, and government ministries. Our clients include the World Bank, TechnoServe, the Mastercard Foundation, and others.

We operate across the Netherlands, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and Peru, with 80+ full-time staff and more than 2,000 enumerators. We believe meaningful impact requires being on the ground, building local teams, and establishing long-term trust. Our office culture is collaborative and gives people autonomy to grow into their roles.

**THE ENVIRONMENT YOU'RE STEPPING INTO**

You will join our Netherlands team in a collaborative and engaging environment. We are low on bureaucracy but high on individual accountability. You won't be micromanaged here. We want you to use your judgment to solve problems, support our fast-paced teams and improve the systems you work with. You will report to our Operations Manager and work closely with our Analytics team, Data Protection Officers, and research, operations and technical colleagues across country offices. Your work will help keep compliance practical and manageable for colleagues.

**HOW YOU'LL MAKE AN IMPACT**

You will help protect the data entrusted to Laterite and make compliance easier to maintain across our research and operations. During your first six months, you will take over recurring work and help address an agreed set of priority gaps.

***An important note on this role***

**You will help build and improve our compliance processes.** Some routines are already in place, while others need to be developed with the Operations Manager and DPOs. We are developing processes that colleagues can use without unnecessary administration.

**Laterite is not a technology company but is building tech products to complement our research and social impact work.** Your experience on Laterite's Analytics team will be unique and likely dissimilar to similar roles within technology companies.

**The DPOs lead on local requirements and regulatory changes.** You will help coordinate follow-up across countries and help check that agreed actions are implemented. Management retains policy approval and risk decisions. This role is not an appointment as DPO or sole legal or technical security lead.

**Technical work will reflect your experience and the agreed scope**. This includes routine Google Workspace administration and assessing device-management improvements with technical colleagues. Implementation and any wider endpoint responsibilities will be agreed separately.

Your responsibilities will include:

- **Design and set up missing compliance processes**, working with the Operations Manager and DPOs to address applicable legal requirements and agreed priorities.
- **Improve how we manage compliance with the Operations Manager**. Make processes easy to maintain and reduce unnecessary work for colleagues.
- **Coordinate the DPO group and follow up implementation across countries**. The DPOs lead on local requirements and regulatory changes. Keep actions moving and flag gaps or delays to the Operations Manager.
- **Help assess and roll out device-management improvements with technical colleagues**. Follow up security reviews and agreed actions on access, backups, incident procedures and secure software development.
- **Support privacy work across research projects**, including processing records, initial privacy checks, approved agreements and notices, training, and follow-up on data requests or incidents. Arrange specialist review where needed.
- **Prepare client security questionnaires and keep supplier and subprocessor records current**, including AI services. Check that responses are supported by evidence and reviewed before submission.
- **Maintain compliance records and supporting evidence**. Follow up agreed actions with colleagues and prepare short progress updates.
- **Carry out agreed Google Workspace administration**, such as account setup and closure, using approved procedures. Technical duties will reflect your experience and agreed responsibilities.

You will manage agreed routines independently, ask for specialist input when needed and keep colleagues informed of progress. The Operations Manager, DPOs and technical colleagues will support you in the areas they lead.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

You have one to three years of practical experience in privacy, information security, compliance or operations, with examples of improving processes and completing work independently. You enjoy bringing structure to complex workflows and draw energy from working on data and cybersecurity.

Specifically, you have:

- A bachelor's or master's degree in law, cybersecurity, information systems, business information technology, security studies or a related field.
- Working knowledge of GDPR and the ability to explain privacy and security requirements clearly.
- Experience keeping reliable records, checking evidence and following up actions independently.
- The ability to design workable processes and reduce unnecessary administration.
- Confidence coordinating teams across offices and raising gaps or delays constructively.
- Clear written and spoken English. Dutch is not required or preferred.
- Good judgment about when to seek legal or technical advice.

In addition, we welcome:

- Experience with client questionnaires, audits or supplier and subprocessor reviews.
- Experience in research, international operations or international development.
- Familiarity with Google Workspace administration, endpoint security or device management.
- Interest in learning across privacy, information security and operations.
- Familiarity with secure software development.

We consider practical experience alongside qualifications. If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be exactly who we're looking for.

**WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU**

- **Competitive compensation.** EUR 33,446-38,275 gross per year at 0.8 FTE, including holiday allowance, commensurate with experience, plus 18.4 days of annual leave. Salaries are pegged against Laterite's pay matrix and grades are reviewed every 12 months.
- **Professional growth.** Laterite provides an annual learning budget of up to USD 1,000 per person and 10 days of time off for professional learning each year. You will also have the chance to apply your skills in an organisation working in the social sectors.
- **Flexibility.** 32 hours per week (0.8 FTE), with 0.6 or 1 FTE open for discussion. You can work from home a couple of days per week and from a remote location of your choice for up to 6 weeks per year. Our office is in the heart of Amsterdam, about a fifteen-minute walk from Amsterdam Centraal Station.

jobs.title: WASH & Shelter Project Manager - Deir ez-Zor
jobs.description:

- The WASH and Shelter Project Manager is responsible for planning, developing, monitoring, and evaluating assigned WASH and shelter projects while assessing needs, designing projects, writing proposals, initiating, and effectively managing and reporting on the project according to the objectives, timeframe, and budget. Provide technical support, leadership, and strategic direction; meet quality standards in WASH and shelter delivery, encouraging beneficiary participation, liaise with other stakeholders, and manage and train WASH and shelter staff.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Manage assigned the projects in order to meet objectives within budget and allocated time frames.
- Set clear objectives and indicators for WASH and shelter activities in collaboration with the shelter staff, field managers, and, where appropriate, with the local communities.
- Continuously monitor and supervise WASH and shelter activities, overseeing the technical design and execution and evaluating progress through outputs and impacts using both quantitative and qualitative data.
- Ensure accurate and timely reporting of activities according to donor and other applicable timeframes and formats.
- Provide input into the integration of beneficiary participation and accountability in all aspects of the project
- Provide strong leadership of the assigned shelter project, ensuring short- and long-term positive impacts and outcomes for the beneficiaries, local authorities (where applicable), other partners and stakeholders, and local shelter staff.

- Manage the shelter budget for assigned projects and ensure all expenses are according to budget and meet the IYD standards concerning financial management, including accountability and good governance.

- Provide coaching and technical supervision to staff to develop staff ownership and responsibility.
- Develop and maintain appropriate, regular, transparent, and supportive communication structures with the assigned shelter team and other relevant stakeholders (e.g. beneficiaries, community leaders, local and national government officials, UN agencies, and other NGOs) to ensure good cooperation and partnerships.

- Creativity

- Commitment to Continuous Learning
- Technological Awareness.

- Leadership
- Building Trust
- Vision
- Managing Performance
- Empowering Others

1. **Technical Competencies:**

- Strong knowledge of the rules and regulations of major institutional donors such as UN agencies, ECHO, European Commission, US Government donors, and UK donors.

jobs.title: Climate Fundraising Expert
jobs.description:
**Join MSF OCG as a Climate Fundraising Expert!**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

The EcoShift project aims to enable MSF to access new, non-cannibalising funding streams for climate mitigation and adaptation in support of our medical humanitarian mission by establishing the strategic, operational, and fundraising foundations required to engage effectively with climate-focused donors. Sponsored by MSF Operational Center Geneva and funded by the Transformational Investment Capacity, it is intended for the entire MSF movement.

Within the ecoShift project, the Climate Fundraising Expert develops a compelling case for support and a fundraising strategy for MSF’s international Climate Fund to mobilise donor support across the movement. Central to the role is building the knowledge, skills and confidence of philanthropy teams in MSF sections to navigate the specificities of climate fundraising, including donor motivations and expectations and the links between climate action and MSF’s medical humanitarian mission. The Expert works alongside these teams to translate this expertise into effective implementation of the strategy in their respective markets.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

The core responsibilities of the ecoShift Climate Fundraising expert are:

- Create a robust, donor-ready case for support, translating MSF’s climate-relevant work into compelling, fundable propositions and clearly articulating the links between climate action and MSF’s medical humanitarian mission. Develop the corresponding donor-facing materials and content, including fundraising brochures, and presentations, ensuring consistent and compelling messaging across formats.
- Building on ecoShift phase 1, develop a fundraising strategy for the Climate Fund, defining fundraising objectives, priority donor segments and a donor engagement roadmap. Ground the strategy in an assessment of climate-aligned donor prospects and funding opportunities - including philanthropic and institutional donors and climate-specific funding mechanisms - considering their priorities, eligibility criteria and funding modalities, with a particular focus on donors new to MSF.
- Build the capacity of philanthropy teams in priority markets to engage in climate fundraising through practical tools, a dedicated SharePoint site, ongoing guidance, and peer learning, focusing on climate terminology and concepts, donor motivations and expectations, and communicating climate-related impact within MSF’s medical humanitarian mission.
- Work alongside philanthropy teams in MSF sections to adapt and implement the strategy in their markets. Jointly develop and implement donor-specific engagement plans, supporting, when relevant, initial relationship-building, donor presentations and follow-up, while strengthening teams’ capacity through practical experience and shared learning.
- Monitor progress against fundraising objectives and the development of the donor pipeline with participating sections. Use results, donor feedback and teams’ experience to refine the strategy, engagement approaches and capacity-building support.
- Contribute to the preparation and implementation of the handover plan for the International Office (IO) fundraising team, ensuring continuity of the fundraising strategy, support to section teams and climate fundraising expertise during the transition to “Business As Usual” phase, that the Expert may be part of.

## Your profile

*Education*

- University degree in Business Management, Marketing, Environmental studies, Communications, or International Relations or equivalent professional experience

*Experience*

- At least five years’ experience in philanthropy or institutional fundraising, including demonstrated success in securing support for climate-related initiatives.
- Proven experience developing fundraising strategies, compelling cases for support and tailored donor proposals.
- Experience designing and delivering training, coaching or practical support to fundraising teams.
- Experience working across countries and organisational entities.
- Familiarity with MSF or medical humanitarian organisations is an asset.

*Languages*

- English and French are the working languages of MSF Switzerland. Excellent written and spoken English, C1 necessary.
- French, B2 an asset.

*Technical & Functional Knowledge*

- Strong understanding of climate philanthropy and relevant funding mechanisms, including donor priorities, eligibility requirements and funding modalities.
- Sound knowledge of climate concepts, including mitigation, adaptation, resilience and decarbonisation, and their connections to health and humanitarian action.
- Ability to translate technical climate information into credible fundraising propositions and communicate climate-related results accurately.
- Knowledge of prospect research, donor cultivation, proposal development, stewardship and pipeline management.
- Familiarity with adult learning approaches and the development of practical fundraising resources.

*Skills*

- Strategic thinking combined with the ability to translate plans into practical action.
- Excellent writing, presentation and interpersonal communication skills.
- Strong facilitation and coaching skills, with the ability to adapt support to different levels of knowledge and experience.
- Ability to build trust, influence and coordinate across teams without direct managerial authority.
- Strong analytical, organisational and project management skills.
- Excellent ability to work in a multicultural environment successfully and to demonstrate commitment and support for diversity, gender-responsive, inclusive, and non-discriminatory behaviour and attitudes.

## Terms of employment

- Part-time position 80% (32h/week)
- Fixed-term contract, until 31.07.2027
- Working place: Any MSF HQ office that allows sufficient overlap with the team’s working hours.
- Ideal start date: February 1st, 2027
- The position may be hosted by different MSF entities. The final contracting entity, duty station and applicable employment conditions will be determined by MSF according to organisational needs, contractual feasibility and internal validation.

jobs.title: Human Resources Assistant (Daily-Worker) - Damascus
jobs.description:
The HR Assistant is responsible for the day-to-day running of HR data archiving (physical and digital) and the administrative side of the recruitment process. The role works under the guidance of the HR Coordinator, handles confidential information, and does not take selection or approval decisions.

**Functional Responsibilities**

- Organise, scan, index and file HR documents (physical and digital) following the DCA personnel file standard and naming convention.
- Create and complete new joiner files from the checklist, and update existing files as documents change.
- Track missing or expired documents, and prepare follow-up lists for the HR Coordinator.
- Support the collection and filing of documents from staff, including during all-staff document requests.
- Maintain the archive index and staff document trackers, and make sure files are retrievable on request.
- Apply confidentiality, access-control, retention and archiving rules, and keep files secure at all times.
- Prepare and publish vacancy announcements as instructed, and keep the vacancy tracker up to date.
- Receive and register applications, and keep the recruitment records and candidate data organised.
- Prepare longlists and screening sheets for review by the HR Coordinator and hiring managers.
- Schedule interviews and tests, contact candidates, prepare interview packs, and record interview outcomes.
- Send reference check forms and regret messages as instructed, and file the replies.
- Compile complete recruitment files for each vacancy (advertisement, applications, scoring sheets, selection reports, references).

- Keep candidate information strictly confidential.
- Prepare reports and summaries on archive status and recruitment activity (open vacancies, files complete or incomplete) when requested.
- Suggest improvements to filing systems, forms and templates.

**Minimum qualifications and experience**

- University degree or diploma in human resources, business administration, management or a related field.
- At least 1 year of experience in HR or administrative support, including filing and documentation.

- Strong attention to detail, organisation and discretion with confidential information.

jobs.title: OFICIAL DE ADMINISTRACION Y FINANZAS
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
**OBJETIVO DEL TRABAJO**

El (la) oficial de administración y finanzas, garantizará el cumplimiento de los procedimientos administrativos, de recursos humanos (RRHH) y finanzas de acuerdo con las políticas internas de ACTED y de los donantes en la base de Carabobo.

El (la) oficial de administración y finanzas, trabajará bajo la supervisión directa del gerente de base y en coordinación con los diferentes de departamentos de la oficina central de Caracas.

**Funciones y Responsabilidades**

**1. Finanzas**

- Asegurar el seguimiento del presupuesto/control de gastos de los proyectos a través del BFU proporcionado desde el departamento financiero de Caracas.
- Apoyar en la elaboración de presupuestos para nuevos proyectos cuando sea requerido.
- Monitorear la conformidad de los documentos financieros.
- Gestionar la tesorería de la base de Carabobo.
- Realizar y gestionar los pagos en efectivos cuando sean autorizados según los procedimientos internos de ACTED y la regulación de los donantes.
- Realizar el arqueo de caja y completar el CFU semanalmente.
- Apoyar en la evaluación de las necesidades mensuales de efectivo para la base.
- Elaborar y verificar las cuentas de cobro del personal para la gestión efectiva de sus honorarios profesionales.
- Garantizar la ejecución oportuna de pagos a proveedores.
- Apoyo en auditorias, escaneo verificación, corrección de piezas y expedientes, hasta cerrar de manera satisfactoria los archivos para la organización y donantes.
- Recibir, enviar, registrar, distribuir, archivar y mantener física y digitalmente los documentos de archivo en las unidades de conservación e instalación de acuerdo con los procedimientos.

**2. Administración**

- Apoyar técnicamente el proceso de transferencias documentales.
- Elaborar, tramitar y mantener seguimiento oportuno de las actividades y procedimientos a desarrollar.
- Apoyo logístico, organizar las solicitudes de compra y/o servicio de acuerdo con los procedimientos de la organización y de los donantes.
- Desarrollar y actualizar los procesos administrativos de Acted: reglamento interno, Manual de procedimientos, memos, etc.
- Seguimiento y actualización de los procesos legales: representación legal, registros diversos (Ministerios e instituciones Públicas, etc.).
- Gestionar los contratos administrativos (oficinas, guest-house) y el seguimiento administrativo (renovación de contratos, relación con los puntos focales, etc.).

**3. Recursos Humanos**

- Asegurarse de que los equipos de la base conocen, entienden, aplican y respetan el reglamento interno de ACTED.
- Reclutamiento (en coordinación con el Departamento de Recursos Humanos) del personal nacional de la base.
- Revisión de los TDR de los equipos a fin de actualizarlos y ajustarlos a los contratos laborales.
- Gestionar el seguimiento administrativo de los documentos de los empleados (seguimiento de las vacaciones, de las ausencias, del pago de los cargos sociales, etc.).
- Junto con el gerente de base hacer el seguimiento de las evaluaciones anuales.
- Proponer planes de formaciones de los empleados cuando es necesario.
- Soporte en relaciones laborales y administración del personal.
- Apoyar el establecimiento de buenas relaciones interpersonales de trabajo en la base. (Resolución de conflictos).
- Controlar los archivos de Recursos Humanos.
- Liquidación de nómina, gestión de seguridad social y novedades relacionados con los contratos del personal contratado.
- Apoyar el desarrollo y actualización de las políticas de gestión nacional de recursos humanos.
- Atender y dar respuesta oportuna a los requerimientos, dudas o solicitudes administrativas presentadas por el staff.
- ## Requisitos
- Obligatorios:
- Profesional graduado titulado (a) como administrador de empresas, ingeniero industrial, contador público o carreras afines.
- Al menos tres (3) años de experiencia en administración y finanzas. (Preferiblemente en una ONG internacional).
- Experiencia en el trato con socios nacionales y autoridades locales/gubernamentales
- Experiencia en habilidades organizativas comprobadas.
- Experiencia trabajando en entornos de trabajo multicultural
- Manejo avanzado de herramientas de reporte financiero y control de gastos.
- Conocimiento de procesos de procura y normativas de transparencia.
- Dominio de Paquete Microsoft Office
- Habilidades blandas: dinamismo, liderazgo, gestión de equipo, autonomía, alta atención al detalle, responsabilidad, comunicación asertiva, orientación a resultados, transparencia, flexibilidad.
- **Competencias:**
- Compromiso con la transparencia en el manejo de fondos y procesos de selección.
- Capacidad para la organización y priorización de actividades.
- Orientación al servicio: disposición para dar respuesta a los requerimientos con amabilidad, empatía y respeto, incluso en situaciones bajo presión.
- Capacidad de atención al detalle.

## Condiciones

- Contrato de prestación de servicios bajo la figura de Honorarios Profesionales durante 3 meses con posibilidad de renovación según disponibilidad presupuestaria y desempeño.
- Lugar de trabajo: Oficina de ACTED en Carabobo - Venezuela.
- Honorarios profesionales según la escala de la organización.

Trabajo presencial y posibles viajes a las bases.

jobs.title: Global Security and Operations Advisor
jobs.description:
The Norwegian Red Cross is seeking an experienced Global Security and Operations Advisor for a full-time position based at our headquarters in Oslo.

The position is part of the Operations Unit within the International Department, which provides strategic direction and operational support to the Norwegian Red Cross's international humanitarian operations. The unit is responsible for global operational preparedness, emergency response, security management and coordination with Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement partners.

As Global Security and Operations Advisor, you will strengthen security management across our international operations, support country offices in risk assessment and emergency preparedness, and provide strategic advice to senior management. You will play a key role in critical incident management, staff safety and capacity building, working closely with the ICRC, IFRC and our regional and country teams.

We are looking for a professional with extensive experience in humanitarian operations as well as security management in complex humanitarian environments, strong coordination and analytical skills, and the ability to operate effectively under pressure.

The position involves international travel, potentially up to three months per year.

## Responsibilities

- Oversee the adequate maintenance and use of security tools and procedures to ensure that the Norwegian Red Cross can fulfill its duty of care obligations towards its staff.
- Ensure capacity building of field staff and in situ support to enable an adequate security management in priority countries and priority emergency response operations.
- Support humanitarian operations management in critical countries at the request of the Head of Operations.
- Ensure strong and timely coordination with Norwegian Red Cross security staff at regional and country levels, as well as with International HR. Liaise with ICRC and IFRC Secretariat, as well as with relevant national society security personnel.

## Qualifications

\- Considerable experience from security and operational management in complex emergencies.
\- Relevant critical incident management experience an asset.
\- Available to deploy for short field missions on short notice following a request.
\- Proven ability to handling of confidential information and documents
\- Good understanding of information technology and how to use it for security management a requirement
\- Good knowledge of humanitarian systems is an asset. Fluency in English required. Proficiency in Norwegian, French, Russian or Arabic is an asset.

## Personal qualifications

\- Ability to work under stress and support others working under stress
\- Ability to think holistically and identify solutions
\- Ability to cooperate and share competency.
\- Ability to convince and gain acceptance
\- Ability to communicate effectively.
\- Ability to develop others. Ability to be solution oriented

## We offer

- Meaningful and challenging work in Norway's largest volunteer-based humanitarian organisation, making a real difference in complex humanitarian contexts.
- The opportunity to contribute to the safety and security of humanitarian staff and operations worldwide.
- A dynamic, international working environment with dedicated colleagues and a strong professional network across the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement.
- Employment conditions governed by the applicable collective bargaining agreements, currently the Tekna Basic Agreement and Negotia Collective Agreement.
- The position is based in Oslo and involves international travel, potentially up to three months per year.
- Flexibility to respond to critical incidents outside regular working hours may be required.

The Norwegian Red Cross is committed to diversity and inclusion. We encourage qualified candidates to apply regardless of age, gender, disability, religion, belief or ethnic background. We provide reasonable workplace accommodations when needed.

jobs.title: HR Specialist
jobs.company: Medecins du Monde - Turkey / Dunya Doktorlari Dernegi
jobs.description:
**Vacancy Announcement: HR Specialist, Damascus, Syria**

**Dünya Doktorları Derneği**

**Medecins du Monde Turkey (MDM-T) /** **Dünya Doktorları Dernegi (DDD)** is a Turkish based humanitarian non-governmental organisation that facilitates access to healthcare for populations affected by armed conflict, violence, natural disasters, disease, famine, poverty and exclusion.

Our organization collaborates with partners and key stakeholders to implement projects that facilitate access to primary and secondary-level healthcare services to respond to the medical needs of displaced population.

DDD is the 16th member of the Doctors of the World International Network that is committed to meeting the health needs of vulnerable people globally.

Please visit [www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr](http://www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr) to learn more.

**Organisation:**

DDD (MdM Türkiye)

**Duty Station:**

Damascus, Syria

**Contract Duration:**

6.months,renewable

**Reporting to:**

DAM Office Manager

**About the role**

DDD is recruiting an HR Specialist, based in the Damascus operational office, to provide day-to-day HR services within the scope assigned by the Office Manager. The Specialist will coordinate personnel administration, recruitment, onboarding, payroll preparation and employment-related administrative requirements.

During the initial set-up, the Damascus office will provide HR support to DDD’s teams in Syria. The Specialist will take over agreed operational HR tasks from Istanbul HQ and establish the records, tools and workflows needed to carry them out, working with HQ on technical guidance, policy interpretation and approvals under DDD’s delegation of authority. As HR capacity is established in other offices, responsibilities may be redistributed.

**Key responsibilities**

*Personnel administration and payroll preparation*

- Prepare employment contracts, amendments and other personnel documents for review and signature, and maintain accurate and confidential personnel files.
- Track contract expiry dates, probation periods, renewals, leave and attendance, and alert managers to upcoming decisions and deadlines.
- Prepare and verify monthly payroll inputs, including contractual changes, attendance, leave and approved adjustments, and resolve discrepancies with Finance.
- Coordinate staff departures, including clearance, exit documentation and communication to Finance and other functions.

*Recruitment, onboarding and staff support*

- Coordinate recruitment with hiring managers, including vacancy publication, candidate communication, interviews, reference checks and documentation of selection decisions.
- Organise onboarding and explain HR procedures, employment conditions and staff support arrangements to new employees.
- Support managers with probation objectives and reviews and periodic performance reviews; consolidate training needs and follow up on agreed actions.
- Respond to routine staff queries and refer sensitive personnel matters through the appropriate confidential channels.

*Employment compliance*

- Monitor employment-related administrative requirements with country management, HQ and legal advisers, and maintain a calendar of applicable deadlines.
- Prepare and verify documentation for employee registration, social insurance and other employment-related declarations, in coordination with Administration and Finance.
- Retain evidence of submissions and decisions, and prepare HR documentation for internal reviews, audits and compliance checks.

*HR systems, reporting and workforce planning*

- Establish and maintain reliable HR records and tracking tools for staffing, recruitment, contracts, probation, leave and attendance, agreeing with each field location who provides the data, how it is checked and when it is submitted.
- Prepare periodic HR reports and provide staffing data to Finance for personnel cost forecasts, budget preparation and BvA; help country management anticipate vacancies, recruitment and contract renewals.
- Document recurring HR workflows and develop practical templates and checklists, supporting field managers and focal points in applying them.
- Coordinate the transfer of agreed HR responsibilities, records and tools from Istanbul to Damascus, identifying gaps and following up on corrective actions with HQ and country management.

*HR and administrative organisation and capacity development*

- Contribute to the progressive transfer of operational HR and administrative responsibilities from Istanbul to Damascus, and clarify responsibilities and information flows between Damascus, other field locations, country management and HQ.
- Assess existing personnel administration practices, records, tools and workflows within the scope of operations.
- Supervise and support HR and administrative personnel assigned to the scope of operations, and identify their training and capacity development needs.
- Propose improvements that strengthen administrative reliability, legal compliance and operational efficiency without unnecessarily complicating existing processes.

Istanbul HQ retains institutional HR policy oversight, methodological guidance and the validation responsibilities established under DDD’s delegation of authority. Recruitment decisions, contractual commitments and formal approvals follow DDD’s delegation of authority.

**Initial priorities**

- Review personnel records, contracts, payroll inputs and pending employment formalities for the teams initially supported by the Damascus office.
- Establish a reliable personnel register, HR calendar and monthly payroll preparation schedule with Finance.
- Agree and implement the transfer of operational HR tasks from Istanbul and establish reporting arrangements with the teams supported by Damascus.

**Required profile**

- Relevant university qualification in human resources, business administration, management, law or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Demonstrated experience in personnel administration, recruitment and payroll preparation in an NGO, international organisation or comparable operational environment.
- Practical knowledge of Syrian employment administration and applicable labour and social insurance requirements.
- Proficiency in Excel and experience maintaining reliable HR records or using HR information systems.
- Ability to organise competing priorities, handle confidential information with discretion and work with managers and staff across locations.
- Professional working proficiency in Arabic and English.

**Expected professional competencies**

- Organisational judgement: identifies administrative priorities, anticipates deadlines and distinguishes material compliance risks from routine issues.
- Operational autonomy: organises priorities, takes initiative and resolves day-to-day HR and administrative problems without continuous supervision.
- Practical problem-solving: develops simple, reliable and workable administrative solutions adapted to operational constraints.
- Collaboration: maintains constructive working relationships with operational teams, HQ counterparts, public administrations and external advisers.
- Reliability and confidentiality: commitment to accurate personnel records, professional discretion, data confidentiality and consistent application of procedures.
- Adaptability: willingness to work in an evolving organisational environment where some systems, procedures and responsibilities remain under development.

**Compliance & Ethics**
Promote and encourage a culture of compliance and ethics throughout Dünya Doktorları Derneği. As applicable to the position, maintains a clear understanding of Dünya Doktorları Derneği and donor compliance and ethics standards and adheres to those standards. Conducts work with the highest level of integrity. Communicates these values to staff and to partners and requires them to adhere to these values.

**Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse**
Actively promote PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) standards within Dünya Doktorları Derneği and amongst beneficiaries served by Dünya Doktorları Derneği.

**NB:** Considering the purpose and values of the organisation, DDD requests to its employee complete flexibility in term of duties and commitment, as their job description and job title can be adjusted throughout the year according to needs and priorities.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.Please be advised that female candidates are highly encouraged.

*Dünya Doktorları Derneği is an equal opportunity employer whereby we ensure all hiring and employment decisions, and operates all programs, services, and functions without the practices that discriminate against any person employed or seeking employment based on race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, age, marital status, disability, genetic information or any other status or characteristic protected under applicable law.*

**Closure Date: 31.11.2026**

Due to the urgency to fill this post, DDD reserves the right to review the CVs on a rolling basis and selected candidates may be interviewed prior to the closing dates listed, therefore early applications are encouraged.
DDD is not in a position to respond to every applicant individually due to the anticipated high number of applications.
Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted for the first interview.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

**General Information**
DDD retains the discretion to re-advertise the vacancy, to cancel the recruitment, to offer a contract with a modified job description or for a different duration, or to offer a contract at a lower grade.

jobs.title: Call for Proposals : Study on youth inclusion trajectories in Syria’s transition
jobs.description:
The Advocacy Department of SIF is seeking a consultancy firm or multidisciplinary team to conduct a study on the inclusion trajectories of young women and young men in Syria's transition.

As Syria navigates a transition shaped by the consequences of conflict and the challenges of reconstruction, the study aims to better understand the factors that enable or hinder young people's inclusion and the realisation of their rights.

Using a participatory approach, the study will inform the development of programmatic and advocacy recommendations for Syrian authorities, donors, international organisations and civil society actors.

**Required expertise:** Consultancy firms or multidisciplinary teams with expertise in quantitative and qualitative research, youth and inclusion, children's rights and child protection, as well as conflict and transition contexts. The involvement of Syrian researchers based in Syria is required.

**Submission deadline: 9 December 2026**

**Contact: i.sinan@sif.org**

**Please consult the Terms of Reference for application modalities:** [**ToR SIF Study on youth inclusion trajectories in Syria**](https://sif.org/images/ressources/plaidoyer/ToR_SIF-Study-on-youth-inclusion-in-Syria.pdf)

**----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------**

La Direction du Plaidoyer du SIF recherche un cabinet de conseil ou une équipe multidisciplinaire pour réaliser une étude sur les trajectoires d’inclusion des jeunes femmes et des jeunes hommes dans la Syrie en transition.

Dans le contexte Syrien de transition marqué par les conséquences du conflit et les défis de reconstruction, cette étude vise à mieux comprendre les facteurs qui favorisent ou entravent l’inclusion des jeunes et la réalisation de leurs droits.

Fondée sur une approche participative, elle permettra de formuler des recommandations programmatiques et de plaidoyer à destination des autorités syriennes, des bailleurs, des organisations internationales et des acteurs de la société civile.

**Profils recherchés :** cabinets de conseil ou équipes multidisciplinaires disposant d’une expertise en recherche quantitative et qualitative, jeunesse et inclusion, droits et protection de l’enfance, ainsi qu’en contextes de conflit et de transition. La participation de chercheurs et chercheuses syriens présents sur place est requise.

**Date limite de soumission : 9 décembre 2026**

**Contact : i.sinan@sif.org**

**Consulter les termes de référence pour connaître les modalités de candidature :** [**TdR SIF Etude sur les trajectoires d’inclusion des jeunes en Syrie**](https://sif.org/images/ressources/plaidoyer/TdR-SIF-Etude-sur-les-trajectoires-dinclusion-des-jeunes-en-Syrie.pdf.pdf)

**Terms of Reference**

**Request for Quotation for Final Independent Project Evaluation service, for the project titled “Towards More and Better Employment through Enhanced Support to Private Sectors in Southern Iraq – with a Focus on Green Business”**

1. ## Background information

Private sector development in Iraq is challenged by several factors, as the economy is largely dominated by the oil sector, and state-owned enterprises further impede incentives for private sector growth and diversification in the wider economy. Moreover, local firms struggle to become competitive within national and international markets, and an abundance of cheap imports combined with low levels of investment has hindered the development of nascent domestic activities[1.](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark0) Iraq is also known for a challenging business environment, which makes it difficult for “start-ups” and/or MSMEs to flourish and expand their business in the formal economy and green businesses. According to the World Bank report in 2020, Iraq is ranked 172 out of 190 countries for “ease of doing business”[2](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark1). This relates in particular to the financial and time-related costs of setting up businesses, which the report estimated take 26.5 days on average and cost about 14.6% of income per capita.

Another factor that halts private sector development is access to credit, where Iraq is ranked 186 out of 190 countries in the world. ILO research on financial inclusion from 2019 highlights several challenges to accessing credit and formal financing services[3.](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark2) The banking sector in Iraq is considered relatively small with limited capacity, leading to strong competition from informal financial service providers. The previous illiquidity of banks has also resulted in low levels of trust among the population in the banking sector, while private-sector banks consider many SMEs to be very high risk, thus reducing the likelihood of lending to what effectively represents most enterprises in Iraq. A survey conducted in 2020 by UNDP on MSMEs, covering Baghdad, Basra and Nineveh (where 20% of the nation’s MSMEs are located) found that only 1 percent of micro-enterprises held bank accounts, rising to 2.6 percent among small enterprises and 16 percent among medium enterprises, while 30 percent of enterprises had attempted but failed to obtain financing, and 55 percent showed reluctance to borrow[4.](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark3) To support SME’s access to finance, the Central Bank of Iraq initiated a “One Trillion Iraqi Dinars Initiative[5](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark4)” in 2014, but uptake was identified as low, partly related to the difficulty of finding bankable projects but also due to the lack of guarantee required by the banks from the MSMEs.

Lack of business management skills and financial literacy, coupled with lack of access to credit and loan services, makes it even more complex for entrepreneurs and enterprises to startup businesses in Iraq. Furthermore, Iraq's private sector is characterized by high rates of informality and a decent work deficit.

Iraq is characterized by a “demographic window of opportunity” with a very large young population and a working-age population growing at a higher rate than the overall population, but is currently unable to catalyse on this opportunity, as job creation is not keeping up with the growing size of the workforce[6.](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark5) The situation is considered a “jobs crisis of unprecedented proportions”[7](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark6)

Despite all the above-mentioned challenges, the sector has enormous potential for growth and job creation if there is an enabling business environment for MSMEs. The ILO, having the expertise and experience globally, in the region and in Iraq, namely: building on its well-established business and financial management tools, and its previous agreement with the Central Bank of Iraq, aspires to

1 UNESCO (2019), *Assessment of the Labour Market & Skills Analysis Iraq and Kurdistan Region-Iraq - Informal Sector, available here*

2 World Bank (2020), *Doing Business Report*, available [here](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/688761571934946384/pdf/Doing-Business-2020-Comparing-Business-Regulation-in-190-Economies.pdf)

3 ILO (2019), *Advancing Livelihoods Through Financial Inclusion in Iraq*, available [here](https://www.ilo.org/beirut/publications/WCMS_777429/lang--en/index.htm)

4 MOP, CSO, UNDP and USAID (2021) *Iraq MSME 2020 Survey*, available [here](https://www.undp.org/iraq/publications/iraq-msme-2020-survey)

5 Iraqi Economists Network, available [here](http://iraqieconomists.net/en/2020/01/28/the-1-trillion-iraqi-dinars-initiative-of-the-iraqi-central-bank/)

6 Rabi, Amjad (2022), *Generation 2050: Turning Iraq’s Demographic ‘Gift’ into an Economic Window of Opportunity*, available [here](https://www.ilo.org/wcmsp5/groups/public/---arabstates/---ro-beirut/documents/publication/wcms_848620.pdf)

7 World Bank (2018), *Jobs in Iraq: A Primer on Job Creation in the Short Term*, available [here,](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/255111529495871846/pdf/Jobs-in-Iraq-a-primer-on-job-creation-in-the-short-term.pdf) p. 1

achieve the following two objectives while creating more and better jobs through this project in two governorates of Southern Iraq, Basra and Muthanna. These are: 1) Improve the business ecosystem for MSMEs in Iraq to grow and thrive through policy options, along with national and subnational dialogue amongst key stakeholders in private sector development; and 2) Capacitate and empower national/subnational financial and non-financial institutions to better support entrepreneurs and MSMEs to unleash their full potential.

The ILO signed the development cooperation agreement with the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, and the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) dated 09 March 2023 to implement the project. The project intends to deliver the following three outcomes while aspiring to attain the aforementioned key objectives:

1. Enhanced business support ecosystem for MSMEs to grow and thrive with a focus on the green economy.
2. Improved business and financial management skills at the meso and micro levels (institutional and individual).
3. Improved financial inclusion of start-up businesses and MSMEs with a focus on the green economy.

The logical framework and Theory of Change (ToC), which depict the underlying results chain, indicators, targets, sources of verification, and assumptions regarding each project objective, can be found in **Annex 1**.

This project is designed to contribute towards the achievement of several objectives of the current Decent Work Country Programme (DWCP) for Iraq (2019-2023). In particular, it contributes to the achievement of Outcome 4, which is creating more and better employment opportunities, ensuring that private sector development supports the much-needed creation of new jobs.

Moreover, it also contributes to the accomplishment of some important objectives of the ILO Programme & Budget (P&B) 2022-2023, which set out the strategic objectives and expected outcomes for the organization’s work, Outcome 4: Sustainable enterprises as generators of employment and promoters of innovation and decent work. The project's implementation is also expected to contribute to achieving the Country Programme Outcomes (CPO) IRQ 126 and IRQ 127.

Most importantly, the project contributes to the attainment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) under the UNSDCF (2020-2024) for Iraq under strategic priority 2: Growing the Economy for All, especially in what concerns the promotion of inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment, and decent work for all (SDG 8), target 8.5 “achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value”.

All proposed activities have been looked into through a gender and disability inclusion perspective and reinforce equal consideration of women and Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) while implementing the activities.

**Project management set-up and implementation arrangement**: The governance structure of the project is led by a project Steering Committee comprised of concerned Ministries from the Government of Iraq (MoLSA, CBI, MoT, MoP), Social Partners (Workers’ and Employers’ organizations), Chamber of Commerce, IFI, MFI, and Trade Unions, which was established in the early implementation phase of the project. The Steering Committee has been overseeing implementation, facilitating

coordination and communication with policymakers, central and local authorities, other service providers and donors. The Steering Committee held one annual meeting to review project progress and capture lessons learned.

At the local government level, the Directorate of Labour and Social Affairs, Directorate of Youth and Sport and Directorate of Environment are the main counterparts of the project. The ILO has also been extensively engaging with Business Development Service (BDS) providers, TVET centres, development partners and civil society organisations) to strengthen collaboration in delivering services through the centre.

The project is implemented under the overall guidance and supervision of the ILO Country Coordinator based in Baghdad, with the project team based in Baghdad and Basra that includes the Project Manager and National Senior Project Officer who are responsible for overall planning, technical guidance, activity implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting of the project in close collaboration with local implementing partners.

Operational Support Unit (OSU) stationed in Erbil and Baghdad provides administrative and financial services to the project team. The Enterprise Development and Employment Specialists of the ILO Beirut DWT backstop the project. Programme Support Unit at the Regional Office for Arab States (ROAS) – Beirut provides administrative support to the project. ENTRPRISE and SECTOR departments at Headquarters provide technical support to the project.

Short-term International/National experts services were also provided for preparing technical support, guidelines, training materials, supervision and other required assignments.

1. ## Purpose, objectives, and scope of the evaluation

ILO considers evaluation as an integral part of the implementation of development cooperation projects. Therefore, the evaluation will be planned and implemented in accordance with the ILO Evaluation Policy [8](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark7) and the ILO Results-Based Evaluation Strategy[9](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark8) using the ILO policy guidelines for evaluation: Principles, rationale, planning and managing for evaluations. The evaluation will comply with the evaluation criteria established by the OECD / DAC Quality Standards for Development Evaluation and the UNEG Code of Conduct for Evaluation in the UN System.

The final evaluation will examine the relevance and coherence while identifying strengths and weaknesses in the project design, strategy, and implementation mechanisms, as well as lessons learned from implementation. The evaluation is expected to review the effectiveness, efficiency and timeliness of project implementation; analyze effectiveness of implementation and partnership arrangements; identify lessons learned about project design, implementation and management for future projects; and highlight technical achievements. Finally, the project’s final evaluation will assess the ILO contribution towards potential impact, analyze sustainability of results and assess whether the project has achieved the intended results and the development objectives.

Specifically, the independent endline evaluation should consider the **OECD DAC Criteria** below:

- **Relevance: Alignment with the country, constituents’, and beneficiaries’ needs, changes in context and review of assumptions:** Is the project’s design adequate to address the problems at hand? Were the project objectives and outcomes relevant in relation to the context on the ground?

8 [Evaluation policy | International Labour Organization](https://www.ilo.org/about-ilo/how-ilo-works/accountability-and-transparency/evaluation-office/evaluation-policy)

9 [ILO results-based evaluation strategy 2023-25 | International Labour Organization](https://www.ilo.org/publications/ilo-results-based-evaluation-strategy-2023-25)

- **Coherence:** The extent to which the project strategy is compatible with other projects in the country, whether implemented by the ILO or other stakeholders, especially within the green economy sector? How far are the project’s objectives aligned with the ILO’s Programme & Budget?
- **Effectiveness: Results in terms of outcomes and outputs achieved:** How has the project contributed towards the project’s outcomes and development objectives? To what extent did it contribute to the ILO’s Programme & Budget, Country Programme Outcomes, and more broadly the SDGs?
- **Efficiency: Use of resources in achievement of projected performance:** How have the resources been used to fulfil the project performance efficiently with respect to cost, time and staff?
- **Assessment of potential impact:** To what extent has the project contributed to long-term intended and unintended impact?
- **Sustainability:** Will the project’s effects remain over time? What can be done to replicate or scale up results achieved in the targeted and other governorates of Iraq?

The final evaluation will comply with ILO policy guidelines for results-based evaluation[10,](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark9) and the UNEG ethical guidelines[11](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark10) will be followed.

The final evaluation will cover the implementation period since the start of the project, which is from 9 March 2023 up until the end of the project on January 31st, 2027. The evaluation will examine achievements of the project outcomes and outputs to date. As cross-cutting themes, the evaluation will also take specific note of the integration of gender mainstreaming[12,](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark11) disability inclusion, International Labour Standards, social dialogue[13,](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark12) and environmental sustainability, as well as contribution to SDGs[14.](https://reliefweb.int/#_bookmark13)

The evaluation will also provide due attention to how the project is relevant to the ILO’s programme and policy frameworks, UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework and other relevant national development frameworks.

**The primary clients of this evaluation** are Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs, the Ministry of Trade, Ministry of Planning Central bank of Iraq, Basra and Muthana local Governorates and the Directorate of Labor and Social Affairs in Basra and Muthana Governorates – Directorates of youth and sport and Vocational Training Centre in Basra and Muthana Governorates, branches of Worker’s and Employer’s representative organizations in Basra and Muthana, Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, ILO DWT-Beirut, ILO ROAS, ILO-Iraq. jobs.description:
**PRÉSENTATION ALIMA**

**L’ESPRIT ALIMA :** La raison d’être d’ALIMA est de sauver des vies et de soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, sans aucune discrimination identitaire, religieuse ou politique, à travers des actions basées surla proximité, l’innovation et l’alliance d’organisations et d’individus. Nous agissons avec humanisme, impartialité et dans le respect de l’éthique médicale universelle. Pour accéder aux patients et aux patientes, nous nous engageons à intervenir de façon neutre et indépendante.

**LES VALEURS et PRINCIPES de notre action, inscrits au sein de notre CHARTE :**

- Le patient et la patiente d’abord
- Révolutionner la médecine humanitaire
- Responsabilité et liberté
- Améliorer la qualité de nos actions
- Faire confiance
- L’intelligence collective
- La responsabilité environnementale

ALIMA promeut et défend les principes des droits humains fondamentaux. ALIMA a une approche de tolérance zéro envers les personnes coupables d’actes de violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi qu’envers l’inaction face à des faits de violence supposés ou avérés. La protection des personnes bénéficiant et impactées par notre intervention est notre priorité absolue dans tout ce que nous faisons. Toute personne collaborant avec ALIMA s’engage à :

- Respecter la charte, le code de conduite, les politiques institutionnelles incluant la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la politique de prévention de la corruption et de la fraude ;
- Signaler toute violation aux politiques, documents cadre et procédure à une supérieure, un supérieur, une référente, un référent.

**SOIGNER - INNOVER - ENSEMBLE :** Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA a touché plus de 18 millions de bénéficiaires dans 15 pays, principalement en Afrique. En 2024, nous avons développé 59 projets de réponse médicale humanitaire pour répondre aux besoins de populations touchées par les conflits, les épidémies et l’extrême pauvreté. L’ensemble de ces projets se font en appui aux autorités sanitaires nationales à travers les structures de santé (dont hôpitaux et centres de santé). Notre action découle d’une adaptation constante aux réalités du terrain et aux progrès de la médecine. En 2024, ALIMA a atteint 5,9 millions de bénéficiaires. Nous travaillons en partenariat, notamment avec des ONGs locales, dès que cela est possible afin de nous assurer que nos patients et patientes bénéficient de l’expertise là où elle se trouve, que ce soit au niveau de leur pays ou du reste du monde. Par ailleurs, pour améliorer la réponse humanitaire, nous menons des projets de recherches opérationnelles et cliniques notamment dans le domaine de la lutte contre la malnutrition et les fièvres virales hémorragiques.

**L'ÉQUIPE ALIMA :** plus de 2000 personnes œuvrent actuellement pour ALIMA. Les équipes terrain, au plus proche des patients, reçoivent leur support des équipes de coordination généralement basées en capitale des pays d’intervention. Celles-ci reçoivent le support des 4 équipes desk et de l’équipe du service urgences et ouvertures basées au siège opérationnel de Dakar, Sénégal. Les équipes de Paris et New-York travaillent activement à la collecte de fonds ainsi qu’à la représentation d’ALIMA. Le reste de la Galaxie ALIMA comprend des individus et des équipes partenaires qui travaillent pour le compte d’autres organisations telles que les ONGs médicales BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP, les organismes de recherche PACCI, INSERM, INRB, les Universités de Bordeaux ou de Copenhague, l’ONG Solidarités International et bien d’autres.

**NOS THÉMATIQUES PROJET :** Malnutrition, Santé sexuelle et reproductive incluant les violences basées sur le genre, Santé Primaire et secondaire, la chirurgie, les soins pédiatriques, les maladies tueuses tel que Paludisme, IRA, Diarrhée, Épidémies (Fièvres hémorragiques, méningite, Choléra, Rougeole, Dengue, Covid-19).

**NOS PAYS D’INTERVENTIONS :** Mali, Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, Ethiopie, Haïti, Nigeria, Niger, Tchad, République Démocratique du Congo, Cameroun, Guinée, Soudan du Sud, Sénégal, Mauritanie et Soudan.

**ALIMA EN RCA :**

Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA mène des interventions humanitaires centrées sur la santé. Présente en République centrafricaine (RCA) depuis 2013, l’organisation y développe des activités axées sur la prise en charge médico-nutritionnelle des enfants, la santé reproductive, les soins de santé primaires et secondaires, la réponse aux épidémies ainsi que la recherche opérationnelle.

Forte de ses 15 années d’expérience en action médicale humanitaire, y compris en RCA, l’organisation s’appuie à la fois sur l’expertise de professionnels internationaux et sur celle du personnel local afin de répondre efficacement aux besoins des populations.

ALIMA dispose également d’une solide expérience dans le renforcement de l’offre de soins en RCA, tant au niveau primaire que secondaire.

La RCA compte près de 6 millions d’habitants répartis dans 35 districts sanitaires et plus de 1 000 formations sanitaires. ALIMA y apporte son soutien aux populations affectées par les conflits armés, les catastrophes naturelles et les épidémies. L’organisation intervient dans les domaines de la santé et de la nutrition dans des zones touchées par des crises humanitaires et sécuritaires, ayant des conséquences importantes sur l’état nutritionnel et l’accès aux soins des populations vulnérables.

À ce jour, ALIMA est présente dans six districts sanitaires (Haut-Mbomou, Berberati, Carnot, Gamboula Batangafo-Kabo et Bouca) et appuie plus de 20 formations sanitaires ainsi que deux hôpitaux (Hôpital secondaire de Zémio et l'hôpital du district de Bouca).

**LIEU DU POSTE**

Bangui - République Centrafricaine

avec des déplacements fréquents sur les différents projets de la mission.

**PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ**

**Niveau 3 :** Le ou la titulaire du poste pourra être amené·e à faire des visites terrain. Il·Elle pourra donc être en contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

**LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES**

Il·Elle rend compte au Chef de mission (responsable hiérarchique), et Référent Financier du Desk ( responsable technique) basé à Dakar.

Il·Elle encadre des administrateurs, administratrices, superviseur·e·s et assistant·e·s administrateurs de coordination et de terrain, responsables comptables, archivistes.

Il·Elle travaille en étroite collaboration avec les coordinateurs et coordinatrices (médical, logistique , ressources humaines et projets).

**MISSION ET ACTIVITES PRINCIPALES**

Le ou La Coordinateur·trice Financier·e (COFIN) appuie les coordinations de capitale et de projet sur tous les sujets touchant à la gestion financière et administrative de l’ensemble des projets qui constituent la mission pays. Il.Elle garantit la bonne gestion des fonds et leur transparence en assurant la gestion comptable et financière de la mission dans le respect du cadre de gestion ALIMA et de la législation locale.

**Gestion budgétaire**

- Contribuer à la définition de la stratégie de la mission en élaborant les budgets et les amendements budgétaire de la mission
- Consolider et réaliser des budgets, en collaboration avec les Coordinateurs et Coordinatrices (mensuels généraux et spécifiques)
- Elaborer les suivis budgétaires destinés au siège et les membres de la coordination pays et projets,
- Maîtriser et analyser les suivis budgétaires en vue les présenter aux équipes et au siège , afin d’attirer leur attention sur les possibles sous consommations et sur consommations budgétaires,
- Produire les rapports financiers à destination des bailleurs de fonds afin qu’ils soient validés par le siège dans les délais impartis dans les conventions de financement.

**Comptabilité**

- Avoir une connaissance parfaite en matière de comptabilité
- Garantir l’existence et le respect des règles de gestion des ressources financières et comptables dans le pays
- Encadrer et superviser le système de comptabilité assurant la transparence, la complétude des informations financières, le respect des procédures et la lisibilité des dépenses.
- S’assurer de la conformité des pièces comptables et des imputations (codes projets, comptables et codes budgétaires) et faire des retours réguliers au responsable comptable de la mission.
- Assurer l’archivage des pièces comptables de la mission

**Gestion de la trésorerie**

- Assurer en permanence un niveau de trésorerie nécessaire et suffisant au bon déroulement des opérations avec une maîtrise maximale des risques sécuritaires et opérationnels
- Assurer le respect des procédures de gestion des espèces sur sa mission
- En fonction de l’évolution du contexte, définir et mettre à jour le guide de gestion et sécurisation de trésorerie

**Gestion générale des moyens**

- Mettre en place les éléments nécessaires au suivi de l’utilisation des ressources matérielles
- Participer à l’élaboration du cadre d’approvisionnement de la mission (plan d’approvisionnement)
- Validation financière des engagements de dépenses et conformité des pièces comptables.

**Financements institutionnels**

- S’assurer le respect des engagements pris auprès des bailleurs institutionnels (rencontres régulières, suivi financier mensuel, rapports, recommandations, etc.)
- Respect des procédures Bailleurs

**Audits**

- En collaboration du service d’audit interne, Piloter les audits réalisés sur la mission
- Mise en œuvre et application des recommandations de l’audit interne et externe
- Être le point focal des audits de nos bailleurs de fonds au niveau mission en lien avec le département d’audit interne d’Alima. Préparer la documentation, contrôler son contenu et alerter en cas de besoin.

**Encadrement et animation d’équipe**

- Mettre en place un département finance à la coordination dans un esprit et un fonctionnement garantissant les synergies entre services.
- Impulser des échanges de bonnes pratiques intra et inter départements.
- Définir les profils de poste et les plans d’objectifs de performance des membres de son équipe dans un objectif de développement des compétences. Participer aux bilans de son équipe dans une approche de parcours professionnel.
- Rendre possible des formations et changement de poste en renforçant leurs compétences et développant leur autonomie
- Proposer et anticiper des détachements vers d’autres missions ALIMA
- Identifier les compétences que les membres de son équipe doivent acquérir pour maîtriser leurs postes et organiser des formations pour les renforcer OU S’assurer de l’adéquation des besoins de l’organisation avec les savoir-faire et les motivations de ses collaborateurs
- Incarne et transmet les valeurs, veille au respect du code de conduite et des politiques institutionnelles, de l’état d’esprit et des comportements individuels et collectifs attendus
- Organiser et animer des réunions d’équipe

**Mise en œuvre des mesures de prévention contre les abus de pouvoir, les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la fraude et le Blanchiment d’argent**

- Participer aux formations et aux séances de sensibilisation
- Assurer en continue la formation et la sensibilisation de tous les staffs sur la politique anti-fraude
- Appliquer les standards relatifs à la prévention des abus
- Assurer que les membres de son équipe suivent les formations et les séances de sensibilisation et appliquent les règles de prévention des abus
- Contribuer à créer et maintenir un environnement épanouissant et protecteur

**EXPERIENCES ET COMPETENCES**

**Expériences**

- Bac + 5 en Gestion, Finance, Comptabilité, école de commerce ou équivalent
- Expérience prouvée en gestion, finance, comptabilité (minimum 5 ans- dont au moins 2 ans sur le terrain en tant qu’administrateur sur un projet ou en Coordination au sein d’une ONG Humanitaire Internationale)
- Connaissance des bailleurs humanitaires
- Maîtrise de l’informatique, dont impérativement un niveau avancé d’Excel et GSuite

**Qualités du candidat**

- Rigueur professionnelle
- Discrétion
- Calme, excellente gestion du stress et sang-froid
- Très bonnes capacités de communication et d’écoute
- Expérience en gestion d’équipe et supervision
- Capacité d’adaptation
- Excellente capacité de compréhension
- Compétences en formation et accompagnement

**Langues**

- Maîtrise du français (oral et écrit) indispensable
- La maîtrise de l’anglais est un atout

**CONDITIONS**

**Durée et type de contrat :** CDD de droit français de 12 mois avec possibilité de prolongation

**Prise de poste :** janvier 2027
