jobs.title: GORS Program Lead - DRC
jobs.description:
**Location:** Kisangani, Tshopo Province, Democratic Republic of Congo

**Position Type**: Consultancy (40 hours per week)

**Length of contract**: 3 months, Renewable subject to satisfactory performance and availability of funding.

**Compensation:** Rates competitive for DRC

**Background**

Global Emergency Group, Inc. (GEG) leads the Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS) program in support of the U.S. Department of State. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), GORS requires effective country leadership to translate agreed program objectives into coordinated implementation in Tshopo Province, including support to provincial health authorities and implementing partners and the activation of Rapid Response Teams when required.

The position brings together program management and oversight of the support services needed for delivery. It ensures that technical activities are feasible, appropriately resourced and implemented efficiently, with clear accountability for results, expenditure, personnel and operational risk. It maintains programmatic and operational coordination with the Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC), while preserving each program’s separate mandate, management, and contractual accountability.

**Requirements Overview, reporting line and working relationships**

Lead the coordinated, cost-efficient implementation of GORS in the DRC, delivering agreed results to the required quality and within approved budgets and timeframes. Align technical delivery with finance, human resources, logistics, supply chain and security support, and maintain effective relationships with government counterparts, implementing partners, DART representatives and the GORS HQ team.

The post holder reports directly to the GORS Program Director, based in Washington, DC. The Program Director sets objectives, agrees priorities and delegated authority, reviews performance and resolves matters requiring program-level approval. The position has one direct management reporting line.

The post holder works closely with the following senior colleagues, whose specialist responsibilities remain in place:

- Senior Technical Director: technical priorities, quality standards, technical supervision and validation of program results.
- Senior Safety and Security Lead: security policy, specialist risk advice, incident escalation and decisions reserved to the security management framework.
- Director of Field Operations and Security: country operational and security backstopping, preparedness and incident-response coordination.
- Senior Operations Lead: operational systems, finance and administrative support, HR processes, compliance and escalation of support-service constraints.
- Senior Logistics Lead: logistics and supply chain strategy, planning; procurement, assets and fleet standards, and technical backstopping.

The post holder coordinates agreed program priorities and day-to-day delivery and provides documented performance feedback to the designated manager. Technical personnel retain functional guidance from the relevant technical leads; security personnel retain specialist direction through the approved security reporting arrangements.

**Scope of Work**

**Position Description**

1. **Program leadership and implementation**

- Translate approved GORS objectives into a consolidated provincial implementation plan with defined activities, geographic coverage, deliverables, staffing, resource requirements and milestones.
- Lead routine implementation reviews with technical and support teams. Align priorities and resolve scheduling, resource and delivery constraints before they affect agreed results.
- Monitor progress, quality, expenditure and delivery risks. Identify underperformance or changing needs and propose corrective actions, reprioritization or resource adjustments to the Program Director.
- Ensure that problem-solving support to selected Health Areas has an agreed purpose, defined activities, counterpart responsibilities and measurable completion criteria.
- Promote proportionate staffing and support arrangements, compare operational options and avoid unnecessary costs or duplication while maintaining delivery quality and duty-of-care requirements.

**2. Representation and stakeholder coordination**

- Serve as the official GORS focal point for the Government of the DRC (GDRC) and implementing partners within delegated authority. Maintain effective engagement with the provincial government health office and relevant national, provincial and local counterparts.
- Coordinate and document agreements on geographic areas of operation, including Health Areas receiving problem-solving support and locations considered for Rapid Response activation. Obtain required internal approvals before committing resources or changing approved scope.
- Serve as the designated GORS Program focal point for US Dept of State DART, when required. Maintain regular communication, facilitate field engagement and consolidate requests and follow-up actions in coordination with the Program Director.
- Represent GORS in relevant coordination forums, communicate agreed program positions and maintain a stakeholder contact and action record. Refer contractual, policy or resource commitments beyond delegation to the Program Director.
- Maintain a constructive support relationship with authorities and implementing partners. Distinguish GORS support commitments from decisions and responsibilities that remain with the competent public authorities or partner organizations.

**3. Rapid Response planning and activation**

- Liaise with the provincial government health office and relevant partners to identify when and where GORS Rapid Response support is needed, informed by technical assessment and operational feasibility.
- Develop a documented activation proposal specifying the response objective, location, scope, timeframe, activities, success metrics, costs, counterpart arrangements and transition or closure criteria.
- Obtain technical validation and the required program, budget and security approvals before activation. Confirm transport, accommodation, equipment, communications and referral arrangements with the responsible leads.
- Coordinate deployment and implementation, ensuring that the Response Coordinator has clear objectives, reporting requirements and support arrangements. Review progress and escalate requests for changes to scope, duration or resources.
- Coordinate response closure, handover and after-action review. Consolidate results, expenditure and lessons to inform subsequent activations.

**4. Project data and donor reporting**

- Coordinate provincial project data collection and consolidate timely, accurate inputs to support the preparation of donor-facing reports, working with technical leads, MEL personnel, and other relevant staff.
- Monitor the country team’s contribution to donor reporting obligations through an agreed reporting calendar. Assign input owners and internal deadlines and follow up missing or delayed contributions.
- Review country inputs for completeness, consistency and supporting evidence. Seek technical and financial validation from the responsible specialists and resolve discrepancies before forwarding reporting packages.
- Prepare draft donor reports, responses to data calls, briefing notes and implementation updates for HQ review. Clearly explain achievements, constraints, expenditure variances, risks and proposed corrective actions.
- Provide HQ with cleared country inputs by agreed internal deadlines and track feedback and revisions. Final donor-report approval and formal submission remain with the HQ team unless explicitly delegated in writing.

**5. Finance budget and cost control**

- Maintain oversight of the GORS program budget with the finance team. Review expenditure, commitments, cash requirements and forecasts against the implementation plan and approved funding.
- Analyze significant variances and the cost implications of changes to activities or deployment plans. Recommend adjustments early and obtain approval for reallocations or expenditure beyond delegated limits.
- Ensure that requests and expenditure have a documented program purpose, correct budget allocation and complete supporting records. Maintain separation between requesting, verifying receipt, approving expenditure, and executing payment.
- Oversee timely preparation of cash forecasts, advances, expense reconciliations and invoice packages. Follow up outstanding documentation and unresolved provider or payment issues with the relevant finance and operations colleagues.
- Review the value and performance of support arrangements with operations and logistics leads. Document cost-efficiency opportunities and apply approved cost-allocation arrangements where services are coordinated with another program (HASC).

**6. Logistics and daily operational support**

- Oversee daily operating readiness, including functional office space, utilities, staff accommodation where required, communications, equipment, transport and movement arrangements.
- Coordinate, supply chain, procurement and logistics planning with the Logistics Coordinator and Senior Logistics Lead so that technical and field requirements enter a consolidated, prioritized supply and service plan.
- Oversee vehicle and driver availability, rental-service performance, movement schedules and supporting records. Ensure that service requests, logbooks and invoices managed by the Fleet Officer are consistent with approved activities and contract terms.
- Oversee effective inventory, asset custody, maintenance and handover arrangements. Review service-provider performance and require corrective action through the appropriate procurement and contract-management channels.
- Anticipate operational bottlenecks and arrange timely support with the Senior Logistics Lead and the Director of field Ops and Security DFOS. Ensure that qualified corporate advisers, including accounting or legal support where required, address issues within their remit.

**7. Safety, security and operational risk**

- Act as the program focal point for operational risk mitigation. Maintain a consolidated risk register covering delivery, financial, HR, logistics, security and relevant health-related operational risks, with mitigation measures, owners and escalation triggers.
- Ensure that approved security plans, briefings, movement procedures, communications and tracking arrangements are applied to GORS activities, with specialist support from the Senior Safety and Security Lead, DFOS and Safety and Security Coordinator.
- Integrate security, access and emergency-response requirements into activity planning, accommodation, procurement and deployment decisions. Ensure that personnel receive required security and relevant health or IPC briefings before deployment.
- Immediately escalate incidents and significant concerns through the established notification chain. Coordinate program support to the designated incident-management lead and follow up agreed corrective actions.
- Take immediate protective action when necessary, including pausing an activity where essential controls are absent, and promptly escalate. Obtain specialist review and the required authorization before resumption; residual-risk acceptance and security approvals remain with the designated authorities.

**8. People management and team development**

- Maintain a staffing and deployment plan linked to approved activities and budgets. Define duties, duty stations, competencies, supervision arrangements and recruitment priorities with the relevant technical and support leads.
- Work with HR and recruitment colleagues to finalize position descriptions, contribute to shortlisting and interviews when required, and provide documented selection recommendations. Hiring approvals, contractual terms and contract signatures follow the authorized HR process.
- Ensure that incoming personnel DRC-based staff complete onboarding and induction and receive clear objectives, reporting lines, initial workplans and the tools needed to perform their roles.
- Set and follow up objectives for direct reports. Coordinate country work schedules, attendance, leave, travel, workload and handovers within delegation and with the designated technical line managers.
- Provide regular coaching and documented feedback. Contribute evidence and recommendations to DRC-based staff evaluations led by HQ, including probation, development needs and contract-renewal reviews, according to the agreed HR process.
- Promote respectful conduct, staff wellbeing and timely compliance with administrative requirements. Refer grievances, safeguarding concerns or disciplinary matters through the appropriate confidential HR channels.

**9. Coordination with HASC Program**

- Maintain regular programmatic and operational liaison with HASC teams in country to understand respective activities, geographic coverage, field presence and deployment plans.
- Identify complementary support and practical coordination opportunities that reduce duplication, improve situational awareness or make transport, accommodation, communications and other services more efficient. Submit proposed arrangements through the relevant program and functional authorities.
- Document approved coordination and any service-sharing arrangements, including responsibilities, access to information and cost allocation. Preserve separate program workplans, budgets, donor reporting, management authority and contractual accountability.

**Required Position Qualifications**

- Advanced degree or equivalent senior experience in international development, humanitarian response, program management or a related field.
- At least 15 years of progressively responsible program leadership in complex environment.
- Demonstrated management of multidisciplinary teams, substantial budgets and high-risk international operations.
- Strong experience in emergency-response governance, risk and compliance management.
- Proven ability to make timely, documented decisions under uncertainty and maintain constructive senior relationships.
- Fluent professional English and French.
- DRC nationality

**Competencies/Performance Criteria**

Adherence and promotion of the GEG Way.

**Travel Frequency and working arrangements**

The position is based in Kisangani and requires a sustained in-country presence, with regular field travel within Tshopo Province and other approved travel in the DRC as operationally required. Deployments are subject to the applicable security and movement-clearance arrangements. The post holder complies with GEG conduct, PSEA policies, security, health and administrative policies and maintains reliable communication with the HQ team. Working arrangements and availability during response activations will be agreed with the Program Director in accordance with the contract.

**About Global Emergency Group**

Founded in 2007, GEG is a benefit corporation that supports vulnerable people affected by crisis in more than 52 countries by providing a broad range of humanitarian support services to a wide range of organizations, including the United Nations, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, donor governments, companies, major international and national NGO’s and local communities. Every day, these organizations and communities rely on GEG’s emergency response expertise, and on the combined capabilities and dedication of its people to implement strategies, find solutions and seize opportunities to assist the world’s most vulnerable people.

Global Emergency Group is committed to being an equal opportunity employer and recruiting people of diverse backgrounds and experiences. GEG does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion or belief, color, gender, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, age, medical condition, disability, ancestry, national origin or ethnic group. All recruitment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

jobs.title: Global Donor Engagement Officer
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

We’re striving to build an organization that is a supportive, kind and inspiring place to work. We encourage bold leadership, innovation, creative partnerships and accountability to those we serve.

The Awards Management Unit (AMU) is a global unit with teams in New York, Washington DC, London, Nairobi, Berlin, Stockholm and Amman with staff presence in many other locations around the world. Its purpose is to lead IRC’s work to engage and influence government donors, secure funding, and enable compliant and effective program delivery for our clients. The AMU sits within IRC’s Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) department, alongside IRC’s international country programs, emergencies unit and technical teams.

This role sits in AMU's **Global Business Development (BD) Team**, which leads IRC's public business development strategy and engagement for the organization’s international work, and helps align resources across the organization to strengthen donor engagement and drive BD to secure funding.

**The Purpose of the Role**

The Global Donor Engagement Officer will report to the Donor Engagement Director, and work closely with Donor Engagement Advisors, Regional Heads of Business Development, and wider AMU, CRRD and Policy & Advocacy colleagues.

The Officer will provide flexible support across multiple donors to help IRC deliver its public BD Strategy. Specifically, the role will coordinate support for donor engagement, relationship building, and influence with the US Department of State (DoS) and other relevant US government agencies, with Green Climate Fund (GCF), Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) and other institutional donors as assigned. The Officer will draw on these relationships and networks to build a portfolio of tools, information and assets that enable IRC to engage donors proactively, influence their strategies, and pursue priority funding streams.

The Officer will serve as a key donor engagement support resource in Washington, coordinating with internal and external Washington-based counterparts.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Strategy**

- Provide support to the Donor Engagement Director in development of relevant donor strategies (which may include research, coordination and some writing) for key donors in the portfolio **(USG, GCF, and emerging MDBs)**.
- Coordinate action plans related to strategy implementation, report-on progress, lessons-learned, and how risks are being managed and mitigated.

**Portfolio Management**

- Support the Donor Engagement Director with the departmental co-leadership of the **Green Climate Fund**, working together with the Climate Global Practice team. Support efforts to drive and track GCF accreditation, pipeline development, strategy development, and donor coordination in partnership with relevant teams.
- Convene and manage info and intelligence on IRC's engagement with **US DoS** (and other USG agencies as relevant) and **MDBs**, coordinating that engagement where relevant.
- Build and coordinate a network of contacts within relevant donor teams to enable effective outreach and engagement.
- Represent the IRC at external meetings, events, and forums as appropriate.

**Coordination, Research and Knowledge Management**

- Map donor organizational structures and identify key contacts to help IRC achieve its strategic aims.
- Use Salesforce to plan, track, and maintain a register of donor engagement at country, regional, and global levels; triangulate information across levels so staff are well briefed and consistent in their donor engagement and influence.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of assigned donors' strategies relevant to IRC's work, such as funding priorities, geographic interests, and political climate.
- Analyze and summarize press releases, policies, and other announcements, and share them internally.
- Research, track, and update data and analysis on strategy, funding trends, and peer activity for US DoS, GCF, and MDBs.
- Develop materials (strategy summaries, donor profiles, primers on donor funding, talking points, etc.) that equip colleagues engaging with assigned donors to demonstrate alignment between IRC and donor technical priorities.
- Support the Donor Engagement Director in developing, maintaining, and improving donor tracking tools and resources
- Serve as the focal point enabling IRC visitors to DC (including Regional and Technical Leadership, Country Directors, Regional VPs, and the President/CEO) to engage with relevant donors, working in partnership with CRRD (International) and Policy & Advocacy, with the Donor Engagement Director, and relevant Donor Advisors, including the World Bank Donor Engagement Advisor.

**Skills, Knowledge and Qualifications:**

We are seeking a candidate with diversity of experience (i.e., paid and volunteer work; lived experiences; transferable skills from another industry etc.)

**Job Requirements:**

- 3-6 years relevant experience in humanitarian and international development, business development, donor relations, policy or advocacy or a combination of these.
- Experience working with humanitarian and development donors and including experience with US Government, GCF, World Bank or other Multilateral Development Banks.
- Strong collaboration approaches, in a large organizational setting.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presentations, and development of effective briefing material.
- Ability to work well under pressure in a fast-paced and changing environment with multiple stakeholders.
- Good analytical skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Experience undertaking reviews of policies and reports, producing associated written and verbal guidance to relevant staff.
- Excellent interpersonal skills. Ability to collaborate with others and work as part of a team.

**Preferred experience & skills:**

- Technical knowledge of IRC thematic work, particularly climate related work.
- Experience of having worked with new and innovative financing models in humanitarian and international development.

Candidates must have the right to work within the country they are applying. IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

**Compensation:** ($68,000 - $82,023.30 annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Sterile Processing Project Manager
jobs.description:
**Who We Are**
Mercy Ships is a global faith-based charity that uses hospital ships to bring life-changing surgeries and transformational medical training to people in some of the most challenging contexts along the African coast. For over 40 years, Mercy Ships has been delivering lasting hope and healing through safe surgical care, while working alongside partners and stakeholders to strengthen local healthcare systems in more than 55 countries. Since the inception of this dream by founders Don and Deyon Stephens in 1978, Mercy Ships has served more than 2.7 million direct beneficiaries without regard for race, gender, or religion.

Do you have a heart for the hurting and a desire to invest your talents and experiences into a mission with eternal significance? For every transformative surgery that takes place onboard one of our Mercy Ships, there are dozens of men and women being used of the Lord to prepare the way through their vocational gifts and talents!

**This is a full-time position with the initial on-site deployment in Sierra Leone and requires international travel.**

As a Sterile Processing Project Manager, you will work together with the Program Director and the International Programs department, and partner country stakeholders to develop and implement sterile processing programs in the designated partner country to achieve country objectives for development and advancement of the sterile processing workforce and service delivery.

**How You Will Contribute:**

- Requires primary work location in a partner nation.
- Develop, coordinate, and maintain clear lines of communication between Ministry of Health, national hospitals and education institutions, and training participants for sterile processing training and/or mentorship programs.
- Conduct assessment of training needs in collaboration with the Program Director, Regional Director, and Country Director.
- Co-design, develop and deliver appropriate sterile processing training and mentorship programs that address the country goals for sterile processing workforce development.
- Develop relationships with national partners, healthcare agencies and other national or international Non-Government Organizations to enhance program delivery and strategic outcomes.
- Ensure practical coordination, implementation, and monitoring of project activities to meet expected results, together with partners.
- Line manage Mercy Ships Sterile Processing Technicians based in partner nation.
- Provide technical expertise and practical support for equipment selection, donation and commissioning for hospitals in the partner nation.
- Provide technical expertise and practical support for (re)design of sterile processing departments for hospitals in the partner nation.
- Provide technical expertise about consumables that hospitals in the partner nation need to procure for sterile processing activities.
- Participate in the Equipment Donation Review Team (EDRT) as needed.
- Collaborate with the Program Governance and Coordination (PGC) team Program Quality and Impact (PQI) team for the implementation of monitoring and evaluation plans and all necessary project documentation including concept papers, project plans, requests for proposals (RFPs), partnership agreements, and final reports.
- Work together with the MEL Specialist in-country to collect data at pre-agreed intervals, generate reports and deliver regular reflective reviews with implementing partners.
- Document processes related to program delivery to increase the effectiveness of future programs.
- Manage project budget and report spending in Emburse Professional, in a timely manner.
- Prepare internal and final project reports in collaboration with the Program Officer and Program Director in a timely manner, according to project reporting cycles.
- Write and create content for internal and external communication describing sterile processing projects to help share the work of International Programs.
- Support project assessment, development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation in new and existing partner countries, as requested, to expand programmatic activity (surge involves travel).
- Maintains alignment and upholds Mercy Ships Core Values, Code of Conduct, and follows the policies and procedures published on Compass.
Follows the model of Jesus and aligns with our core values by Loving God; Loving and Serving Others; Being a Person of Integrity; and a Person of Excellence in all you say and do.
- Other duties may be assigned that are not included in the information provided in this job description.

**Ideal Candidate:**

- Supportive of Mercy Ships mission and vision and committed to its core values.
- Understand and apply servant leadership, work collaboratively with integrity, and demonstrate accountability.
- Excellent organizational skills and ability to manage complex projects from creation to completion, plan and prioritize multiple deliverables, and coordinate to meet deadlines.
- Ability to adapt skills in challenging work settings.
- Must have excellent written and oral communication skills.
- Must possess cross-cultural awareness and sensitivity.
- Familiarity with medical terminology, anatomy and physiology is required.
- Possess a strong customer service mindset including attitude and approach.
- Must be fluent in English, both written and verbal.
- French language skills - International B1 Level (or equivalent) are strongly desired, B2 level desirable when serving in Francophone countries.
- Full, clean international driving license strongly preferred.

**Education and/or Experience:**

- At least 5 years' experience as a Sterile Processing Technician
- Experience providing sterile processing training in resource-constrained settings
- Experience in managing sterile processing staff
- Experience working with and/or delivering sterile processing training with educational institutions preferred.
- Certification in sterile processing from recognized professional body preferred

jobs.title: Project Manager (Open to Nationals and Expatriates)
jobs.description:
**Position Title : Project Manager**

**Reporting to : Country Director**

**Technical Supervisor : HoP**

**Duty Station : Bamenda (NW), with frequent travel in NWSW of Cameroon**

**Area of Operation : Southwest and Northwest Region, Cameroon**

**Employment Period : 1 year**

**Type of Contract (Expat/National) : Expat or national**

**Salary & Benefits : TBC**

**Introduction**

The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunity for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfilment of the wish to return home.

The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956 and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with about 6,000 staff. Based in Copenhagen (Denmark) and present in 30 countries, the Danish Refugee Council is a non-profitmaking, politically independent, non-governmental and non-denominational relief organization.

Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced. All our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation, honesty and transparency.

**1. Background**

Present in Cameroon since 2017, DRC operates in the three complex humanitarian crisis: the conflict in the **Lake Chad Basin**, the crisis in the **North-West and South-West regions (NWSW)**, and the impact of the presence of hundreds of thousands of Central African Republic (CAR) refugees in the **Eastern façade regions**.

In Cameroon, **DRC**’s interventions are focused on **Emergency Response** and **Durable Solutions** via our expertise in protection, economic recovery and peacebuilding.

In the Northwest region of Cameroon, DRC is leading the FLASH project which is a localized rapid response mechanism (RRM) for multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) and protection in hard-to-reach areas, implemented through two national partners: SHUMAS and COMINSUD. It combines community early warning system, rapid assessments, emergency cash transfers and protection assistance and response coordination, while strengthening local leadership and response capacity. Looking ahead, FLASH will focus on strengthening risk preparedness, extending displacement analysis to the South-West, and developing a joint strategy with local partners to ensure the mechanism’s sustainability beyond DRC’s potential exit. DRC is envisioning to develop a Nexus approach to contribute to reboot the economic recovery and livelihood of displaced and host populations.

**2. Purpose**

Under the direct supervision of the Country Director, the NWSW Project Manager is responsible for the quality implementation of the "Localised RRM" project in the NWSW regions of Cameroon, as well as for the overall monitoring and capacity strengthening of the two (2) National NGO partners of the project; He/she is also responsible for any contractual, control and accountability aspects related to the implementation of the project as well as driving the reflection for a post emergency/Nexus strategy with the partners and external stakeholders. Additionnally, the NWSW Project manager is responsible for the base management of the Bamenda office and supervises a small team.

**3. Duties and Responsibilities**

**PROGRAMMATIC MANAGEMENT:**

- Planning: Prepares, plans and monitors the timely implementation of activities, in close collaboration with the partners, and in a progressive handover perspective.
- Beneficiary Engagement and Accountability: Oversees that accountability, feedback and reporting mechanisms are put in place and that beneficiaries are engaged with all aspects of the project.
- Internal coordination: Ensures good coordination and communication within the NW office and the Country Office of DRC Cameroon.
- External coordination: Ensures excellent coordination and communication with all other humanitarian stakeholders and fora operating in the context of the NWSW region, as well as with local authorities, with emphasis on the effective collaboration and coordination of RRM activities. External coordination is particularly crucial with: ABC and OCHA coordination fora, all humanitarian stakeholders supporting, contributing or completing RRM response, authorities, donors, and RRM in Far North.
- Representation: Represents DRC in external meetings in the NW region with local authorities, other I/NGOs and International Organizations. Ensures good relations with the implementing partners, and with any local, civil, traditional or community authorities for the successful implementation of the project;
- Information management and documentation tracking: She/he is accountable for the proper collection, management and archiving of all related project documentation for the purpose of internal and external audits
- Technical oversight and quality assurance: Together with partner teams and DRC technical departments, develops and rolls out tools for quality implementation of the activities
- Directly manages NWSW project team
- MEAL: as a direct manager and with the support from the MEAL/IM specialist based in Yaoundé, supervises and supports the MEAL/IM specialist for the proper planning, capacity strengthening and implementation of MEAL activities for DRC and its partners.
- Project’s strategy: continuously adapt the project to the context and suggest strategic evolutions, in close concertation with FLASH partners.
- Work together with SHUMAS and COMINSUD on a joint post-crisis positioning and programming in NWSW, in a nexus approach.
- Project’s budget monitoring and development: Plans costs and forecasting and highlights timely unspent/unforeseen cost in close collaboration with the HoP. When requested, supports the development of new budget proposals

**PARTNERSHIP MANAGEMENT:**

- Coordinates continuous assessment of FLASH partners' capacities, development of training plans when necessary, mutual capacity building and training (from DRC to partners, from partners to DRC, from partner to partner) with support from technical staff of the NW Area Office and the Country Office, and strong involvement of FLASH partners.
- She/he is accountable for the involvement and commitment of local DRC partners in the implementation of activities and the achievement of all commitments according to the terms of the signed sub-grant contracts. Oversees partners’ compliance with the rules and regulations of the grant agreement between them and DRC.
- Is responsible to define (collectively with the partners and the CO) and monitor the FLASH project’s handover plan from DRC to SHUMAS and COMINSUD.
- Maintain clear and transparent communication with local partners and carry out regular visits to the field and to the partners' premises to provide technical support for the staff and to ensure the progress and quality of the interventions.
- Contribute to the organizational transformation of DRC Cameroon towards greater localization. Collect lessons learned and best practices as well as case studies (from DRC and/or other partners) that can be used for DRC's continuous learning, for reporting to donors as well as for DRC's communication materials.
- Capitalization: set up and regularly update a toolbox bringing together tools, modules, etc. to strengthen the skills and practices of DRC teams in capacity building of partners for the entire DRC CMR mission.

**HUMANITARIAN ACCESS**

- Produce analysis and evaluations on the humanitarian space and access adapted to the presence of DRC in Cameroon on a regular basis. Keep a register of developments related to access and humanitarian space.
- Build a network with all stakeholders and develop a strategy to improve acceptance and access of DRC in the field.
- Work in close collaboration with both national partners considering the Equitable Partnership for H2R framework.
- Organize joint access mission with national partners and other NGOs to strengthen access where needed.
- Work in collaboration with the Access Hub and program teams to ensure that humanitarian access strategies deliver the purpose while minimizing unforeseen adverse consequences on people in need (do no harm), within DRC risk acceptance.

**GRANT MANAGEMENT:**

- Internal reporting: Sharing quality internal and external reports. Validation and transmission of technical activity reports, narratives and other documents provided by the project to the donors, in compliance with procedures and deadlines.
- Communication and visibility: Contributes to the project's communication and visibility strategy.
- Project Development: Supports the development of a new inclusive approach which can benefit the local and displaced populations with relevant stakeholders, in a nexus/post-crisis spirit.

**SUPPORT SERVICES:**

- FINANCE and LOGISTICS: Monitors the timely procurement plan and quality of goods and services as well as effective fleet management.
- Budget monitoring and development: Plans costs, controls accounting and forecasting and highlights timely unspent/unforeseen cost in close collaboration with the HoSS. When requested, supports the development of new budget proposals
- Focal point for the day-to-day management of the base

**SAFETY**

- Security Management: Maintains a close relationship with the Country Director to develop increased knowledge of the area of intervention and potential threats. Immediately reports any breach of security protocols to the Country Director.
- Participate in relevant access and safety working groups and roundtables for the Northwest/Southwest.

*The responsibilities listed above are not exhaustive and may be readjusted according to operational needs but will remain in line with the overall purpose of the role.*

**4. Required Qualifications (including years of professional experience)**

- At least 5 years of experience in project management (with at least 2 years of experience in RRM-type or other emergency project management)
- At least 3 years of experience engaging with local and national actors (LNAs)
- Experience in cash transfers and protection activities will be considered an asset
- Ability to work long hours under pressure, in a flexible, adaptable and autonomous manner
- Ability to work effectively in extreme circumstances, including stress, high security risks and difficult living conditions (isolated area)
- Willingness to travel multiple consecutive days to the field in remote areas, where there is a large presence of Organised Armed Groups and other military actors
- Proficiency in the office pack (Word, Excel, Power Point, Internet browsing, etc.), Teams and Outlook
- Ability to work with disaster-affected communities in a sensitive and participatory manner
- Possess excellent oral and written communication skills as well as analytical abilities
- Ability to think strategically and connect emergency responses to longer term solutions
- Capacity to mobilize different stakeholders around common objectives
- Excellent inter-personnel communication and diplomatic skills

**Education: (including certificates, permits, etc.)**

University degree (BAC+3 /4) in Social Sciences, Economics, Rural Development, project management or equivalent

**Language:**

- English (Expert)
- Fluency in French will be considered an advantage
- Knowledge of the Local Language (pidgin) will be considered an asset

**Key Players: (Internal and External**)

- NGO partners
- Local authorities and Internation NGOs/Organizations
- Program/Support Team/Technical Unit in CO
- Local communities and beneficiaries

**5.Required Skills & Qualities**

- In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:
- Striving for excellence: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process
- Collaborating: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback
- Taking the lead: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation
- Communicating: You listen and speak effectively and honestly
- Demonstrating integrity: Upholding and promoting the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment
- Ability to work in a multinational and multicultural environment
- Proven analytical and critical thinking skills
- Team-oriented & good sense of humour

**6.General Regulations**

- The employee shall follow DRC instructions on safety, confidentiality and ethical guidelines, including the Code of Conduct and the Humanitarian Accountability Framework
- Employee should not engage in any other paid activity during the DRC contract period without prior authorization
- Employee should not engage in any activity that could harm DRC or the implementation of any project during the DRC contract period
- Employee should not give interviews to the media or publish project-related photos or other material without prior authorization
- Employee shall return all borrowed equipment for the project to DRC after the end of the contract period or upon request

jobs.title: Stagiaire Finance
jobs.description:
**Titre du poste : Stagiaire Finance**

**Supervisé par : Chef des Services Supports**

**Responsable hiérarchique technique : Finance Specialist**

**Supervise : NA**

**Lieu d’affectation : Yaoundé**

**Zone d’intervention : Cameroun**

**Période considérée : 03 mois (renouvelable)**

**Type de contrat (National) : Contrat national (uniquement réservé aux ressortissants Camerounais)**

**Salaire et avantages : Indemnité de stage et assurance santé**

**Introduction**

Le Conseil Danois pour les Réfugiés (DRC) porte assistance aux réfugiés et aux personnes déplacées à travers le monde : nous fournissons une aide d’urgence à ces personnes, nous combattons pour leurs droits et nous renforçons leurs opportunités pour un meilleur futur. Nous travaillons dans des zones affectées par les conflits, ainsi que le long des routes de déplacements, et au sein des pays dans lesquels les réfugiés s’établissent. En coopération avec les communautés locales, nous nous efforçons d’atteindre des solutions responsables et durables. Nous travaillons pour une intégration réussie des communautés vulnérables et, lorsque cela est possible, à la réalisation de leur souhait de retour chez eux.

Le Conseil Danois pour les Réfugiés (DRC en sigle, pour Danish Refugee Council) a été fondé au Danemark en 1956 et est depuis devenu une organisation humanitaire internationale avec plus de 7,000 employés et de 8,000 volontaires. Ayant son siège établi à Copenhague, et présent dans 40 pays, le DRC est une organisation d’aide non gouvernementale, à but non-lucratif, politiquement neutre et indépendante et non-confessionnelle.

Notre vision est une vie avec dignité pour toutes les personnes déplacées dans le monde. Tous nos efforts reposent sur notre boussole morale : l’humanité, le respect, l’indépendance, la neutralité, la participation, l’honnêteté et la transparence.

**1. Contexte**

DRC Cameroun a commencé ses opérations au Cameroun en 2018 en répondant aux besoins humanitaires des réfugiés de la République centrafricaine (RCA) et des Camerounais vulnérables dans la région de l'Adamawa. Actuellement, DRC opère avec un bureau régional à Meiganga et deux bureaux auxiliaires à Djohong (région de l'Adamawa) et Garoua-Boulai (région de l'Est). Les interventions se concentrent sur la recherche de solutions durables pour les plus vulnérables, en utilisant l'approche holistique de graduation pour améliorer à la fois la protection et le redressement économique. Par la suite, fin 2018, DRC a commencé ses activités dans la région du Sud-Ouest du Cameroun fin 2019 pour répondre aux besoins des personnes déplacées de force dans le contexte de la crise anglophone, en commençant les activités humanitaires en janvier 2019. DRC opère dans les divisions de Meme, Fako, Kupe-Manenguba et Ndian avec un bureau à Buea et une sous-base à Kumba. La programmation se concentre sur les zones rurales et difficiles d'accès afin de répondre aux besoins fondamentaux des populations en matière de nourriture, d'abris et de NFI, tout en améliorant l'environnement de protection et en offrant des opportunités génératrices de revenus.

En 2023, DRC a étendu ses activités à l'Extrême-Nord du Cameroun afin d'apporter une réponse en matière de protection, de paix positive, de gouvernance et de résilience économique aux crises multidimensionnelles et interconnectées qui affectent la région.

**2. Objet**

DRC Cameroun cherche à recruter un (e) stagiaire en finance pour son bureau basé à Yaoundé.

**3. Fonctions et Responsabilités**

Sous la Supervision du spécialiste Finance, le stagiaire Finance est chargé de :

**Archivage (60% de son temps)**

- Vérification de la cohérence entre les pièces justificatives et les références des transactions comptables.
- Vérification de la présence des pièces obligatoires dans les dossiers de dépenses.
- Classement des documents par période, selon les standards DRC.
- Mise à jour d'un tableau de suivi des documents archivés et des pièces manquantes.
- Signalement des documents incomplets, illisibles ou mal classés.

**Audit & Conformité (15%) :**

- Participer à la préparation des dossiers de justification des dépenses pour les audits internes et externes.
- Vérifier la disponibilité et la complétude des pièces justificatives conformément aux procédures financières de DRC.
- Contribuer à la collecte des documents demandés par les auditeurs.
- Assurer le suivi des pièces justificatives manquantes en collaboration avec les différents départements.
- Participer à la préparation des dossiers de contrôle fiscal sous la supervision du spécialiste Finance.

**Administration et relations externes (10%) :**

- Appuyer le Département Finance dans le dépôt et le retrait des documents auprès des établissements bancaires.
- Assister dans la transmission et la collecte des documents auprès des services des impôts.
- Participer au suivi administratif des dossiers bancaires et fiscaux.
- Assurer le classement et l'archivage des documents reçus des partenaires externes

**Appui aux opérations financières (15%)**

- Appuyer le Département Finance dans le dépôt et le retrait des documents auprès des établissements bancaires.
- Assister dans la transmission et la collecte des documents auprès des services des impôts.
- Participer au suivi administratif des dossiers bancaires et fiscaux.
- Assurer le classement et l'archivage des documents reçus des partenaires externes
- Participer au suivi des factures fournisseurs en attente de paiement et contribuer à la vérification de leur documentation

**4. Qualifications requises**

**Expériences et compétences techniques** :

- Être titulaire d'un diplôme de niveau Bac+2 minimum ou être étudiant en cours de formation universitaire dans les domaines de la Finance, de la Comptabilité, de la Gestion, de la Business Administration ou d'une formation professionnelle équivalente.
- Avoir une connaissance de base des logiciels de gestion comptable et financière (SAGE, Microsoft Dynamics, NAVISION, SAGA, etc.) constitue un atout.
- Avoir une bonne maîtrise des outils Microsoft Office, notamment Word, Outlook et PowerPoint.
- Avoir une bonne maîtrise d'Excel, notamment les formules de base, les fonctions de recherche, les filtres et le tri.
- Disposer de bonnes capacités d'analyse, d'organisation et de traitement des données financières.
- Avoir de bonnes capacités rédactionnelles et être capable de contribuer à la préparation de rapports et de documents de suivi.
- Disposer d'excellentes aptitudes relationnelles et être capable de travailler en équipe, de respecter les délais et de s'adapter à un environnement de travail exigeant.
- Avoir une bonne capacité d'adaptation et un intérêt pour le fonctionnement des organisations internationales et du secteur humanitaire.
- La maîtrise du français et/ou de l'anglais constitue un atout.

**5. Compétences et qualités exigées**

- À ce poste, vous devez démontrer les cinq compétences essentielles du DRC, à savoir :
- Viser l'excellence : vous vous concentrez sur l'obtention de résultats tout en garantissant un processus efficace. Vous vous efforcez de produire un travail précis, approfondi et professionnel avec une utilisation optimale du temps et des efforts.
- Collaborer : vous coopérez avec et impliquez les parties concernées, recherchant activement leur opinion et partageant des informations clés avec elles. Vous soutenez et faites confiance aux autres, tout en encourageant les commentaires.
- Prendre les rênes : Vous prenez la responsabilité et donnez la priorité à votre travail en fonction de la vision et des objectifs généraux de DRC. Vous prenez l’initiative face à un défi ou une opportunité et vous recherchez des solutions innovantes.
- Communiquer : vous écrivez et parlez efficacement et honnêtement tout en adaptant votre style et votre ton à la situation. Vous écoutez activement les autres et les impliquez dans le dialogue.
- Faire preuve d’intégrité : Vous respectez et promouvez les normes les plus strictes en matière de conduite éthique et professionnelle en relation avec les valeurs et le code de conduite de DRC, y compris la protection contre l’exploitation sexuelle, les abus et le harcèlement.
- Capacité à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel et cosmopolite
- Proactivité, avec une approche coopérative et collaborative
- D’excellentes capacités de communication (notamment l’attention et la patience) sont nécessaires
- De bonnes capacités organisationnelles sont requises
- Sens de l’éthique exemplaire
- Capacité à travailler en équipe et bon sens de l’humour

**6. Réglementations générales**

- L'employé doit suivre les instructions de DRC en matière de sécurité, de confidentialité et de directives éthiques, y compris le code de conduite et le cadre de responsabilité humanitaire
- L'employé ne doit exercer aucune autre activité rémunérée pendant la durée du contrat DRC sans autorisation préalable
- L'employé ne doit pas s'engager dans une activité qui pourrait nuire à DRC ou à la mise en œuvre de tout projet pendant la durée du contrat DRC
- L'employé ne doit pas accorder d'interviews aux médias ni publier de photos liées aux programmes de DRC ou partager d'autres documents sans en recevoir l’autorisation préalable
- L'employé doit restituer tout l'équipement prêté par DRC pour effectuer le travail après la fin de la période du contrat ou sur demande de DRC.

jobs.title: Field Administrative Officer
jobs.description:
**Summary:** The Field Administrative Officer is responsible for ensuring effective management of field-level administrative functions, operational support services and institutional liaison with relevant stakeholders. The position will provide administrative and logistical support to field operations while representation the Country Director in field-level meetings and coordination forums when formally delegated.

The position plays an important role in strengthening communication between the Nairobi Office and Kakuma field operations, maintaining effective relationships with government authorities, humanitarian actors, development partners and community stakeholders, and ensuring that organizational interests and priorities are appropriately represented. The position is also responsible for ensuring that field administrative activities comply with organizational policies, procedures, donor requirements and applicable national laws and regulations. The position will be based at Kakuma Field office.

**Financial and Administrative Support.**

- Maintain proper documentation for administrative expenditure.
- Verify supporting documents for office-related expenses before submission to Finance.
- Support petty cash management.
- Coordinate submission of invoices, receipts and payment requests.
- Provide administrative and operational support to program and technical teams as required.
- Monitor administrative expenditure and report significant variances or emerging resource requirements.
- Coordinate and oversee the day-to-day administrative functions of the field office.
- Ensure effective management of office facilities, utilities, supplies and administrative services.
- Maintain proper filing systems, correspondence, documentation and records management.
- Coordinate office maintenance, repairs and other essential services.
- Ensure adequate availability of office supplies and stationery.
- Maintain confidentiality and proper custody of organizational documents.
- Prepare periodic administrative reports and provide updates on field office operational requirements

**Logistics and Procurement Support**

- Coordinate administrative and logistical requirements for field office activities.
- Support procurement processes in accordance with organizational policies and procedures.
- Facilitate collection of quotations and preparation of procurement documentation.
- Coordinate delivery, inspection and receipt of procured goods and services.
- Maintain proper supplier records and procurement documentation.
- Monitor office supply requirements and facilitate timely replenishment.
- Maintain accurate and updated field office asset and inventory registers.
- Ensure proper tagging, allocation, tracking and accountability of organizational assets.
- Coordinate periodic physical asset verification and inventory checks.
- Monitor vehicle utilization, fuel consumption and maintenance schedules.
- Maintain vehicle logbooks and relevant transport documentation.
- Coordinate transportation arrangements for staff, visitors and official field activities.

**Field Representation & Coordination:** The position will represent the Country Director in designated field-level meetings, coordination forums and institutional engagements, subject to prior authorization or formal written delegation. In this capacity, the postholder shall:

- Represent the organization in authorized engagements with local government authorities, UN agencies, international and national NGOs, development partners, community leaders and other relevant stakeholders.
- Prepare meeting briefs, background information and talking points to support the Country Director’s engagement and decision-making.
- Document key discussions, decisions, recommendations and action points, and submit timely meeting reports and updates to the Country Director and relevant management.
- Follow up on agreed actions and facilitate effective communication and coordination between field offices, the Country Office and relevant external stakeholders.
- Maintain constructive professional relationships, promote collaboration and information sharing, and safeguard the organization's image, credibility and institutional interests.
- Monitor emerging field-level developments and provide timely, factual updates on operational activities, stakeholder concerns and issues requiring management attention.
- Maintain and regularly update records of key institutional contacts, partners and relevant coordination platforms.
- Escalate sensitive policy, political, security, reputational and strategic matters to the Country Director for guidance and appropriate action.
- Serves as the Field Office’s designated security focal point, coordinating security-related matters and ensuring effective communication, guidance, and follow-up on security issues.

**Qualifications: Required education, experience, certificates, licenses or registrations**
- Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Management, Development Studies, Logistics, Supply Chain Management or a related discipline.
- A relevant professional qualification or additional training in administration, operations, project management or stakeholder relations is an advantage.
- At least 3–5 years of relevant professional experience in administration, operations, institutional liaison or coordination, preferably within an INGO or humanitarian organization.
- Demonstrated experience in field office administration and operational support.
- Experience engaging with government authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, development partners and other institutional stakeholders.
- Previous experience attending coordination meetings or representing an organization in delegated engagements is highly desirable.
- Experience working in donor-funded program and humanitarian or development environments is an advantage.
- High level of computer skills and knowledge of databases.
- Excellent oral and written communication skills.
- Citizen of Kenya or have authorization to work in Kenya.

**Competencies (Knowledge, Skills and Abilities)**
- Demonstrates high levels of integrity, honesty, confidentiality, discretion and ethical conduct, consistently upholding CVT’s core values, humanitarian principles and organizational standards.
- Excellent written and verbal communication, interpersonal and relationship-management skills
- Strong administrative, planning, organizational and coordination abilities, with the capacity to manage competing priorities, handle high workloads, coordinate multiple activities and meet deadlines.
- Strong analytical, critical-thinking, statistical and problem-solving abilities, with sound judgment, attention to detail and the capacity to make informed decisions.
- Highly motivated, proactive and self-driven, with the ability to work independently under minimal supervision, adapt to changing priorities and perform effectively under pressure.
- Good understanding of humanitarian coordination structures, field operational environments, donor compliance requirements, organizational policies and internal control systems.
- Knowledge of procurement procedures, logistics coordination, fleet operations, asset management and related administrative processes.
- Good report-writing, minute-taking, record-keeping and briefing preparation skills, with proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
- Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds, coupled with willingness and ability to travel within Kenya and the region as required.

jobs.title: Physiotherapist Intern
jobs.description:
**Summary:** The Center for Victims of Torture (CVT) is offering a paid physiotherapy internship for recent graduates who want to develop their skills in trauma-focused rehabilitation with survivors of torture and war trauma. The internship combines structured training, regular clinical supervision and practical experience in individual and group physiotherapy. The intern will work under the guidance of the Physiotherapist Trainer as part of an interdisciplinary team.

**Learning and professional development**

- Attend and actively participate in required training, clinical supervision, case discussions and team debriefings. These are core responsibilities of the internship.
- Agree learning goals with the Physiotherapist Trainer, review progress regularly and apply feedback to clinical practice.
- Develop skills in trauma-informed assessment, clinical reasoning, individual and group facilitation, and collaborative care. Bring questions and clinical uncertainties to supervision and seek guidance when needed.

**Supervised clinical practice and progression**

- During the initial period, observe assessments and co-facilitate individual and group sessions with an experienced clinician. Take on agreed parts of assessments and sessions with direct guidance.
- Build skills in planning and delivering treatment in line with CVT’s physiotherapy manuals and guidelines, reviewing client progress and supporting clients with self-management.
- Take on responsibility for leading clinical activities independently as agreed by the Physiotherapist Trainer. Progression will depend on demonstrated competence. Regular supervision will continue as responsibilities increase.

**Contributing to the team**

- Keep accurate, timely clinical records and follow CVT’s confidentiality, safeguarding and clinical procedures.
- Work with physiotherapy colleagues, psychosocial counsellors and social workers to coordinate care, discuss client needs and support referrals.
- Support the day-to-day running of the service and assist with community outreach and external training as needed.

**Qualifications and skills**

- Degree in physiotherapy from a recognized institution.
- Required professional registration and a current license to practice in Kenya.
- Strong spoken and written communication skills in English and Swahili.
- Ability to work collaboratively, respond to feedback and take an active role in learning.
- Recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Applicants may draw on their student clinical placements when describing their experience.

**Internship duration:** 3 months, with the possibility of a further 3-month extension subject to performance.

jobs.title: Officer, Strategic Events, West Coast
jobs.description:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Background**:

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises, helping people to survive, recover and rebuild their future. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, we are at work in over 40 countries and 25 offices across the U.S.

**Job Overview:**

The Strategic Events Team designs and executes high-impact events focused on thought leadership, stewardship, cultivation, and fundraising. These events aim to introduce new audiences to the IRC’s mission and deepen engagement with current supporters.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Experiential Marketing, this role collaborates with colleagues across the Philanthropy teams, focused on the Western Region, and the broader Marketing and Mobilization team. The Officer will consult on, conceptualize, and implement engagement activities that support ambitious fundraising goals and elevate the IRC’s profile.

Working closely with the Events, Experiential Marketing and Philanthropy teams, this role will help plan and execute both short- and long-term strategies for events and experiential marketing campaigns that align with the following objectives:

- Supporting private fundraising efforts
- Developing corporate partnership opportunities
- Elevating the IRC's public profile
- Enhancing global brand awareness

The Officer of Strategic Events, West Coast will collaborate with internal and external partners across domestic markets with key focus on the West Coast and other new markets for the IRC – including but not limited to, the Bay Area, Los Angeles, Texas, Arizona, Seattle, and Colorado. This individual will contribute expertise in event strategies in new and existing markets, event programming, marketing, logistics, and production coordination. This individual will collaborate closely with our west coast philanthropy team on developing key relationships with donors, and partners alike. This is an individual contributor role that applies specialized event and functional skills to deliver objectives, woring with guidance and approval from the Associate Director of Strategic events and the Senior Director ofExperiential Marketing.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Collaborate with the team and key internal stakeholders to develop events (both live and virtual), ranging from high-level gatherings to large-scale dinners, thought leadership conferences, and meetings.
- Work with senior leadership and philanthropy stakeholders, who set the strategy and tone for each visit, to project manage and coordinate multi-day leadership trips and market activations.
- Coordinate logistics involved with regional leadership visits. Including contributing to trip briefings and tiktoks.
- Develop event themes, structures, and program elements and compelling IRC content
- Lead and oversee various aspects of event project management, including team coordination, logistics, production, and execution from planning through post-event wrap-up. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
- Leading kickoff meetings
- Drafting concept notes
- Creating creative briefs
- Conducting venue searches
- Booking and managing event speakers – both internal and external
- Managing the approved budget
- Managing event logistics including AV
- Managing printing (signage, badges, programs, collateral)
- Preparing and distributing event materials, communications, and other professional documents
- Developing full scale run of shows
- Day of event coordination and management
- Evaluating event effectiveness and analyzing audience data

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s Degree minimum or minimum 3 years experiencewith the shown ability to organize events through all phases of development

**Skills and Competencies:**

- Outstanding MS office and Event database management skills (Salesforce and Pardot, aka Salesforce Marketing Cloud Account Engagement, experience preferred)
- Proven project and event management skills (in person and virtual) with the ability to balance multiple time-sensitive tasks simultaneously and prioritize tasks appropriately
- Strong budget management and vendor negotiation skills
- Exceptional attention to detail
- Ability to work to in quick turnaround standards and planning lead times
- Confidence to push back constructively and offer alternatives as the events expert
- Sound judgement to resolve and logistis challenges by drawing on past experience within establish boundaries and procedures
- Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate and collaborate effectively and diplomatically with donors, clients, colleagues, vendors and consultants
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Creative with a passion for story-telling
- Resilient and able to remain calm in high pressure situations
- A great teammate able to work effectively with multicultural, global teams
- Dedication to respecting and maintaining confidentiality of information
- Passion for the IRC’s mission

**Working Environment:**

- Remote/Flex time work
- Successful candidate should be available to work late evenings and open to travel for events as the need arises.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $85,000-$89,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.
