jobs.title: MOSAIC- Short-term Volunteering Greece ( February-March)
jobs.description:
The organization was established in **2016** in response to the European refugee crisis and now manages cultural centers and residential programs for migrants and refugees in Spain and Greece. We are a small international team united by a commitment to breaking down barriers to social inclusion for migrants and refugees.

**Our main projects in Greece include:**

- Early childhood education center.
- Socio-educational activities with children and youth.
- Education activities for adults.
- Women Space.
- Transport and mobility projects to connect refugee camps to urban areas.
- European Union projects that foster social innovation and exchange of best practice.

For a period of **2 months**, starting in **early February 2027**, we are offering different volunteering positions within OCC Greece, focused on supporting the implementation of the projects in Polykastro.

**OCC Greece is looking for EU and Greek volunteers for the following positions, with the possibility to combine more than one position:**

● **Teaching for children, youth, or adults:** Teaching English, German, Dutch, French and/or Greek basic literacy to adults and/or minors from the displaced community.
● **Kindergarten:** Supporting the organisation and delivery of educational and
recreational activities for young children.
● **Women’s Space:** Organizing and implementing recreational/well-being activities for women and girls.
● **Monitoring and Evaluation:** Administrative work for monitoring and evaluating our organisation, in collaboration with the correspondent OCC manager.
● **Communications:** Use and editing of communications media via our
communications equipment, administration of social media accounts, promotional campaigns, etc.
● **Computer/IT Classes:** Teaching and promoting basic digital literacy skills i.e. use of Microsoft Office, setting up and email, etc to our beneficiaries’ Community.
**● CV Hub:** Supporting the development of CVs, navigating online job platforms, identifying employment opportunities and submitting job applications.
**● Community Garden**: Supporting participants in the development and maintenance of a community garden in collaboration with local farmers and members of the displaced communities. Activities may include preparing the soil, planting and caring for vegetables, watering, harvesting and distributing fresh produce. Volunteers will also support organise participatory gardening activities and workshops on sustainable agriculture and environmental awareness.

**We are looking for volunteers with the following profile:**

● Good level of English and/or Greek.
● Specific age (18-30 years old)
● Being easy-going and eager to work in an intercultural, autonomous
environment.
● Being motivated, proactive, open-minded, creative, and self-reliant.
● Available to share an apartment and bedroom with other volunteers (shared
rooms with exclusively same-sex/gender volunteers).
● Training and/or experience in teaching and education is an asset.
● Basic gardening skills or an interest in gardening and sustainable **agriculture** are an asset.

**This means that volunteering provides:**

**● Travel costs coverage:** Up to the limits established in the Erasmus+ Guide
distance calculator from the volunteer’s region of residency to our center, and
back.
**● Accommodation:** Free accommodation is offered in Polikastro, Greece, along with other volunteers. Apartments are fully equipped (kitchen, bathrooms, washing machine, etc.). Bedrooms are shared with other volunteers of the same gender.
● **Monthly food + pocket money:** 270€
**● Insurance:** Henner
**● Language courses:** In person or online

jobs.title: Community Liaison Manager, Syria
jobs.description:
**Community Liaison Manager, Syria**

**The starting salary package for this position is £43,828 GBP including all allowances.**

**This is a permanent position.**

**This is an unaccompanied post.**

**About MAG:**

MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in over 40 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.

**About the role:**

In this role, you will play a vital part in assisting the CLM Team Leader (CLM-TL) and Senior Management Team to ensure that MAG’s approach to community participation in mine action is efficiently integrated into the planning, implementation and monitoring of programme activities.

To manage and assess CL resources, field activities and staff in their area of operations, ensuring quality implementation, stakeholder engagement, alignment to donor and authorities’ requirements, and contributions to the improvement of MAG methodologies, tools and deliverables.

To lead the gathering and dissemination of relevant and accurate information in their area of operations, in coordination with the CLM-TL, to enable informed decision making, maximisation of impact and the achievement of MAG’s vision, mission and key aims.

**About the Syria programme:**

MAG has been responding to the Syria crisis since 2013, working to support development by finding and destroying the explosive remnants of war so that communities can raise their families and pursue their livelihoods in a safe and secure environment, free from fear of death or injury. In addition to our current programme in the North West, you will also support the safe expansion of initiatives across all of Syria, based on where and how opportunities arise in the future.

**Responsibilities:**

**Technical**

- Plan CL activities efficiently to ensure project outcomes are met in a cost-efficient manner benefiting to the donor, beneficiaries and affected communities in general.
- Support and facilitate maximum community participation and understanding during all stages of clearance activities.
- Maintain regular liaison with CLM-TL, TOM, TFMs and technical staff to align CL deployment with wider operational planning, information needs, evidence-based tasking, and support to land release activities as required.
- Advise on safe and effective management of all aspects of CL and related tasks in the area of operation and ensure that these are consistent with MAG’s mandate and in accordance with relevant IMAS, NMAS and MAG Standard Operating Procedures.
- Assist and support the development of the country programme strategy, plans, proposals and budgets relevant to CL.
- Conduct and direct needs/context assessments, stakeholder mapping, data gathering and analysis, to help prioritise affected groups, intervention scopes, and geographical areas for Community Liaison activities: Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (RE), Non-Technical Survey (NTS), Impact Assessment (IA) and liaison for land release.
- Assist in the identification, design and implementation of RE projects and delivery channels, as well as the development, contextualisation and testing of RE materials and messaging.
- Ensure NTS activities follow due process, NMAS, IMAS and MAG SOPs, adopting an evidence-based approach and following safety measures in place.
- Conduct and support impact assessments and evaluation studies as required, including on-site interviews with beneficiaries and other stakeholders, and contribute to the refinement of impact measurement tools and indicators.
- As per CLM-TL guidance/orientations, implement Quality Management (QM) system and tools to assess needs in capacity building in CL-related topics (including but not limited to RE, NTS and impact assessment activities) to plan and deliver training accordingly.
- Monitor and evaluate CL deliverables closely, conduct regular follow-ups with CL staff, and undertake regular planning and tracking to ensure targets are met.
- Develop team capacity in the use of MAG Operations Management Information System in their area of operations, for data collection, analysis, reporting, strategic planning and impact assessment purposes.

**Communication & Reporting**

- Establish and maintain on-going liaison and information exchange networks with all relevant stakeholders (government, INGOs, national NGOs, mine action centres, health care providers etc.).
- Where MAG is implementing CL via implementing partners, ensure regular and cordial partnership relations.
- Represent MAG CL in coordination meetings, workshops, and technical working groups as required.
- Assist with proposal writing and budgeting as required.
- Provide clear and accurate reports for donor, authorities and HQ purposes, including case studies and oral testimonies.
- Ensure proper documenting, archiving and storage of CL resources (photographs, reports, EORE materials, studies, training packages, etc.).

**People Management and Capacity Building**

- Direct, supervise, manage and develop CL Supervisor, team leaders and CL teams to deliver high-quality work
- Coordinate and build capacity of implementing partners.
- Recruit national CL staff in coordination with relevant departments.
- Set objectives and conduct appraisals for CL staff and other line reports in line with MAG procedures.
- Plan and conduct relevant training activities for national staff where required, including RE/NTS/IA, participatory learning and facilitation techniques. Incorporate findings of quality management and/or training needs assessments.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with national staff and communities to foster acceptance and maximise impact.
- Uphold humanitarian principles, cultural sensitivity and MAG’s safeguarding framework.
- Promote an inclusive, team-oriented culture aligned with MAG’s values.
- Support CLM-TL to ensure Job Descriptions for CL staff are up to date and in line with MAG standards.

**We’re looking for someone with:**

**Essential Experience**

- Experience of working overseas in community liaison within Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA), Armed Violence Reduction (AVR), Conflict Preparedness and Protection (CPP), and/or educational development roles, delivering programmes that effectively engage local stakeholders.
- Experience of conducting needs or risk assessments in order to design and implement appropriate interventions.
- Strong background in the monitoring and evaluation of development or humanitarian projects.
- Experience in the design and delivery of formal and informal training, with a strong focus on practical learning and effective skills transfer.
- Experience of leading, motivating, coaching and training a diverse team to foster a high-performing and collaborative working environment.
- Experience applying participatory research techniques in operational and community-based settings.
- Experience of working independently for extended periods of time in ‘stand-alone’ environments, exercising sound judgement and initiative with minimal supervision.

**Essential Skills and Knowledge**

- Strong information management skills, with the ability to organise, analyse, and present data effectively
- Understanding of humanitarian response and risk reduction.
- Understanding of diversity and inclusion.
- Good negotiation skills, enabling constructive engagement with a wide range of stakeholders.
- Excellent organizational skills with the ability to coordinate activities and projects in line with accountability principles.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills · Excellent people management, including the ability to motivate, guide and support teams to perform at a high standard.
- Sound understanding of rural livelihood and key international development issues.
- Relevant IT and numeracy skills.
- Good spoken and written English language skills.

**Desirable**

- Experience in managing NTS operations.
- Experience delivering NTS, EORE and CL trainings.
- Arabic language skills.
- Experience of working in Syria, and/or solid understanding of the Syrian context.
- Completion of a recognised EORE course or Mine Action related training

Please note that as part of MAG's commitment to safeguarding, this post is subject to background checks before an offer of employment is confirmed. For more information on MAG’s approach to safeguarding and background checks on our website**.**

MAG is committed to the principles of diversity, equality and inclusion. If you think you would be suited to one of our roles we would welcome your application regardless of your background. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive working environment where all employees feel respected and supported in fulfilling their potential.

**Remuneration Package:**

- **Renumeration Package:** £43,828 per annum including basic salary and all allowances and this increases with service.
- **Accommodation:** MAG will provide accommodation in-country.
- **Leave:** We recognize our staff work hard and need the appropriate time out to stay motivated. You'll have a minimum of eight weeks out of the programme per year.
- **Flights:** MAG provides four international flights home per year**.**
- **Insurance:** Internationally contracted, programme-based staff are automatically covered by MAG's comprehensive insurance package including: Personal accident and medical expenses insurance; Death by natural causes insurance and access to 24-hour medical assistance.

**This position is also open to National candidates:** The package will be aligned with the applicable in-country salary scale, including relevant benefits and entitlements in accordance with MAG Syria's national employment policies. Shortlisted candidates will receive an information sheet outlining the full details of the package during the recruitment process. If you would like any more information about this please contact **recruitment@maginternational.org**

jobs.title: Team Leader (Health Systems)
jobs.description:
## OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

WHO’s work in countries operationalizes the General Programme of Work (GPW14) and the European Programme of Work 2025-2029 (EPW2). GPW14 focuses on accelerating progress toward Health for All by strengthening systems for health, improving access to essential services, advancing preparedness and resilience, and reducing health inequalities. EPW2, endorsed at RC75 following extensive consultation with Member States, reaffirms WHO/Europe’s role in bringing unique value to countries through five core functions:
1\. International knowledge hub for health – providing authoritative evidence, norms, policies and best practices from across the Region and globally to inform national public health decision-making.
2\. Impartial coordinator for everyone’s health – convening national stakeholders and partners to align strategies and support coherent, multisectoral responses to shared health challenges.
3\. Leader in tracking and managing cross-border health threats – supporting surveillance, preparedness, and coordinated action on public health emergencies in line with the Preparedness 2.0 agenda.
4\. Driver of health system transformation – advising national authorities on evidence-informed reforms and policies that strengthen health systems and improve performance.
5\. Voice for health equity – helping countries identify who is being left behind and integrating equity considerations into health policies and strategies.

In this context, WHO Country Offices enable the translation of global and regional commitments into national action. They support Member States by providing strategic advice, convening dialogue across sectors and partners, connecting national authorities with WHO’s technical expertise, and facilitating the use of evidence and best practices to inform policy.

## DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

• Provide strategic, technical and programmatic advice to the WHO Representative on public health priorities and the development and implementation of national health policies, strategies and plans.
• Coordinate with technical focal points at regional and headquarters levels to mobilize relevant WHO expertise and promote coherent technical support. Provide strategic and technical advice to the Head of the WHO Office on national public health priorities, and lead the development of strategies, policies and programmes in collaboration with national authorities, public health partners and key stakeholders to advance national health objectives and WHO priorities. Recommend health-development initiatives in the areas of health systems planning, management and strengthening, and partnership building at country level.
• Lead the country office’s technical and capacity-building work, including in the area of public health systems and programmes, ensuring their implementation in line with national strategies and results.
• Provide strategic and technical support to the Head of the WHO Office and partners in developing and implementing sustainable measures for post-emergency recovery, rehabilitation and transition towards resilient health systems. Provide oversight of and ensure the development and submission of monitoring and reporting on technical public health initiatives/ health systems at country level.
• Represent the Head of WHO Office at official meetings with the government, national counterparts, donors, UN agencies and other stakeholders.
• Manage the overall compliance and performance management standards of the Health Programme, including defining work planning parameters to establish performance standards, accountability, and indicators for progress monitoring and reporting.
• Ensure internal controls are in place and adhered to, in order to ensure due diligence and mitigate financial risk to the health programmes at country level.
• Provide expert policy advice and guidance to the government and national stakeholders on the design, implementation, and evaluation of national health policies for health system strengthening in order to move towards Universal Health Coverage (UHC).

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

### Education

**Essential:** An advanced university degree (Master’s level or above) in public health, medicine, international health, management or social sciences or related field.

**Desirable:** Specialized training in emergency management, international aid, humanitarian principles, health system recovery, epidemiology, health economics, health financing project management and impact evaluation.

### Experience

**Essential:** At least 10 years of experience in the development and management of technical public health programmes, including a minimum of five years in an international context, with at least two years of experience in fostering collaborative partnerships and managing and coordinating health programmes in acute and protracted emergencies and humanitarian settings.

**Desirable**: Relevant work experience in WHO, other UN agencies, health cluster partners, relevant nongovernmental or humanitarian organizations. Also in managing diverse teams and financial resources at international level.

### Competencies:

Teamwork
Respecting and promoting individual and cultural differences
Communication
Promoting the Organization's position in health leadership
Building and promoting partnerships across the Organization and beyond
Creating an empowering and motivating environment

### Functional Knowledge and Skills:

• Programme and financial management and/or the administration of complex health programmes and services at the international and country level.
• Ability to lead and coordinate multidisciplinary teams, projects and programmes.
• Ability to manage and adapt to complex and changing political, social, and economic contexts.
• Strong skills in diplomacy and political acumen.
• Emotional awareness: Ability to identify and harness one’s emotions and apply them to tasks; and the ability to manage emotions, which includes both regulating one’s own emotions when necessary and helping others to do the same.

### Use of Language Skills:

**Essential:** Expert knowledge of English. Intermediate knowledge of another United Nations language.

### Information and technology (IT) and other skills

Knowledge of Microsoft Office software applications. Excellent presentation skills.

## REMUNERATION

WHO salaries for staff in the Professional category are calculated in US dollars. The remuneration for the above position comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 103.165 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable), a variable post adjustment, which reflects the cost of living in a particular duty station, and currently amounts to USD 3,055 per month for the duty station indicated above. Other benefits include 30 days of annual leave, allowances for dependent family members, home leave, and an education grant for dependent children.

**Link to apply:** [**Job Description - Team Leader (Health Systems) (2605057)**](https://careers.who.int/careersection/ex/jobdetail.ftl?job=2605057&tz=GMT%2B02%3A00&tzname=Europe%2FKiev)

jobs.title: HEAD OF PROGRAMMES AND STRATEGY
jobs.description:
## **ROLE PROFILE**

Title: Head of Programmes and Strategy

Functional Area: Programmes

Reports to: Country Director

Location: Amman, Jordan

Travel required: As Required

Effective Date: ASAP

Grade: Level 18

## **The organization**

Plan International is an independent child rights and humanitarian organisation committed to children living a life free of poverty, violence and injustice. Plan actively unite children, communities and other people who share our mission to make positive lasting changes in children’s and young people’s lives. Plan support children to gain the skills, knowledge and confidence they need to claim their rights to a fulfilling life, today and in the future. Plan place a specific focus on girls and women, who are most often left behind. Plan have been building powerful partnerships for children for more than 80 years and are now active in more than 70 countries. Plan International Jordan is established in 2016 and has programmes in governorates in the centre, north and south regions as well as host communities and Azraq camp

## **ROLE PURPOSE**

The Head of Programme and Strategy (HoPS) is a new consolidated senior leadership role that brings together programme implementation, technical quality, and organisational strategy under one unified mandate. The role reports directly to the Country Director and is a standing member of the Country Management Team (CMT).

The HoPS assumes full accountability for the effective delivery of all Plan Jordan programmes across all thematic areas and locations — both host communities and Azraq Refugee Camp — and is the primary custodian of Plan Jordan's programmatic vision, translating the Country Strategy 2025–2030 into coherent, evidence-based, gender-transformative programming that delivers lasting impact for children, girls and young people in Jordan. The role operates deliberately across the humanitarian-development nexus, requiring a leader who can hold both dimensions simultaneously without compromising either.

The post holder serves as a strategic thought partner to the Country Director, contributing to CMT leadership on organisational direction, programme innovation and evidence-based decision making, and works in close collaboration with the Head of Resources Mobilisation to ensure programme quality and evidence systematically strengthen donor engagement and resource mobilisation.

## DIMENSIONS OF THE ROLE

- Reports to the Country Director and is a standing member of the Country Management Team (CMT).
- Directly supervises: SOYEE Programmes manager, Inclusive Education/Protection Programmes manager, Impact and Research Manager, Technical specialists, and Senior International Expert
- Oversees the implementation of the Plan Jordan Country Strategy 2025–2030, ensuring quality, evidence-based and rights-grounded delivery across all thematic areas.
- Holds a unified mandate across two dimensions: (1) programme implementation and leadership; (2) technical quality, sector strategy and programme design; where as advocacy, influencing and strategic positioning is encompassed throughout.
- Ensures effective and efficient use of organisational resources, adherence to all relevant Plan policies and procedures and local laws across the full programme portfolio.
- Provides technical oversight across Plan Jordan's thematic sectors: Inclusive Quality Education (IQE), SOYEE (Skills, Opportunities and Youth Economic Empowerment), Child Protection and GBV, Psychosocial Support, and Gender.
- Acts as the senior representative for Plan International Jordan at governorate, national, and where relevant, international levels.
- Works in close collaboration with the Head of Resources Mobilisation, the P&C Manager, the Head of Support Services, and the PMU to ensure integrated, cross-functional delivery.

## ACCOUNTABILITIES

**1. Strategic Planning and Country Strategy Implementation**

- Lead and support the annual planning process for the full programme portfolio, ensuring alignment with the Plan Jordan Country Strategy 2025–2030 and Plan International's global strategies and campaigns.
- Work closely with all Country Office departments to ensure project budgets are developed and implemented in tandem with the country approved budget and relevant financial policies.
- Ensure that all funded projects are implemented to a consistent high standard, on time, within approved budgets and in line with approved log frames.
- Review and ensure alignment of programme priorities, strategies and plans with the Country Strategy and the broader Plan International frameworks.
- Support the Country Director and CLT in the development of both strategic and operational plans in accordance with Country Strategy and planning guidelines.
- Provide leadership in strategy formulation, implementation planning, execution, and monitoring to ensure alignment with global Plan International guidance, regional strategy, country context, and donor requirements.
- Develop and review technically sound sector approaches and strategies enabling PIJO to respond to both humanitarian emergency and sustainable development needs across all operational areas.

**2. Programme Implementation Leadership**

- Lead, coach and support the Thematic Programmes Leads, Projects Managers/experts in Azraq Camp and HCs, and Senior in achieving the targets of the annual plans.
- Develop appropriate work mechanisms ensuring that teams work in coordination, leading to the achievement of planned objectives set out in approved annual plans and the Plan Jordan Country Strategy.
- Foster a values-based, feminist leadership culture within all programme teams.
- Ensure an enabling environment for staff performance, recognition and innovation across the full programme portfolio.
- Ensure close coordination between programme implementation, the MERL function, and the Head of Resources Mobilisation to ensure quality field inputs to grant proposals and strategic initiatives.
- Ensure close coordination with P&C and Support Services to ensure compliance with Plan's and donors' policies and procedures across all programme activities.
- Ensure the production of high-quality internal reports and donor reports in close coordination with National Offices and the Regional Hub.

**3. Technical Quality and Programme Design**

- Lead the technical quality agenda across Plan Jordan — ensuring that all programmes meet Plan International's global quality standards and sector-specific minimum standards (INEE, CP in Humanitarian Action, SPHERE, etc.).
- Co-Lead on proposal development and submission, including identifying priority areas of intervention, potential partnerships, and ensuring timely and high-quality submission to donors.
- Lead rapid and detailed assessments in new target areas; determine priorities, immediate activities, and required resources.
- In close collaboration with regional specialists, define objectives and key outcomes of Plan Jordan's programmatic response in line with national strategies.
- Develop evidence-based programme plans including programmatic, research and advocacy priorities, closely linked to sector programmes.
- Ensure robust monitoring, evaluation, research and learning (MERL) systems are in place, and that the country office engages in the collection, use and sharing of evidence for decision-making.
- Ensure regular communication with thematic leads and project coordinators to integrate appropriate technical input and priorities in programme design and implementation.
- Coordinate regular field monitoring visits to assess progress, identify technical quality issues, provide solutions and implement modifications as required.
- Ensure that quality data collection and information management systems are in place for appropriate programme analysis, planning, evaluation and advocacy.
- Ensure outcomes from regular monitoring and periodic evaluations feed into learning and improvement of projects — and that learning is documented in the most effective way, demonstrating value for money.

**4. . Resource Mobilisation Support and Donor Engagement**

- Work in close collaboration with the Head of Resources Mobilisation to leverage programme quality, technical expertise and field evidence in funding applications, donor reports and strategic positioning.
- Build and maintain direct relationships with donor technical staff, representing Plan Jordan's programme quality and thematic expertise in donor dialogue.
- Identify and pursue strategic partnership and consortium opportunities that strengthen Plan Jordan's competitive positioning.
- Support the Country Director in representing Plan Jordan's value proposition — including the humanitarian-development nexus positioning and flex fund return on investment story — to donors, National Offices and the Regional Hub.

**5 . Networking, Partnerships, Safeguarding and Inclusion**

- Build and maintain relationships with government ministries, UN agencies, INGOs, national NGOs, local partners and relevant coordination platforms across all thematic areas.
- Represent Plan Jordan in network and alliance meetings, working groups and thematic task forces at national and international levels.
- Ensure Plan International's safeguarding, gender equality and inclusion policies are fully embedded across all programmes, partnerships and implementation modalities — treating safeguarding as a programmatic priority, not a compliance exercise.
- Ensure all supervised staff understand and fulfil their safeguarding and Code of Conduct responsibilities, and that partner organisations are adequately assessed and monitored on safeguarding and GEI standards.
- Promote gender-transformative and inclusive programming across all thematic areas, ensuring girls and young women are positioned as rights-holders and agents of change.

**6. People Management**

- Lead, manage and develop supervised staff — fostering an empowering, inclusive and values-based work environment aligned to Plan's feminist leadership principles.
- Set clear performance objectives, conduct appraisals, provide coaching and mentoring, and ensure performance records are submitted to P&C on time.
- Work with the P&C Manager to identify training needs, support recruitment, and ensure succession planning across the programme team.

### Child protection, gender equality and inclusion

- *Ensures that Plan International’s global policies for Safeguarding Children, Young People and Programmes Participants and Gender Equality and Inclusion are fully embedded in accordance with the principles and requirements of the policy including relevant Implementation Standards and Guidelines as applicable to their area of responsibility. This includes, but is not limited to, ensuring staff and associates are aware of and understand their responsibilities under these policies and Plan*

## KEY RELATIONSHIPS

**Internal:**

- Country Director — primary line manager and CMT business partner.
- SOYEE Programmes manager, Inclusive Education Programmes manager Projects Manager Azraq Camp, MERL Manager, Senior International Expert DAAP — direct reports.
- Head of Resources Mobilisation — close collaboration on donor engagement, proposal development, and strategic positioning.
- Key CMT members
- Protection, Gender & Safeguarding Specialist — technical guidance and safeguarding oversight.
- PMU — coordination on programme management quality, MERL and donor reporting.
- Youth Advisory Panel (YAP) — engagement and representation.

**External**:

- Government counterparts — Ministry of Education, Ministry of Social Development, Ministry of Labour, Ministry of Interior, and relevant governorate-level authorities.
- UN agencies, INGOs, national NGOs, and civil society networks.
- Plan International National Offices, Regional Hub, and global technical networks.
- Donors — representation, reporting, and relationship management.
- National and sub-national advocacy and policy forums, coalitions, and working groups relevant to Plan Jordan's thematic priorities.

## **TECHNICAL EXPERTISE, SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE**

**Essential**

- A Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, International Relations, or a related field.
- A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in development and/or humanitarian programming, with at least 5 years at senior management level in an NGO or INGO environment.
- Proven track record in both programme implementation leadership and technical quality management across at least two of the following sectors: child protection, education, GBV, youth economic empowerment, gender, psychosocial support.
- In-depth and strategic understanding of integrated development issues and critical analysis of child poverty.
- High-level knowledge of strategic planning processes and theories of child-rights programming.
- Demonstrated understanding of and commitment to children's issues in Jordan and the region.
- Proven understanding of gender-in-development concepts and the promotion of girls' rights in the context of international conventions (CRC, CEDAW) and the SDGs.
- Strong experience in proposal development, programme design, and donor engagement across multiple funding mechanisms.
- Demonstrated ability to network and liaise with UN bodies, coordination mechanisms, government authorities, and donors.
- Excellent skills in project design, time management and problem-solving.
- Proven skills in developing and managing effective, motivated and diverse teams.
- Excellent English and Arabic language skills, both written and spoken.

**Desirable**

- A Master's degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, International Relations, or a related field.
- Knowledge of the national policy and legislative landscape related to education, child protection, gender, and youth in Jordan.
- Experience in programming related to child labour, child marriage, girls' rights, SRHR, and ECCD.
- Familiarity with Plan International's programme quality frameworks and global campaigns.
- Experience working in camp or refugee settings.

## **PLAN INTERNATIONAL'S VALUES IN PRACTICE**

**We are open and accountable**

- Promotes a culture of openness and transparency, including with sponsors and donors.
- Holds self and others accountable to achieve the highest standards of integrity.
- Consistent and fair in the treatment of people.
- Open about mistakes and keen to learn from them.
- Accountable for ensuring we are a safe organisation for all children, girls & young people

**We strive for lasting impact**

- Articulates a clear purpose for staff and sets high expectations.
- Creates a climate of continuous improvement, open to challenge and new ideas.
- Focuses resources to drive change and maximise long-term impact, responsive to changed priorities or crises.
- Evidence-based and evaluates effectiveness.

**We work well together**

- Seeks constructive outcomes, listens to others, willing to compromise when appropriate.
- Builds constructive relationships across Plan International to support our shared goals.
- Develops trusting and ‘win-win’ relationships with funders, partners and communities.
- Engages and works well with others outside the organization to build a better world for girls and all children.

**We are inclusive and empowering**

- We empower our staff to give their best and develop their potential
- We respect all people, appreciate differences and challenge equality in our programs and our workplace
- We support children, girls and young people to increase their confidence and to change their own lives.

## **PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENT**

Typically office-based with regular in-country travel and occasional international travel.

## **Level of contact with children**

Mid contact: Occasional interaction with children

## **ROLE PROFILE**

**Type of Role:** Fixed Term Contract

**Contract Duration:** One year, renewable subject to the availability of funds and satisfactory performance.

**Reports to:** Country Director

**Location:** Amman, Jordan

**Grade:** Level 18

**Closing Date:** 2 December 2026

*Female candidates are highly encouraged to apply. Plan International operates an equal opportunities policy and actively encourages diversity, welcoming applications from all areas of the international community.*

*Early application is encouraged as we will review applications throughout the advertising period and reserve the right to close the advert early.*

*Internal candidates will be given priority consideration.*

*Please note that only applications and CVs written in English will be accepted.*

*A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International's Child Safeguarding Policy.*

**About Mehad Organization:**

humanitarian organization: medical aid and relief, non-profit, non-governmental,

It was founded in January 2012, with the vision to work under a unified strategic framework aiming to provide medical service non-profit to affected people and communities, regardless of nationality, ethnicity, gender, religion or political loyalty.

Our values:

- Trust
- Ambition
- Accountability

**General information:**

- Working system: Administrative / Full-time

Position Title: **Health Advisor**‏

Number required:1

Code: AHR-MH-26-52

Closing date: 2026-11-25

**Background:**

Mehad seeks to recruit a Health Advisor to provide technical supervision and expertise to health staff, strengthen the quality of health services, deliver relevant training, and contribute to the development of project proposals.

The Health Advisor will work closely with Mehad’s teams and departments to design health projects and proposals and support their implementation, in coordination with relevant authorities and partners, ensuring that activities respond to community needs and align with applicable national standards.

8. Review health-related proposals and project documents to ensure technical quality, feasibility, and alignment with Mehad’s priorities and donor requirements..

10. Contribute to the assessment of needs for medicines and medical supplies, in coordination with the relevant departments within the organization.
11. Represent Mehad in relevant Health coordination meetings and forums.
12. Attend coordination meetings at the organizational level, and with donors.
13. Carry out other relevant duties as requested by the line manager.

**Requirements:**

1. Bachelor's degree in a medicine
2. At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in health programming, or health-service delivery supervision.
3. Experience in project planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting.
4. Experience contributing to the development of health project proposals.
5. Good knowledge of relevant clinical and public health standards, guidelines, and service-delivery approaches.
6. Experience working with health authorities, health facilities, NGOs, or other health-sector partners.
7. Strong communication, coordination, and report-writing skills.
8. Fluent in Arabic and English, both spoken and written.
9. Strong computer skills (MS Office).
10. Ability to travel and change of work hours.

jobs.description:
**CONTEXT**
MSF is supporting the re-opening of a public maternity hospital in Haiti. The project focuses on restoring a 3,000 sq m medical facility in Port-au-Prince, to deliver critical Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) care.

**MAIN PURPOSE**
As a water and sanitation Manager & Construction working with MSF, you can help ensure access to lifesaving healthcare for people in need. Our water and sanitation experts design and manage water and sanitation projects in addition to supervising and training staff.

**ACCOUNTABILITIES**

***Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP / MBBR / ABR) Implementation:***

- Finalize and validate the complete technical engineering design for the hospital wastewater treatment system.
- Oversee technical contractors and suppliers during construction, supervising civil works (reinforced concrete slabs) and the installation and commissioning of the MBBR (Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor) unit.
- Lead the design, tendering, and construction of the site-wide wastewater network, including Anaerobic Baffled Reactors (ABRs), lifting pump stations, grease traps, septic tanks, and soak-away systems.

***Water Desalination & Potabilization System Project:***

- Lead the complete design, tendering, and contracting process for the site desalination and water potabilization plant (water softening + reverse osmosis / RO).
- Ensure that maintenance access, availability of critical spare parts, electrical power quality, and long-term operational sustainability are fully integrated into the design from the initial engineering phase.
- Prepare complete tender documentation, lead technical evaluations of supplier bids, and support final contract awards and vendor management.

***WATSAN Design for New Buildings & Extensions:***

- Develop, review, and validate comprehensive WATSAN engineering designs, plumbing schematics, and layout plans for the Labor Room, Newborn Ward, Laundry Facility, and other new infrastructure projects.
- Rethink and upgrade the stormwater/runoff drainage system across the hospital compound.
- Lead technical discussions with medical, Infection Prevention Control, and construction teams to ensure alignment with clinical protocols, hygiene constraints, and operational needs.

***Handover, Maintenance Strategy & System Exploitation Transfer:***

- Handover Dossiers & As-Built Plans: Establish complete handover documentation, As-Built drawings, pipe/valve schematics, and operating manuals for all newly built WATSAN infrastructure.
- Maintenance & Operations Plan: Develop preventative and corrective maintenance protocols, maintenance schedules, buffer stock lists (spare parts, chemical reagents, filters, pump replacement kits), and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
- Staff Capacity Building: Formulate and execute a structured training and mentoring program for national Watsan staff, logistics technicians, and hospital maintenance teams covering daily operation, monitoring, and safety measures.
- Commissioning & Transition: Oversee step-by-step testing and commissioning phases prior to final user takeover to ensure a smooth, safe, and fully documented transfer of ownership.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- Academic background in civil engineering, Sanitary/Environmental engineering or an equivalent relevant training
- Previous experience in technical aspects of water and sanitation works like hospital plumbing, wastewater treatment plant/desalination and construction
- Hands on experience in an emergency project humanitarian or international development setting with a minimum of 6-months
- Desirable experience in or familiar with implementing and promoting the use of two or more of the following activities (water supply, excreta disposal, waste and wastewater management, vector control, and dead bodies management) in two or more different contexts (conflicts, natural disasters, refugee/Internal Displaced People camps, etc.)
- Desirable experience or background in public health
- Fluency in written and spoken French and Englisch (B2 – C1)
- Computer literacy
- Ability to work in a team, cultural sensitivity, excellent organizational and improvisational skills, and a high level of mental and physical resilience
- Willingness to work in accordance with Médecins Sans Frontières humanitarian principles, charter and mission statement

***What do we offer***

- Expected starting date: 01 February 2027
- Location: Port-au-Prince, Haiti
- Contract type and duration: Fixed term contract – Full time, 6 months
- Salary according to MSF mobile salary grid
- Round-trip transportation to and from assignment and room & board during assignment
- A comprehensive insurance package, including health and emergency evacuation insurance
- Holiday leave (depending on project)
- No family position

The major part of our projects are taking place in acute or chronic crisis areas and instable contexts. Learn more about security management within our organization [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SI7MsR-helE) and about working in acute conflict [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oNXdGhxYDeM). The living conditions in the project can be challenging due to isolation, rough climate, security and set up of the living quarters. Learn more about working and living in the projects [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mc-njOPX-K4).

jobs.title: Collective Portfolio Manager
jobs.description:
**Location:** Any MSF office\*

**Contract:** Permanent contract at 100%

**Starting date:** 01st of February 2027

**Deadline to apply:** 03rd of December 2026 - We reserve the right to close this position once suitable candidates have been identified.

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract

*\*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.*

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

**MSF International**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**Context**

MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF movement and implements international projects and initiatives as requested. In 2026, MSF began a new six-year strategic cycle — the Strategic Planning and Resource Cycle (SPARC) — which replaces the previous Resources-Sharing Agreement (RSA4). SPARC brings together movement-wide priorities, coordinated decision-making, shared accountability and collective investment stewardship across the MSF movement.

Within this framework, the Collective Portfolio is a core mechanism for translating SPARC ambitions into coherent, prioritised and monitorable movement-level investments. It brings together the Common Strategic Priorities Portfolio and other collective portfolio components, enabling the movement to assess strategic fit, sequencing, interdependencies, absorptive capacity, risk and value across a complex set of initiatives. The SPARC Interoperability priority in particular cuts across all other priorities and provides an enabling approach that shapes portfolio implementation and coherence.

The Collective Portfolio Manager is the senior role responsible for holding together the diverse components of the Collective Portfolio during SPARC implementation. The role enables collective ownership, strengthens evidence-based steering, and reinforces accountability for results, resource choices and delivery against SPARC Goals and Principles. It operates across MSF’s decentralised governance and executive environment, working closely with the International Office, Executive Committees, the SPARC Steering Committee, the Portfolio Committee, finance stakeholders, content owners and senior leaders across the movement.

As a member of the International Office management environment, the role also contributes to institutional coherence, organisational learning and SPARC-related change leadership.

**Purpose of the job**

The main purpose is to provide strategic leadership for SPARC’s Collective Portfolio to strengthen movement-wide accountability, prioritisation, effectiveness and alignment across collective investments.

The role ensures that the Collective Portfolio has robust decision-making and accountability mechanisms. This includes ensuring that portfolio composition, investment choices, delivery performance, risk monitoring and resource visibility are integrated into cross-cutting analysis and timely executive decision-making.

The role also leads management of the portfolio of work for the Common Strategic Priorities and advances portfolio, project and change management practice across the International Office and relevant executive platforms. This work involves paying particular attention to interoperability, absorption capacity, sequencing, implementation quality and organisational coherence.

Finally, this position also supports the functioning of the SPARC Steering Committee. It provides coordination, analysis and synthesis needed for the Committee to fulfil its oversight role on behalf of the Full ExCom. The role helps translate information emerging from the Collective Portfolio, SPARC Coordinating Mechanisms and related reporting processes into coherent cross-cutting insight on progress, risks, resource implications, interdependencies and emerging tensions.

**Accountabilities**

**1. Manage the Collective Portfolio, enabling effective collective governance.**

**Expected result: The Portfolio Committee, relevant executive platforms and the Full ExCom have timely, relevant and decision-ready information on portfolio performance, integration, resourcing and risk.**

- Integrate and coordinate across the components and content owners of the Collective Portfolio, in line with the SPARC MoU and related governance arrangements;
- Translate portfolio design into practical governance and decision-making processes that strengthen collective ownership and disciplined portfolio stewardship;
- Oversee and report on portfolio composition, results, dependencies, risks and strategic fit, preparing analysis for decision-making in the Portfolio Committee and/or further escalation;
- Oversee and report on portfolio health, planning, and resourcing in close collaboration with the IO finance team, the FinDir and portfolio content owners, ensuring integration with the movement’s annual resource planning and budget cycle;
- Ensure that strategic, operational, organisational and implementation risks across the Collective Portfolio are identified, monitored and escalated appropriately, and facilitate the development of mitigation strategies with relevant stakeholders;
- Convene, prepare and facilitate the work of the Portfolio Committee in line with its terms of reference, ensuring focused discussion, sound documentation, clear follow-up and accountability for agreed actions;
- Develop approaches to gather learning and insight from portfolio implementation and contribute to the ongoing refinement, adaptation, and maturation of the Collective Portfolio model throughout the SPARC cycle.

**2. Lead management of the portfolio of work in the Common Strategic Priorities, strengthening investment steering.**

**Expected result: Initiatives and projects within the portfolio of work for the Common Strategic Priorities are strategically aligned, appropriately prioritised and collectively steered to optimise their contribution to SPARC goals and principles.**

- Coordinate and align stakeholders in the Common Strategic Priorities, bringing coherence with approved Movement-level goals, principles, and agreed outcomes;
- Build and continuously improve the portfolio pipeline management process, ensuring transparency, consistency, usability and institutional learning;
- Drive analysis required for investment steering, including strategic relevance, interdependencies, timing, delivery feasibility, absorption capacity, opportunity costs, and portfolio balance;
- Cultivate reflection on emerging priorities, initiatives, or opportunities for better effectiveness or efficiency among Priorities;
- Broker shared understanding across stakeholders where priorities compete, perspectives diverge or conditions evolve, enabling collective choices in a decentralised environment without direct hierarchical authority;
- Promote equitable participation and enable the surfacing of diverse perspectives from across the movement in portfolio dialogue and prioritisation processes while maintaining focus on strategic coherence and delivery discipline;
- Track portfolio decisions, commitments and follow-up actions to strengthen visibility, continuity, and accountability.

**3. Cultivate organisational learning, advancing portfolio-wide accountability for delivery results.**

**Expected result: Collective portfolio oversight decisions are supported by evidence, implementation follow-through is tangible, and the movement has stronger accountability for the results of collective investments.**

- Shape and maintain fit-for-purpose portfolio monitoring, reporting and review mechanisms to support executive decision-making and accountability for results;
- Consolidate portfolio information into clear, decision-ready reporting for governance and executive stakeholders, including progress, bottlenecks, deviations, unintended outcomes, risks, resource implications and emerging strategic choices.
- Follow up on regular reporting and related steering decisions, translating learning into actionable change, in particular with regards to gaps, delays, unresolved dependencies or accountability concerns.
- Drive the development of relevant review processes, evaluation exercises and reflection on Portfolio effectiveness, organisational learning and value generation.

**4. Lead project, change and interoperability management practices across the International Office and executive Platforms.**

**Expected result: The International Office and relevant executive platforms apply stronger portfolio, project and change management practices, enabling more coherent delivery, organisational learning and implementation effectiveness.**

- Drive the improvement of portfolio, project and change management standards, practices and governance approaches across the International Office and relevant executive Platforms;
- Guide and promote disciplined approaches to planning, implementation, benefits realisation and organisational change;
- Advise stakeholders on ways to assess absorption capacity, implementation feasibility and unintended organisational effects when shaping or adjusting initiative processes, timelines, or scopes;
- Promote coordinated use of resources across projects, portfolios, and change initiatives, seeking efficiencies and facilitating cross-functional learning in the International Office and executive Platforms;
- Engage and align stakeholders around the SPARC Interoperability priority, facilitating shared accountability and progress against the Interoperability Ambitions to 2031 and related roadmap;
- Convene and facilitate relevant project and portfolio management communities or working groups in the Movement to strengthen knowledge-sharing, consistency, effectiveness and institutional learning;

**5. Advise and support process design and facilitation for strategic initiatives or organisational transformation processes as requested by the ISG/DSG5. Support the SPARC Steering Committee in fulfilling its oversight, coordination and escalation role by providing timely portfolio analysis, cross-cutting insight, and decision-support across SPARC implementation**

**Expected result: the Steering Committee is equipped with clear, integrated and decision-ready information that strengthens its ability to monitor SPARC implementation, identify and address cross-cutting challenges, and provide well-grounded advice and recommendations to the Full ExCom.**

- Consolidate relevant inputs from the Collective Portfolio, SPARC Coordinating Mechanisms, monitoring and evaluation processes, and other reporting streams;
- Surface risks, interdependencies, resource implications, tensions and emerging issues;
- Support the preparation of coherent recommendations and documentation for Steering Committee review and onward escalation to the Full ExCom.

Autonomy, complexity

**Autonomy to deliver results**

Operates with a high degree of autonomy within the mandate of the role. Determines portfolio management approaches, governance rhythms, prioritisation processes, analytical frameworks and facilitation strategies required to strengthen collective investment steering, accountability and executive decision-making. Exercises independent judgement on complex organisational, strategic and implementation issues with movement-wide implications, while escalating matters requiring broader executive or governance authority.

**Complexity of the environment**

The role operates in a highly complex and decentralised international environment involving multiple governance and executive bodies, operational directorates, sections, finance stakeholders and strategic initiatives with intersecting priorities, timelines and resource implications. The role requires navigating ambiguity, influencing without formal authority, balancing strategic and operational considerations, and enabling collective choices where perspectives, incentives and institutional interests may differ. The position must synthesise diverse streams of information into coherent portfolio insight while supporting implementation discipline across a dynamic and evolving strategic cycle.

**SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE**

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse, including those detailed in the MSF Typologies of Abuse. When an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it, without investigating it, to protect others.

- Ensure respectful management and communication at all levels.
- Ensure that staff and consultants under their supervision understand their responsibilities regarding expected behaviour and reporting abuse while working for MSF.
- Welcome complainants, guide colleagues towards the appropriate channels without investigating, and promote a working environment that does not tolerate abuse or inappropriate behaviour.
- Ensure that staff know how to raise concerns and are kept informed of reporting mechanisms.

**REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- Master’s degree or equivalent professional competence in portfolio management, organisational strategy or public administration
- Advanced qualifications or certifications in portfolio, programme or change management are desirable.

**Experience**

- Significant MSF experience is mandatory.
- experience in complex international and multi-stakeholder environments;
- experience leading or coordinating strategic portfolios, organisational transformation initiatives or cross-functional governance processes;
- proven track record of designing and facilitating senior-level consultation, prioritisation and decision-making processes, including with executive committees or governance bodies;
- strong experience influencing senior stakeholders and driving alignment across decentralised structures without direct hierarchical authority.

**Knowledge**

- Understanding of portfolio, programme and change management approaches, governance models, organisational strategy and investment stewardship;
- understanding of complex organisational systems, prioritisation processes, accountability mechanisms and resource planning; familiarity with MSF’s movement dynamics, governance and executive environment, including the interaction between operational, strategic, financial and associative dimensions;
- demonstrated understanding of organisational interoperability, implementation risk, and cross-functional coordination in decentralised environments.

**Languages**

- C2 or excellent English level.
- French, Spanish or Arabic are assets.

**Other**

- Willingness and ability to travel regularly to MSF offices and operational contexts.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding and acceptance of these recruitment procedures.**

jobs.title: Coordinateur.trice Projet - Sud Est - Haïti - H/F
jobs.description:
## **ALIMA sur la base Sud Est Haïti**

ALIMA intervient en Haïti depuis février 2024 dans un contexte de crise politico sécuritaire majeure privant une grande partie de la population d’accès aux soins, en raison de déplacements forcés, de précarité économique ou de la fermeture/dysfonctionnement des structures de santé. ALIMA a déployé 4 cliniques mobiles couvrant 32 sites dans la zone métropolitaine de Port-au-Prince (communes de Delmas, Port-au-Prince, Cité Soleil, Pétion ville et Croix-de-bouquets) et appuie la réouverture progressive et la pleine fonctionnalité des structures sanitaires publiques (Chancerelles, CHAPI, Thomassin 25, Santo 17 et Corail Cesselesse et la maternité de Croix-de-bouquets), en partenariat avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population. Cette approche a permis de faciliter l’accès à un paquet intégré santé primaire/santé sexuelle et reproductive y compris la prise en charge de survivantes de violence sexuelle/santé mentale/Nutrition aux populations déplacées ou vulnérables. ALIMA poursuit et développe une approche communautaire à travers un soutien aux agents de santé communautaires polyvalents sur les sites cliniques mobiles et dans les structures sanitaires soutenues visant à assurer la promotion de la santé et à améliorer la demande des services de santé.

En 2025, face aux difficultés d’accès aux soins pour les femmes enceintes/allaitantes et enfants de moins de 5 ans ainsi que la déportation massive de populations haïtiennes à travers la porte d’entrée d’Anse-à-pitres dans le département du Sud-Est Haïti, ALIMA a étendu sa présence en Haiti en appuyant les centres de santé de Belle-Anse et Mapou (commune de Belle-Anse), les centres de santé de Jéricho, Platon-cèdre et le Centre hospitalier d’Anse-à-pitre (commune d’Anse-à-Pitres). L’objectif est de réduire la morbidité et la mortalité parmi les populations déplacées, déportées et hôtes, à travers trois axes d’intervention prioritaires :

- Amélioration de l’accès aux soins
- Prévention et traitement de la malnutrition
- Réponse rapide aux urgences

Priorités du projet:

Dans le contexte d’insécurité et d’instabilité des populations, donner accès aux soins de santé primaire, secondaire, préventifs, aux populations demande de la ﬂexibilité opérationnelle.

Le principal risque pris en compte est la violence armée, basé sur l’expérience des chocs antérieurs qu’a connu la région. Les principaux facteurs de crise du Sud-Est sont :

- Une forte pression migratoire, en raison des retours forcés de migrants haïtiens déportés de la République dominicaine et des déplacements internes dus m l’insécurité;
- Un système de santé souffrant d’une insuffisance critique des services de santé et d’un accès limité aux soins;
- La survenue des catastrophes naturelles (ouragan, inondations, tremblements de terre), les épidémies et la crise alimentaire).

## MISSION ET ACTIVITES PRINCIPALES

Sous la supervision du Chef de Mission, vous êtes responsable des interventions opérationnelles d’ALIMA dans le cadre du projet. En étroite collaboration avec l'équipe de la capitale, vous définissez les priorités et objectifs du projet et établit un plan pour atteindre ces derniers.

Pour y parvenir, vous examinez les données relatives à la santé de la population et aux besoins humanitaires, analysez le contexte, les questions humanitaires en jeu, ainsi que les risques et contraintes associées au contexte ; par la suite, vous évaluez les besoins en matière de ressources humaines et financières. De plus, vous coordonnez l'exécution du projet, en étroite collaboration avec le coordinateur médical et le chef de mission adjoint, afin d'assurer la réalisation effective des objectifs et aussi afin d'améliorer l'état de santé de la population ciblée ainsi que la situation humanitaire. Enfin, vous veillez au respect des procédures d’engagement des dépenses de ALIMA et du bailleur.

Vous êtes l’interface entre l’équipe de coordination et l’équipe de terrain que vous encadrez et représentez ALIMA auprès des interlocuteurs locaux. Vous êtes le garant sur le terrain des principes opérationnels d’Alima. Au travers des activités, vous les défendez, les appliquez et les diffusez. Vous supervisez et animez l'équipe de terrain et facilitez sa participation à la dynamique du projet.

Vos principales activités :

1. Analyse et gestion de la sécurité
2. Mise en œuvre des programmes
3. 1. Gestion et suivi du projet
2. Diagnostic et conception des projets
3. Mise en œuvre et suivi opérationnel
4. Analyse des données et reporting
5. Gestion des Ressources Humaines du projet
6. Représenter ALIMA sur sa zone d'intervention
7. Prévention contre les abus

## LIEU DU POSTE

Poste basé à Anse à Pitres (avec déplacements fréquent dans le département du Sud Est et possiblement sur tout le territoire haitien)

## LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES

- Sous la responsabilité du Chef de mission ALIMA, vous encadrez l’équipe du projet
- Votre équipe projet est composée d’un.e référent.e médical, d’un.e administrateur.trice, d’un.e Logisticien.ne projet, et d’un.e responsable de la qualité des soins Infirmiers (RSI).

## PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ

- Niveau 3: Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le ou la titulaire du poste sera amené·e à visiter les programmes et être en contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

## EXPERIENCES ET COMPETENCES

- Vous avez une expérience réussie au sein d'une ONGI médicale dans la gestion de projets et la supervision d'une équipe multiculturelle. Vous faites preuve d'une grande capacité de négociation et êtes capable de développer et d'entretenir un réseau efficace. Vous savez évoluer dans des contextes sécuritaires dégradés et/ou d’urgence (gestion des épidémies).
- Une connaissance approfondie des bailleurs de fonds humanitaires est un atout. Vous êtes à l'aise avec les outils informatiques (word, excel et internet). Vous encouragez le travail d’équipe, vous êtes orienté vers la résolution de problèmes et communiquez facilement.

LANGUES

- Bonne maîtrise du français (lu, écrit, parlé) indispensable
- La maîtrise de l’anglais , de l’espagnol ou du creole haitien est un atout

CONDITIONS

- Durée et type de contrat : CDD de droit français de 6 mois renouvelable.
- Prise de poste : ASAP
- Salaire : Selon grille salariale ALIMA + valorisation de l’expérience + Perdiem
- ALIMA prend en charge:
- Les frais de déplacements entre le pays d’origine de l’expatrié et le lieu de mission
- Les frais d’hébergement
- La couverture médicale du premier jour de contrat à un mois après la date de départ du pays de mission pour l’employé et ses ayants droits
- L’évacuation pour l’employé et ses ayants droits

jobs.title: Programme Development Officer
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Programme Development Officer

**Department:** Programme Support

**Division:** Programmes

**Duty Station:** Juba, South Sudan, with some travel within South Sudan and occasionally internationally

**Administrative Line Manager:** Programme Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Full-Time

**Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP)** envisions a worldwide culture of peace where conflicts within and between communities and nations are managed through nonviolent means. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through unarmed civilian protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

**JOB PURPOSE:**

The Programme Development Officer works with the entire country program team to support all stages of the project cycle to ensure compliance with donor regulations (including offering support to sub grantees to ensure their awareness of donor requirements), design projects and write proposals & reports, and represent NP in external engagements when needed.

**COMMITMENT TO NP PRINCIPLES**
All staff are expected to embody and actively work towards NP’s core principles in all aspects of their work:

1. **Nonviolence** in our approach, language, and actions.
2. **Direct Action** when engaging meaningfully with mandate goals.
3. **Radical Connection** through fostering safe, respectful, and inclusive relationships with communities, partners, and colleagues.
4. **Process-oriented** by abiding by NP's values, policies, and the Global Employee Handbook.
5. **Independence** by maintaining integrity in judgment and conduct.
6. **Nonpartisanship** by acting without bias or partisan influence.
7. **Redemption and Healing** by contributing to environments where accountability and growth are possible.
8. **Pluriversality** by embracing and protecting the diversity of all people NP works with and for.

**KEY OBJECTIVES/RESPONSIBILITIES:**
**I. Project Cycle Management:**

**a. Project Technical Design and Development**
• Support the South Sudan country team in identifying opportunities for project funding by tracking upcoming opportunities and those in the pipeline with an online, living document.
• Participate in context and other briefings led by the project and advocacy staff to help identify opportunities for programming which align with community needs/feedback, as well as NP’s strategic framework globally and in-country. Overlay with upcoming funding opportunities to support the team to prioritize where to place time and efforts and code switch between NP’s internal language and the language of donors.
• Lead the project design process in collaboration with project staff, holding ideation workshops when needed, and then synthesizing and articulating colleagues’ input into strong donor materials.
• Proposal development: Establish internal timelines and responsibilities for proposal development, taking the lead in drafting and reviewing, and liaising with other departments (such as Finance for budget development and Global Programme Development for technical support and overall quality assurance).

**b. Compliance**
• Hold ownership of official donor agreements in-country by reading through prior to signature, fully familiarizing with donor requirements, including reporting timeframes and templates, visibility requirements, disbursement schedules, audit and baseline/endline evaluation commitments, and other specific donor commitments. Collaborate across departments (finance, project, and global-based support colleagues) to raise concerns and identify solutions throughout the project cycle.
• Represent NP South Sudan in grants management meetings, taking the lead in preparing for inception meetings and in preparation for grants midterm and other grants related meetings.
• Participate in internal Budget vs Actual meetings to stay abreast of project developments and support colleagues to flag any concerns
related to compliance (ie related to budget category variance, identifying needs for NCEs, etc).

**c. External Facing Engagements**
• Work with the country management team to establish and maintain positive relationships with donors and potential donors, including acting as the focal point for donor relations in-country. Attend donor meetings alongside country management staff and contribute to project and context updates (in writing and in person) which reflect donor language, interests, and NP’s approach and strategic direction.
• Liaise with Program Manager in the cultivation of relationships with partners, whether civil society or international actors. Identify opportunities for formal and informal collaboration, including positioning NP as a subgrantee or consortium member.
• Represent NP South Sudan in partner meetings.

**d. Grants Management & Reporting**
• Maintain a timeline for reporting, identifying upcoming deadlines, and communicating with the relevant team members regarding their responsibilities and timeframes.
• Liaise with MEAL colleagues throughout the project cycle to ensure that the necessary data is being collected in line with donor commitments and NP’s Global MEAL Strategy, pre-emptively identifying and addressing any concerns with the relevant colleagues prior to any reporting deadline.
• Compile input into the correct templates, identify any technical inconsistencies or concerns, and to the extent possible address all concerns prior to sharing with Global Programme Development for review.
• Lead in drafting narrative donor reports and coordinating with the finance department to ensure that financial reports are submitted on time, in adherence with financial reporting requirements, and that they correspond to the narrative reports.
• Contribute to team-wide communications and knowledge management and participate in organization-wide events and discussions on related topics/projects.

**e. Other**
• Travel to field sites in order to enhance understanding of the context and programming for the purposes of developing proposals and reporting to/liaising with donors.
• Support programmatic input into relevant advocacy efforts, whether in-country or at a global level

**QUALIFICATIONS:**
**Required Qualifications**
**Experience**
• At least three (3) to five (5) years of project and grants management experience with a variety of bilateral donors
• Proven experience in grant management, including proposal development for institutional donors
• Experience in institutional donor compliance and familiarity with basic rules and regulations
• Track record of developing successful proposal packages, including narrative, log frames, and budgets
• Significant experience developing narrative donor reports under minimal supervision
• Experience tracking donor trends and opportunities.
• Knowledge of, or demonstrable interest in unarmed civilian protection, human security, violence reduction and/or peacebuilding (preference to candidates with strong familiarity of UCP and ability to differentiate UCP from broader protection and humanitarian language and framing).

**Context-specific**
• Experience implementing programmes in the field, ideally in humanitarian emergencies, and experience in South Sudan or the wider region a plus.

**Education**
• Relevant university degree in social sciences, international development, or related area of studies

**Skills:**
• Self-starter who can take the lead without prompting while also knowing when others need to be looped in/consulted.
• Ability to solve problems, analyse data, and prioritize a high workload with a flexible approach to changing environments.
• Ability to meet strict deadlines
• Attention to detail
• Creativity and innovation in generating new ideas and undertaking research
• Enthusiasm for learning and applying new skills
• Ability to work under pressure and in difficult conditions

**Interpersonal:**
• Ability to work effectively and diplomatically in a multi-cultural environment
• Ability to be a collaborative team player, willing to proactively help colleagues

**Languages and communication:**
• Fluency in written and spoken English, with excellent writing skills which do not require AI for formulation or editing.
• Knowledge of French is a plus.

**Information Technology:**
• Advanced skills in Microsoft Office applications.
• Experience with Salesforce is a plus.

jobs.title: Financial Controller - Haiti
jobs.description:
**About Us**
GOAL has responded to the world’s major humanitarian crises since its founding in 1977, working with vulnerable communities in 13 countries across the globe with a dedicated team of personnel. While GOAL continues to be an agile first-responder to humanitarian crises, it is also committed to working with vulnerable communities to help them survive crises and support them on the road to recovery.

**About Our Programme**
GOAL has been operating in Haiti since the country was devastated by a major earthquake in January 2010. We’re currently transitioning to a much longer-term programming approach linking relief and recovery to development through an integrated, community-led development

In Vanuatu, CARE focuses on gender equality, disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation and inclusive governance to support communities, especially women, to lead, decide and thrive.

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Senior Manager, Programs to lead CARE Vanuatu’s development and humanitarian portfolio, with accountability for program strategy, business development, program quality and partnership integration.

- **Lead and manage designated staff**, setting clear objectives, providing regular supervision and performance reviews, and addressing performance concerns.
- **Support emergency preparedness, response and recovery**, working with the Country Director to clarify and resource Emergency Preparedness Plan responsibilities and leading agreed program contributions.
- **Oversee program and partnership risks**, ensuring appropriate mitigation, clear decision thresholds and escalation to the Country Director, with risks held by those best placed to manage them.
