jobs.title: Human Resources Associate (Nationals only)
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, working in 177 countries and territories. UNDP opened its representative office in Ulaanbaatar in 1976 after more than a decade of successful cooperation with Mongolia. Ever since, UNDP has worked for equitable and sustainable development for the benefit of all Mongolians. UNDP is committed to helping the Government and the people of Mongolia achieve the Sustainable Development Goals as well as other national development priorities. UNDP's country programme is anchored in Mongolia's national priorities. From 2023-2027, the UN Country Team’s partnership with the Government of Mongolia will be guided by the new United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF).

UNDP is looking for a Human Resource Associate to support the HR function for the Country Office in Mongolia.

This assignment is intended to provide maternity leave cover.

Duties and Responsibilities

Ensure effective administration and implementation of HR strategies and policies.

• Ensure full compliance of records and reports with UN rules, regulations, and UNDP policies, procedures, and strategies; effective implementation of the internal controls; and proper functioning of the HR management system and practices.

• In consultation with the direct supervisor and office management, support CO HR business processes mapping, and provide input to content elaboration and update of internal HR Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) where needed in CO to supplement SOPs issued by GSSC/OHR. Adapt processes and procedures where necessary to meet the needs of CO.

• Provide information to management and personnel on the implementation of HR policies, corporate strategies, rules and regulations, HR business processes, and proper use of contractual modalities.

• Collect information and support to UNDP’s participation in inter-agency exercises and surveys, such as comprehensive and interim local salary survey, hardship, and place-to-place surveys, in coordination with the direct supervisor.

• Collect information on the risk management of Country Office HR activities to proactively manage and mitigate the risk.

Provide HR services to the UNDP CO and other UN agencies, including recruitment and staffing.

• Implement recruitment processes in coordination with GSSC and locally with Hiring Managers that includes drafting job descriptions, providing input to job classification process, drafting vacancy announcements, screening candidates, participating in interview panels, providing support for the submission of compliance reviews as per the actions delegated to the CO. In coordination with Hiring Managers, submit requests and appropriate documentation to GSSC for non-delegated actions.

• Facilitate creation and update of positions in ERP (or create positions if delegated) and association and update of positions to chart fields, in coordination with budget owners.

• Follow up with Finance staff and GSSC on Global Payroll issues.

• Monitor and track all transactions related to positions, recruitment, benefits, earnings/deductions, retroactivities, recoveries, adjustments, and separations through ERP and other relevant corporate platforms.

• Process timely contract management actions, in close coordination with supervisors and senior management.

• Provide support to process benefits and entitlements delegated to the CO, as applicable and in coordination with the direct supervisor and management, such as medical evacuations, R&R, safety and security interventions.

• Maintain CO staffing table and local rosters where relevant.

• Validate cost-recovery charges in ERP for HR services provided by UNDP to other Agencies.

• Provide assistance to the contract management, payroll, and separations in coordination with GSSC in accordance with the delegation of authority given to the CO.

• Provide HR support and services to the UN system, including provision of information on personnel benefits and entitlements to UN agencies in line with UNDP policies and in coordination with GSSC as applicable.

• Provide administrative support to retirees as applicable.

Ensure proper staff performance management, talent management and career development in CO.

• Provide background information and maintain related data acting as Secretary to formal CO management groups responsible for collectively reviewing and discussing CO staff performance, talent, and development needs.

• Provide assistance to Performance Management reporting and monitoring.

• Provide input to the CO-wide Learning plan’s preparation in consultation with the Senior Management.

Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO.

• Organize training for the Operations and projects staff on HR issues.

• Assist in the creation and implementation of a local onboarding plan, leveraging corporate resources.

• Synthesize lessons learned and best practices in HR.

• Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Operations Manager, the HR Associate ensures execution of transparent and efficient HR services in the CO. The HR Associate promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach and supports the maintenance of high staff morale.

The HR Associate may supervise and lead clerical and support staff in the HR Unit. The HR Associate works in close collaboration with the Programme, Operations, and project teams in the CO, UNDP HQ OHR Business Partners, and staff in GSSC and other UN Agencies to exchange information and resolve complex HR-related issues.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

- Knowledge Facilitation Ability to animate individuals and communities of contributors to participate and share, particularly externally

Business Management

- Operations Management Ability to effectively plan, organize, and oversee the Organization’s business processes in order to convert its assets into the best results in the most efficient manner. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms

- Working with Evidence and Data Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

Knowledge of and ability to design benefits-related processes, programmes, and tools, including benefit enrolment and amendments

Required Skills and Experience

Experience:

- Minimum of 6 years (with high school diploma) or 3 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible HR and/or administrative experience at the national or international level is required.

jobs.title: Governance Intern (Nationals only)
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) works with governments, civil society, the private sector, and communities to advance inclusive and sustainable development. In Mongolia, UNDP supports efforts to strengthen democratic governance, improve public sector effectiveness, promote transparency and accountability, and expand opportunities for meaningful citizen participation.

The Governance Portfolio contributes to these efforts through initiatives focused on democratic governance, anti-corruption, digital transformation, civic engagement, youth participation, and inclusive public service delivery. Working closely with government institutions, Parliament, civil society organizations, development partners, academia, and youth networks, the portfolio supports innovative and people-centered approaches to governance and sustainable development.

The Governance Intern will support the implementation of activities across the Governance Portfolio through programme implementation, communications and outreach, research, knowledge management, and administrative assistance. This includes support to Youth Co:Lab Mongolia, part of the regional Youth Co:Lab initiative co-created by UNDP and the Citi Foundation, which supports young people to lead social innovation and entrepreneurship for the SDGs through innovation challenges, capacity building and youth policy dialogue. The internship offers an opportunity to gain practical experience in development programming, strengthen professional skills, and contribute to initiatives that advance inclusive governance and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Mongolia.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall guidance and supervision of the Programme Analyst for Governance Portfolio, the intern is expected to provide day-to-day support to the Governance Portfolio team. Summary of key functions are as follows:

- Support the implementation of Governance Portfolio projects and activities, including Youth Co:Lab Mongolia innovation challenges, capacity-building programmes for young social entrepreneurs, and youth dialogues.

- Prepare communications and knowledge products for the portfolio, including social media content, visual materials, presentations, and short articles, in line with UNDP branding and communications guidelines.

- Conduct desk research and compile information on governance, youth participation, and social innovation topics.

- Support the preparation of background notes, concept notes, briefing materials, presentations, and reports.

- Assist with data collection, organization, and analysis, including participant surveys and feedback, to support project implementation.

- Support coordination and outreach with government institutions, development partners, civil society organizations, academia, the private sector, and youth networks, including through digital channels.

- Assist in organizing meetings, workshops, trainings, seminars, and other portfolio events, including logistical and stakeholder coordination.

- Maintain project documentation, stakeholder databases, and communication records.

- Support administrative and operational processes, including payment processing and related follow-up actions.

- Assist with travel arrangements, including travel authorizations, ticket bookings, hotel reservations, and DSA calculations.

- Provide general programme, coordination, and administrative support as required by the supervisor.

- Perform other related tasks as assigned by the supervisor.

Competencies

Core Values: Respect for Diversity, Integrity, and Professionalism

Core Competencies:

- Excellent interpersonal, communication and organizational skills;

- Ability to follow up immediately and facilitates solutions to challenges and attention to details;

- Ability to focus on a variety of tasks within deadlines and to work under time pressure;

- Strong work ethics and commitment;

- Team player organized and resourceful;

- Ability to work as part of a team in an international and multicultural environment.

Required Skills and Qualifications

Education:

Candidates must meet one of the following educational requirements:

- Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as a master’s programme, or higher);

- Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent);

- Have recently graduated with a university degree (as defined in (a) and (b) above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation;

- Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship program and undertake the internship as part of this program.

Field of study:

Social sciences, International Relations or International Studies, Public Administration, Business Management, Communications, Media or Design, and/or other relevant fields.

Experience

Applicants are not required to have professional work experience but experience working in operations and administrative areas is highly desired.

Other:

Volunteering, research, student projects or other extracurricular activities that demonstrate interest in international development, youth engagement or social innovation (e.g., gender equality, human rights, civic participation); and/or practical skills in communications, social media, graphic design, event coordination, or administrative and operational processes.

Language:

- Excellent command of English and Mongolian, both oral and written, is required.

Internship Conditions:

- This internship assignment can also be completed as part of national service obligations or a postgraduate professional traineeship program.

- UNDP will provide a stipend in the monthly amount of USD 223.07 (in-person rate) in accordance with the provisions of the UNDP Internship policy. Except for the stipend, all other expenses connected with the internship will be borne by the intern or her/his sponsoring entity.

- Interns are expected to work full time, but flexibility is allowed for education programmes;

- Interns are not eligible to apply for, or be appointed to, any post in UNDP during the period of the internship;

- Interns are not considered staff members and may not represent UNDP in any official capacity;

- Selected Interns must be able to share proof of education enrolment and/ or graduation, medical/ health and life/accident insurance, valid for the location in which the internship will be carried out and be able to provide insurance documentary proof at the time of their selection;

jobs.title: Analista Proyecto en Cadenas de Valor (Presencial para Tegucigalpa) [Abierto a candidatos internos y externos]
jobs.description:
Enfoque por niveles

En línea con el compromiso de salvaguardar la capacidad y apoyar al personal ya existente en la Organización, la mayoría de las vacantes de PNUD/UNCDF/UNV se publican utilizando un proceso de postulación por niveles, mediante el cual:

• Nivel 0: Personal internacional del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos séran abolidos, o cuyos contratos serán rescindidos o no renovados durante el año 2026

• Nivel 1: Otro personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA)

• Nivel 2: Personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares y Voluntarios Expertos y Especialistas de las Naciones Unidas

• Nivel 3 o sin nivel indicado: Todos los demás tipos de contratos del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU y de otros organismos, y demás candidatos externos

Por favor, tome nota del(los) nivel(es) indicado(s) en el título de la vacante, si corresponde, y asegúrese de cumplir con los requisitos de elegibilidad para postular.

Descripción de la oficina/unidad/proyecto:

El PNUD en Honduras facilita el acceso a asesorías en políticas, finanzas y programas para crear soluciones innovadoras y audaces que aceleren los esfuerzos nacionales para abordar los complejos desafíos del desarrollo. Emplea un enfoque integrador, involucrando activamente y forjando alianzas con diversos actores en la sociedad comprometidos con los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible y el bienestar del país.

El PNUD está presente en unos 170 países y territorios, ofrece una perspectiva global y un conocimiento local. La ventaja comparativa del PNUD en la implementación de proyectos consiste en el aseguramiento de una ejecución presupuestaria (fondos nacionales, préstamos y donaciones, etc.) rápida, eficaz y transparente, con uso eficiente de los recursos, al mismo tiempo que desarrollan y fortalece capacidades en las instituciones de gobierno. El PNUD tiene una capacidad probada de gestión basada en la obtención de resultados, y de transferencia de conocimientos con un expertise de nivel mundial.

La Unidad de Crecimiento Inclusivo del PNUD Honduras forma parte del área de Prosperidad para Todas las Personas y Crecimiento Inclusivo, promoviendo iniciativas orientadas a reducir desigualdades mediante la generación de oportunidades económicas sostenibles, fortalecimiento institucional y mejora de los servicios públicos.

En este contexto, el proyecto Honduras Crece Sostenible busca fortalecer las capacidades institucionales de la Secretaría de Desarrollo Económico (SDE) para mejorar la competitividad, impulsar la transformación productiva y fortalecer el ecosistema empresarial. El proyecto contempla actividades de fortalecimiento institucional, estudios, consultorías, eventos, capacitaciones, mesas de diálogo, cadenas de valor y mecanismos de competitividad que requieren una gestión administrativa, documental y logística eficiente

Alcance del trabajo

Objetivo:

Contribuir técnica y estratégicamente al fortalecimiento de cadenas de valor prioritarias, promoviendo la articulación público-privada, la competitividad, la productividad y la inclusión económica de mujeres y jóvenes.

El/la candidato/a seleccionado/a para esta asignación tendrá las siguientes tareas a cumplir:

1. Co - Liderar la planificación y coordinación técnica de las iniciativas asignadas:

a. Coordinar técnicamente la implementación de las intervenciones piloto en cadenas de valor priorizadas por el proyecto.

b. Redactar reportes de alta calidad con la periodicidad que requieran las iniciativas asignadas.

c. Incorporar transversalmente enfoques de género, juventudes, sostenibilidad, inclusión económica y trabajo decente.

d. Gestionar el desempeño del personal asignado a su cargo, desarrollando evaluaciones periódicas y acompañando la construcción de capacidades de capacidades.

e. Supervisar la ejecución presupuestaria, el cumplimiento de metas y la gestión de riesgos de los componentes e iniciativas bajo su responsabilidad.

2. Contribuir a la gestión de las partes interesadas en las iniciativas asignadas.

a. Apoyar el establecimiento y funcionamiento de mesas sectoriales y mecanismos de diálogo público-privado.

b. Brindar asistencia técnica a actores públicos, privados y organizaciones empresariales participantes.

c. Mantener relaciones colaborativas con las contrapartes o interesados clave en la implementación de las iniciativas.

d. Apoyar en la organización y ejecución de reuniones técnicas periódicas y talleres con socios y contrapartes gubernamentales y otros.

3. Contribuir a la gestión administrativa, financiera y adquisiciones de las iniciativas asignadas.

a. Redactar términos de referencia y liderar el desempeño de consultorías relacionadas con las iniciativas asignadas.

b. Coordinar estudios especializados y actividades de fortalecimiento de capacidades vinculadas con las iniciativas bajo su responsabilidad.

c. Participar como especialista técnico en comisiones de evaluación, que permita la adjudicación de contratos.

d. Acompañar en el seguimiento de contratos adjudicados en las iniciativas asignada.

4. Facilitar el desarrollo de conocimientos y capacidades, y el intercambio de conocimientos.

a. Identificar oportunidades de agregación de valor, innovación, diversificación productiva y acceso a mercados.

b. Elaborar análisis, estudios, diagnósticos y propuestas técnicas para fortalecer cadenas de valor estratégicas.

c. Dar seguimiento a indicadores, resultados y lecciones aprendidas de las intervenciones productivas.

d. Apoyar la generación de evidencia, casos de éxito y productos de conocimiento.

e. Identificar, sintetizar y documentar las mejores prácticas y las lecciones aprendidas que se generen a partir del proyecto y de los socios ejecutores.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente del PNUD.

Acuerdo Institucional

El/la candidato/a seleccionado/ha seleccionado/a reportará directamente a la coordinación del proyecto.

Competencias

Lograr Resultados:

Nivel 2: Escala soluciones y simplifica procesos, alcanza un balance entre rapidez y precisión al hacer el trabajo.

Pensar Innovadoramente:

Nivel 2: Ofrece nuevas ideas/tiene apertura a nuevas aproximaciones, demuestra pensamiento sistémico/integrado.

Aprender Continuamente:

Nivel 2: Sale de la zona de confort, aprende de los demás y apoya su aprendizaje.

Adaptarse con Agilidad:

Nivel 2: Adapta procesos/aproximaciones a nuevas situaciones, involucra otros en el proceso de cambio.

Actuar con Determinación:

Nivel 2: Capaz de perseverar y lidiar simultáneamente con múltiples fuentes de presión.

Comprometerse y Asociarse:

Nivel 2: Es un facilitador/integrador, une a las personas, construye/mantiene coaliciones/alianzas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión:

Nivel 2: Facilita conversaciones para concertar diferencias, considera opiniones en el proceso de toma de decisiones.

Competencias técnicas y multifuncionales

Gestión Institucional - Gestión basada en los resultados:

• Capacidad para gestionar la puesta en marcha de estrategias, programas y proyectos que se centren en la mejora del rendimiento y los resultados demostrables. Conocimiento y comprensión de las teorías, los conceptos, las metodologías, los instrumentos y las herramientas relevantes.

Gestión de asociaciones - Movilización de recursos:

• Capacidad para identificar fuentes de financiación, emparejar las necesidades (tales como programas, proyectos, o iniciativas) con las oportunidades de financiación y establecer un plan para satisfacer los requisitos de financiación.

Finanzas - Planificación financiera y presupuestación:

• Capacidad para poner en marcha y gestionar procesos que ayuden a lograr los objetivos financieros del PNUD a largo y corto plazo, mediante la planificación, la presupuestación, la previsión, el análisis y la presentación de informes.

Agenda 2030: Compromiso y eficacia - Innovación:

• Monitoreo, evaluación y aprendizaje para carteras de proyectos

Agenda 2030: Personal - Género:

• Gestión del conocimiento y aprendizaje sobre igualdad de género

Requisitos mínimos para el NPSA

Requisitos mínimos de educación

• Título universitario de nivel avanzado (Maestría o equivalente) en Economía, Desarrollo Económico, Agronegocios, Competitividad, Desarrollo Empresarial, Ingeniería Industrial, Administración de Empresas o áreas afines es requisito, o

• Título universitario de primer nivel (Licenciatura) en las áreas anteriores, en combinación con dos (2) años adicionales de experiencia relevante, se dará debida consideración en lugar de una Maestría.

Años mínimos de experiencia laboral relevante

• Los aplicantes con título de maestría (o equivalente) en un campo de estudio relevante no necesitan tener experiencia laboral profesional. Los aplicantes con título de licenciatura (o equivalente) deben tener mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia profesional relevante en procesos relacionados con el impulso y liderazgo en cadenas de valor, articulando los diferentes actores a los eslabones de dichas cadenas.

Habilidades deseables

• Experiencia en análisis y fortalecimiento de cadenas de valor, desarrollo productivo o competitividad.

• Experiencia trabajando con sector privado, MIPYMES, cámaras empresariales o asociaciones productivas.

• Experiencia en formulación de diagnósticos, estudios económicos o análisis sectoriales.

• Experiencia en coordinación interinstitucional y facilitación de espacios multi actor.

• Experiencia aplicando enfoques de género, inclusión económica y desarrollo sostenible.

• Experiencia en proyectos de cooperación internacional o desarrollo.

Idioma(s) requerido(s)

• Fluidez en español es requerido.

• Conocimiento técnico de inglés es requisito

Igualdad de Oportunidades

Como empleador que ofrece igualdad de oportunidades, el PNUD valora la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y de las culturas en las que operamos y, como tal, invitamos a todo/as los/las candidato/as calificado/as de diferentes orígenes a aplicar a los diferentes roles en nuestra organización. Nuestras decisiones de empleo están basadas en el mérito y la idoneidad para el puesto, sin discriminación alguna.

El PNUD también está comprometido con la creación de un ambiente laboral inclusivo donde todo el personal esté empoderado para contribuir a nuestra misión, sea valorado, pueda prosperar y se beneficie de oportunidades laborales abiertas a todo/as.

Acoso sexual, explotación y abuso de autoridad

El PNUD no tolera el acoso, acoso sexual, explotación, discriminación y abuso de autoridad. Por lo tanto, todo/as los/las candidato/as seleccionado/as, pasan por verificaciones exhaustivas y se espera que se adhieran a los respectivos estándares y principios.

Derecho a seleccionar múltiples candidato/as

El PNUD se reserva el derecho de seleccionar uno/a o más candidato/as a partir de este anuncio de vacante. También podremos conservar las aplicaciones y considerar a los/las candidato/as que apliquen a este puesto para otros puestos similares en el PNUD con el mismo nivel y con descripciones de puesto, requisitos de experiencia y formación académicas similares.

Uso de IA por parte de los candidatos

Se invita a los postulantes a leer la guía del PNUD para candidatos sobre el uso responsable de inteligencia artificial en los procesos de reclutamiento y selección del PNUD.

Alerta de estafa

El PNUD no cobra ninguna tarifa en ninguna etapa de sus procesos de reclutamiento. Para mayor información, visite www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Communications Intern (Roster, Nationals Only)
jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

As the United Nations lead agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities, and to build resilience to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Our work is concentrated in three focus areas; sustainable development, democratic governance and peace building, and climate and disaster resilience. UNDP advocates for change, and connects countries to global knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life.

UNDP has supported Kyrgyzstan’s development progress since 1992 and supports the country in charting future pathways towards greater prosperity, resilience, and social cohesion. As an impartial policy advisor and integrator, UNDP works within the UN system and with all stakeholders in government, civil society, and private sector to advance inclusive, fundamentally sound development solutions and reforms in complex settings. Our United Nations identity ensures neutrality and respect for people’s choices. Transparency and accountability in operations makes us a trusted partner for national and international development stakeholders.

UNDP encourages and enables collective intelligence, collaboration, integration, critical thinking, and thought leadership. We mainstream innovation, digitalization opportunities, gender equity and diversity/inclusion principles in all aspects of our work. Our staff consistently strive for excellence, effectiveness, efficiency and inclusion across all areas of work.

Duties and Responsibilities

- Technical support: • Support for technical production of communication and advocacy materials and tools for UNDP projects; • Design communications products for social media channels: • Promote and strengthen UNDP’s presence in social media network; • Support with carrying out public events related to projects implementation; • Support with development and coordination of the production of weekly communications plans.

- Visual content production • Assist the team with providing high-quality writing/editing/proofreading social media content and conducting digital outreach in Kyrgyz/Russian and English; • Assist with producing video reels on UNDP key topics in simple way tailored for different social media platforms; • Assist with production of photo essays for UNDP key areas of work; • Contribute to writingstories, articles, blogs, and press releases in English and Kyrgyz/Russian languages.

Perform other duties within your functional profile as assigned and deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the office.

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Communications Officer, the Intern delivers client-focused services in the area of communications. The Intern works in close partnership with UNDP CO Communications Unit, Project Specialists.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Applicants to the UNDP internship programme must at the time of application meet one of the following requirements:

(a) Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme in Media, Communications, Journalism, and Public Relations departments; (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent);

(b) Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as a master’s programme, or higher) in Media, Communications, Journalism, and Public Relations departments;

(c) Have recently graduated with a university degree (as defined in (a) and (b) above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation;

(d) Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship program and undertake the internship as part of this program.

Experience:

- Experience of producing video reels and taking photos is strongly desired (please enclose links to published videos, photos);

- Experience of design is considered as an asset (please enclose links to published designs);

- Experience of using of AI for visual production is an asset (please enclose links to the published works);

- Experience of writing texts is strongly desired (please enclose writing samples);

- Knowledge of English, Russian, and Kyrgyz at the proficient level is required.

Working arrangements:

- UNDP will not be able to sponsor visas / work permits and travel to and from duty station of this internship assignment (Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic).

- The intern should be based in Bishkek throughout the whole duration of the assignment.

- The intern will receive a monthly stipend.

- Internship is full-time, office-based.

- UNDP will not be able to provide personal computer/laptop and other computer equipment.

- Usual working hours at UNDP Country Office are from 9.00 to 18.00.

Disclaimer

Applicant information about UNDP rosters

Note: UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

jobs.title: Asociado(a) de Proyecto en Monitoreo Estratégico y Gestión del Conocimiento para Proyectos de Desarrollo
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de la Coordinación del Proyecto Sinergia+ para fortificar el monitoreo estratégico y la gestión integral del Proyecto, mediante el análisis y seguimiento de los avances, resultados e indicadores establecidos en la Matriz de Resultados y el Documento de Proyecto (PRODOC); la identificación de riesgos y oportunidades de mejora, así como la integración de informes, generando información que fortalezca la toma de decisiones basada en evidencia, la rendición de cuentas y la visibilidad de los resultados e impactos alcanzados por la CONANP y el PNUD en materia de conservación, desarrollo sostenible y gobernanza ambiental.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 6 “Proyectos Estratégicos”

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Asesorar en la planeación e implementación de herramientas que permitan mejorar y hacer más eficiente el se-guimiento y cumplimiento puntual al Programa Operativo Anual.

- Diseñar y coordinar la estrategia y acciones específicas para consolidar la integración de los entregables (medios de verificación), reportes e indicadores definidos en la matriz de resultados del proyecto, PRODOC, así como cola-borar en la integración de los informes de medio término y finales que tenga que reportar el proyecto.

- Establecer y conducir estrategias y acciones específicas para consolidar la integración de los entregables (medios de verificación).

- Analizar y sistematizar la información e insumos disponibles para consolidar la integración de los entregables e informes.

- Coordinar y supervisar el seguimiento a las actividades de las y los colaboradores, asegurando su vinculación con la Matriz de Resultados.

- Consolidar y validar la integración de los indicadores requeridos en la Matriz de Resultados.

- Revisar y emitir recomendaciones técnicas sobre la documentación generada en el y para el Proyecto (lineamien-tos, términos de referencia, entre otros).

- Articular y facilitar la comunicación y coordinación entre consultores, equipo técnico y áreas involucradas.

- Identificar, formular y promover propuestas de mejora en los procesos de seguimiento y elaboración de reportes de monitoreo.

- Identificar, analizar y dar seguimiento a los riesgos que puedan afectar el cumplimiento de los resultados del Proyecto, manteniendo actualizado el registro de riesgos y las correspondientes medidas de mitigación.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El o la persona contratada trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica del/la Coordinador(a) General del Proyecto.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Certificado de Preparatoria/Bachillerato, es requisito.

- Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura en: Ciencias Ambientales, Gestión Ambiental, Turismo, Turismo Sustentable, Biología y afines, no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos/as con certificado de preparatoria/bachillerato se requieren 7 años de experiencia comprobable en gestión, análisis y sistematización de información e indicadores; y gestión de proyectos vinculados con la conservación, manejo y operación de Áreas Naturales Protegidas, incluyendo coordinación interinstitucional y trabajo con equipos multidisciplinarios.

- Para candidatos/as con Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura, se requiere 4 años de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en: Elaboración de informes de calidad.

Habilidades Deseadas:

•Conocimiento / Experiencia en: conservación de la biodiversidad y gestión de Áreas Naturales Protegidas.

•Conocimiento / Experiencia en: elaboración y análisis de indicadores, matrices de resultados y medios de verificación.

•Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Identificación y gestión de riesgos, así como medidas de mitigación de proyectos.

•Conocimiento / Experiencia en: métodos y herramientas de monitoreo y evaluación de proyectos.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Waste Management Specialist (Greening Moonshot) - Home Based - [Open to all applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Job Purpose and Organizational Context

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The UNDP Strategic Plan underscores the organization’s dual imperative to deliver development results with greater efficiency and value for money, while leading by example on sustainability, climate action, and responsible resource use.

Within this context, UNDP has committed to continuously improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and environmental performance of its operations, recognizing that internal operational practices directly affect institutional credibility, partner trust, and staff engagement. The Strategic Plan highlights the need to modernize management practices, strengthen data-driven decision-making, reduce waste and inefficiencies, and align operational systems with UNDP’s broader climate and environmental ambitions.

The Greening Moonshot Initiative, hosted by Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) in collaboration with the Bureau for Management Services (BMS), is UNDP’s flagship, inward-facing transformation effort to reduce the environmental footprint of corporate operations. Through the Greening Moonshot, UNDP has committed to significantly reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving resource efficiency, and adopting best practices across energy use, procurement, mobility, buildings, and waste management. The initiative is overseen by the Moonshot Task Force and supported by a dedicated Moonshot Secretariat.

Waste management is a highly visible and material component of UNDP’s operational sustainability agenda. As a leading development actor working extensively on waste, circular economy, chemicals, and pollution issues at the country level, UNDP is expected to “walk the talk” by applying the same principles internally. At the same time, sound waste management and resource efficiency practices are increasingly recognized as cost‑reduction and efficiency levers.

The Waste Management Specialist position is associated with the Greening Moonshot team and is designed to strengthen UNDP’s capacity to provide coherent corporate guidance, practical tools, monitoring approaches, and strategic recommendations that support offices worldwide in improving waste management performance in a cost‑effective, context‑sensitive manner.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Waste Management Specialist will support the design, rollout, and continuous improvement of UNDP’s corporate approach to waste management and resource efficiency. The assignment balances technical rigor, operational practicality, and cost‑effectiveness, in line with UNDP’s Strategic Plan and Greening Moonshot commitments.

- Develop and improve corporate waste management guidance and tools Continuously improve and maintain waste management guidance for UNDP offices, covering both non‑hazardous and hazardous waste streams, process to limit waste generation and to assist in designing office-specific strategies. Guidance should reflect sectoral best practices, regional feasibility constraints, and life‑cycle cost considerations, and support offices in making efficient, defensible operational decisions. Tools to be developed by the Waste Management Specialist should leverage advancements in automation, AI and digital solutions to maximize the availability, ease of use and impact of advice and guidance generated for UNDP.

2. Monitoring, data quality, and efficiency improvements

- Guide and support the integration of waste management considerations into UNDP’s environmental monitoring and reporting systems, including the Environmental Management Tool (EMT).

- Develop training materials, deliver webinars, and provide targeted support to focal points to improve data quality, consistency, and usability for management decision‑making.

- Provide on-going support to monitoring and reporting efforts by facilities and COs, assist in developing, testing and maintaining assumptions and calculations to generate valuable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

- In the context of UNDP’s Scope 3 Strategy, develop assessment methodologies, coordinate EMT programming and support data collection for project end-of-life waste impacts and support development of subsequent management guidance.

3. Provision of corporate recommendations and strategic alignment

- Based on EMT data, consultations with Country Offices, and engagement with technical networks, develop evidence‑based recommendations for corporate‑level actions that improve waste management outcomes while reducing operational inefficiencies and avoidable costs.

- Prepare briefing materials to support senior management endorsement and strategic decision‑making. Support the development and change management aspects of the Waste Management and Resource Efficiency Strategy.

4. Promote staff engagement

- Guide and support the organization‑wide roll‑out of waste management initiatives through clear communications, consultations with Country Offices, and documentation of lessons learned.

- Practical implementation, peer learning, and solutions that balance ambition with feasibility.

- Organize and lead regular webinars and technical-level discussions. Provide bilateral helpdesk support to Country Offices, Regional Hubs and Headquarters as needed.

5. Support to the greening moonshot secretariat

- Contribute to other Greening Moonshot activities as required, including coordination with procurement, facilities, IT, and programme teams to ensure alignment between operational sustainability objectives, efficiency gains, and UNDP’s broader climate and development commitments.

- Apply a pragmatic, solutions‑oriented approach that strengthens UNDP’s leadership on sustainable operations while recognizing the diversity of operational contexts across regions and offices.

6. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing

- Identify capacity building needs and opportunities.

- Ensure appropriate training, project workshops and other relevant activities are organized and implemented in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Waste Management Specialist will work under the guidance of the BMS and BPPS Moonshot Secretariat Managers and report directly to the Moonshot Secretariat Coordinator. The candidate will be responsible for the fulfilment of the duties and responsibilities specified above.

The incumbent will work from home and will be given access to relevant information necessary for execution of the tasks under this assignment. The incumbent will be responsible for providing his/her own working station (i.e., laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, etc.) and must have reliable internet connection. The incumbent will engage virtually with the supervisor and/or the team on a regular basis. Given the global scope of the work undertaken during this assignment, the incumbent is expected to be reasonably flexible with his/her availability taking into consideration different time zones.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area

Name

Definition

External Relations and Advocacy

Communication

Communicate in a clear, concise and

unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the

audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social

media and other appropriate channels

Business Direction and Strategy

System Thinking

Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element

can impact on other parts of the system

Business Direction and Strategy

Effective Decision Making

Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one's authority, area of expertise and resources and take into consideration potential wider implications.

Business Management

Project Management

Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve

specific goals

Business Management

Working with Evidence and Data

Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making

Business Development

Knowledge Generation

Background

The UNDP Country Office success in its delivery of UNDP programmes is dependent on ensuring an adequate security framework is in place. The Host Government has primary responsibility for the security and protection of personnel employed by United Nations Security Management System organizations, their eligible family members, and property.

The UN House Security Team provides security coverage for UN House personnel, visitors, premises and assets, including 24/7 coverage of designated security posts and daytime coverage during UN House working hours.

Position Purpose

This position serves a dual function, supporting both the UN House/Common Services security arrangements, while also supporting UNDP's broader operational and programmatic objectives.

Under the guidance and supervision of the UNDP Operations Manager, the UNDP- UN House Security Associate supports the activity of the UN House Security Team and provides reliable security services for UN House Agencies. The assignment will include supporting the security arrangement with an outsourced security service, including preparation of technical requirements, technical support to related procurement process and monitoring of contractor performance. Further to support UNDP as required in the implementation of security and safety management in Moldova

The incumbent will work in close coordination with the UN House Management Committee, UNDP Procurement and other relevant functions for the outsourced security services transition and contract implementation. He/she will also work in close coordination with the UNDSS Security Associate for technical security guidance on UN House related matters as well as with UNDP Security Office, through the RSA/SRSS for technical guidance on UNDP related security matters.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Performance monitoring of the security company (Guards team):

- Monitor and coordinate the outsourced security services, aimed at ensuring uninterrupted security coverage of UN House.

- Support induction and briefing of the selected company’s deployed personnel on UN House security procedures, access control arrangements, control-center functions, CCTV and access-control systems, fire and emergency procedures, incident reporting requirements, confidentiality and standards of conduct.

- Draft and/or coordinate post instructions, relevant SOPs, logbooks, access arrangements and operational information required for the UN House security service.

- Check, against contractual requirements, that deployed contractor personnel meet the required qualifications, training and documentation requirements and that the contractor has the required staffing/replacement arrangements in place.

- Monitor service delivery against the contract, technical specifications and agreed KPIs, including staffing levels, attendance, post coverage, response to incidents, reporting, replacement arrangements and compliance with UN House security procedures.

- Maintain regular operational communication with the contractor’s designated supervisor/team leader and promptly escalate performance gaps, security incidents or non-compliance with the UNDP Operations Manager, with technical coordination with UNDSS as appropriate.

- Monitor the performance and conduct of Security Guards and ensure compliance with applicable SOPs and security instructions and support follow-up on corrective actions and prepare periodic performance observations/reports as required.

- Support verification that the contractor operates in accordance with applicable Moldovan legislation and contractual obligations, while referring legal or contractual compliance issues to the responsible UNDP functions for determination.

Monitor the Access Control and Control Center:

- Control admission of authorized personnel and movement of United Nations property into and out of the premises.

- Ensure that unauthorized personnel and prohibited items do not gain access to UN House facilities.

- Conduct patrols and physical security checks of the compound, offices, perimeter and parking areas, and report irregularities.

- Use relevant technical screening and access-control equipment and maintain control of the emergency key system and related records.

- Maintain and/or supervise operation of the security control center.

- Prepare, print, issue, activate/deactivate and replace UN House access cards for personnel, as required, and maintain accurate records of cards issued, returned, lost, damaged or cancelled.

- Monitor and control, as applicable, the UN House Emergency Line and Panic Button, video surveillance system, fire safety and suppression system, electronic door locking/access-control system and VHF working channel.

- Ensure familiarity with and compliance with established procedures for operation of security systems.

Assist in supporting CO in Emergency Response:

- Act as a support response during emergencies or security incidents and promptly report to the designated supervisors.

- Be familiar with emergency procedures, Security Standard Operating Procedures and contingency plans and support their implementation.

- Know how to use firefighting equipment and support emergency response measures on the premises.

- Respond to emergencies affecting the safety and security of UN House personnel, visitors, assets and facilities in accordance with authorized procedures.

Overall security support to UNDP management and personnel:

- Provide support in keeping UNDP management informed of security matters affecting UNDP programmes and its personnel.

- Assist in implementing the Country Security Plan, Contingency Plans, and Business Continuity Management.

- Provide support to the UNDP Operations Manager on implementation of relevant security arrangements, including Warden System support, maps, security routes and related documents, as requested.

- Gather information for inclusion in Country Office security reports;

- Respond to and assist in reporting safety and security incidents affecting UNDP personnel and eligible dependents by gathering and verifying security information relevant to analyzing the situation;

- Maintain information of UNDP security contact details;

- Assist UNDP OM with the preparation and updating security aspects of procedures for dealing with emergencies involving UNDP staff and operations;

- Provide support in organizing training courses on security awareness and preparedness for UNDP personnel and provide security briefings to newly recruited employees;

- Assist UNDP OM during emergencies, incidents and security-related events;

- Monitoring news/information with potential impact on the security environment through different external and internal sources and providing information to OM on possible effects to UNDP personnel, programs and assets;

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

jobs.description:

Background

Viet Nam is entering a new phase of accelerated development, building on more than three decades of sustained economic growth and improvements in human development. The country aspires to achieve high-income status by 2045 and net-zero emissions by 2050, while accelerating modernization, digital transformation and innovation-led growth. Viet Nam’s Human Development Index reached 0.766 in 2023, placing the country in the high human development category, while multidimensional poverty declined from 4.4 per cent in 2021 to 1.3 per cent in 2025.

Despite this progress, structural and spatial inequalities persist. Ethnic minorities, older persons, persons with disabilities, unregistered internal migrants, women and young people continue to face unequal access to services, productive assets, decent work, finance and economic opportunities. Women remain disproportionately represented in informal and vulnerable employment, while youth unemployment is more than three times the national rate. Rapid population ageing, evolving labour-market demands and uneven access to digital skills create additional challenges for inclusive transformation.

Private-sector development is central to Viet Nam’s future growth. The private sector generates 82 per cent of jobs and contributes approximately half of gross domestic product. More than 97 per cent of the country’s active enterprises are small and medium enterprises, but productivity and competitiveness are constrained by limited technology adoption and transfer, restricted access to capital, land and skilled labour, and an uneven capacity to adopt responsible, low-carbon and circular business practices.

The UNDP Country Programme Document for Viet Nam, 2027–2031, responds to these challenges through an integrated, issue-based and portfolio approach linking economic transformation, human development, climate resilience and governance. Under the economic and digital transformation outcome, UNDP will support private-sector competitiveness, responsible business, innovation and technology adoption; expand access to sustainable finance, particularly for small and medium enterprises led by or benefiting women and young people; strengthen resilient livelihoods and shock-responsive social-protection systems; and connect policy reform with investment and implementation at national and subnational levels. Digital and artificial intelligence transformation, gender equality and sustainable finance will serve as cross-cutting accelerators of systemic change.

Within this framework, the Inclusive Growth Unit leads UNDP Viet Nam’s portfolio on inclusive economic and digital transformation. Its work encompasses private-sector development, responsible and sustainable business, small and medium enterprise competitiveness and finance, youth economic empowerment and skills, innovation ecosystems, sustainable and innovative finance, resilient livelihoods, adaptive and shock-responsive social protection, and economic opportunities for groups at risk of being left behind. The Unit works across the Country Office and in partnership with government institutions, provincial authorities, United Nations entities, international financial institutions, development partners, the private sector, social organizations, academia and research institutions to support the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Unit places particular emphasis on connecting inclusive economic transformation with emerging financing opportunities, supporting the development of integrated programmes that translate policy priorities, private-sector innovation and sustainable finance into tangible development results.

Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative and the overall guidance of the Resident Representative, the Programme Specialist - Inclusive Growth serves as a senior policy and programme adviser to Country Office management and provides strategic, technical and managerial leadership for UNDP Viet Nam’s Inclusive Growth portfolio.

The incumbent leads the strategic development, implementation and adaptation of an integrated Inclusive Growth portfolio, contributing principally to the Country Programme outcome on economic and digital transformation while building substantive linkages with climate and environmental sustainability, governance and inclusive human development. The portfolio encompasses inclusive private-sector development, responsible business, innovation and digital transformation, sustainable and innovative finance, resilient livelihoods, adaptive social protection and expanded economic opportunities for groups at risk of being left behind.

The incumbent works closely with the Country Office's Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist to integrate economic and financing perspectives into programme development, identify opportunities for cross-portfolio collaboration and translate emerging policy and financing opportunities into strategic initiatives, partnerships and programme proposals.

The Programme Specialist ensures that UNDP’s policy advice, programmes, partnerships and financing instruments are coherent, evidence-based, gender-responsive, digitally informed and capable of generating scalable and sustainable development results. The incumbent identifies emerging development challenges and opportunities and translates them into strategic initiatives, partnerships and investable programme pipelines.

The Programme Specialist manages and supervises Inclusive Growth Unit personnel and relevant project staff, ensuring strategic prioritization, results-based management, programme quality, financial stewardship, appropriate risk management and compliance with UNDP policies and procedures. The incumbent promotes a collaborative, inclusive and accountable team culture, encourages learning and innovation, and ensures effective cooperation with other programme and operations teams.

The incumbent reports directly to the Deputy Resident Representative and retains accountability for the strategic direction, management, performance and results of the Inclusive Growth Unit. The incumbent works in close technical collaboration with the Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist, drawing on specialized analytical and financing expertise while maintaining clear managerial and programme accountabilities.

The incumbent works closely with government institutions, provincial authorities, United Nations entities, international financial institutions, bilateral and multilateral partners, the private sector, social organizations, academia and UNDP technical and policy networks. The Programme Specialist represents UNDP in relevant policy dialogues, technical forums and partnership platforms, within the authority formally delegated by the Resident Representative.

The incumbent contributes to the Country Office management team and provides senior management with timely advice on programme performance, substantive and operational risks, financing and partnership opportunities, emerging policy priorities and measures required to maintain the strategic relevance and effectiveness of the portfolio.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to respond to changing development and business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. UNDP personnel are therefore expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary arrangements that enable horizontal collaboration and integrated solutions.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Programme Specialist - Inclusive Growth supervises Inclusive Growth Unit personnel and designated project personnel.

Provide strategic and analytical leadership, policy advice and direction for the Inclusive Growth portfolio

- Analyze economic, social and institutional developments, national policy priorities and emerging trends to identify challenges and opportunities for inclusive and sustainable economic transformation.

- Lead the strategic direction and development of an integrated Inclusive Growth portfolio, ensuring alignment with national priorities, the UNSDCF and the UNDP Country Programme.

- Identify and develop strategic programme opportunities in inclusive private-sector development, SME competitiveness, responsible business, innovation and digital transformation, sustainable finance, resilient livelihoods and adaptive social protection.

- Promote synergies within the Inclusive Growth portfolio and across Country Office programmes, working closely with the Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist to integrate economic and financing perspectives into programme strategy.

- Provide evidence-based policy and strategic advice to government counterparts, development partners and Country Office management on inclusive economic transformation, emerging priorities and opportunities, and measures to strengthen development impact.

- Ensure that portfolio design systematically integrates gender equality, disability inclusion, youth empowerment, human rights, environmental sustainability and the principle of leaving no one behind.

Ensure effective portfolio management, programme quality, risk management and team performance

- Lead and supervise the Inclusive Growth Unit, establishing clear workplans, responsibilities and performance expectations, managing staff performance, and promoting professional development, collaboration and accountability.

- Oversee the full programme cycle, ensuring effective planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and closure of programmes and projects in accordance with UNDP policies and procedures.

- Ensure rigorous substantive and operational quality assurance of programme and project documents, implementation arrangements and results frameworks, including the identification, assessment and mitigation of programmatic, fiduciary, environmental, social and reputational risks, in accordance with UNDP standards.

- Oversee portfolio financial performance, delivery, resource utilization and appropriate cost recovery, ensuring timely corrective action to address implementation bottlenecks, underperformance and financial or operational constraints.

- Ensure effective results-based management, including credible indicators, baselines and monitoring systems; high-quality corporate and donor reporting; timely implementation of audit and evaluation recommendations; and systematic use of lessons learned to improve programme performance.

Lead strategic partnerships, private sector engagement and resource mobilization

- Develop and maintain strategic partnerships with national and international partners (government institutions, bi-lateral and multi-lateral donors, IFIs, private sector, civil society), to advance inclusive economic transformation and strengthen UNDP’s positioning and comparative advantage.

- Identify and develop new programme opportunities, translating national development priorities, policy reforms and emerging financing opportunities into integrated, scalable programmes and partnerships, including in private-sector development, innovation, sustainable finance and resilient livelihoods.

- Lead resource mobilization and the development of a forward-looking programme pipeline, overseeing the preparation of high-quality concept notes, project documents, funding proposals and partnership arrangements.

- Engage with national and provincial authorities to identify opportunities for Government Development Financing opportunities in line with national priorities and UNDP comparative advantage.

- Lead the Unit's engagement in relevant partnerships, policy platforms and UN joint programming initiatives, ensuring effective coordination and representation of UNDP within delegated authority.

Promote institutional capacity development, knowledge exchange and learning

- Identify and support institutional capacity-development needs of national and subnational counterparts in areas relevant to inclusive economic transformation, private-sector development, innovation, sustainable finance and social protection.

- Facilitate knowledge exchange, South-South and triangular cooperation, and access to UNDP regional and global expertise to support the adaptation and application of international good practices in Viet Nam.

- Oversee the development and dissemination of knowledge products, lessons learned and practical guidance, drawing on programme experience and partnerships with research institutions, academia and technical networks.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Background

The Security Operations Centre (SOC) is a cost-shared resource established to support the safety and security of personnel, premises, assets and operations across organizations covered by the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS).

The SOC monitors, facilitates and coordinates security communications (voice and data) through the Security Communications System (SCS) within designated operational areas, and maintains administrative datasets that underpin communications readiness, including contact data for UNSMS personnel, offices, vehicles and emergency services.

The post provides essential support to UNDSS and partner entities by ensuring reliable communications, timely escalation and accurate record-keeping in support of security decision-making. The role can be fast-paced and demanding; the incumbent is required to respond promptly to calls for assistance, disseminate accurate instructions, and maintain composure while relaying critical information to UNSMS personnel and other authorised stakeholders.

The SOC Assistant forms part of a response and support function that materially contributes to the protection of UN personnel and continuity of UN operations.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide operational support

- Receive, transmit and relay security and safety messages on behalf of the Designated Official (DO), Security Adviser (SA), Deputy Security Adviser (DSA) and/or Field Security Associates (FSAs), using all approved communication channels in accordance with approved SOPs.

- On receipt of security or safety incident notifications, escalate through the defined channels for follow-up and support without delay, documenting actions in real time.

- Monitor movement of field missions via the SCS as defined by the Security Risk Management (SRM) process and SOPs, ensuring compliance with movement control and check-in requirements.

- Provide immediate support to UNSMS personnel involved in security or safety incidents by alerting response and support functions through the defined channels, maintaining continuous communication with affected personnel, and recording all related information and communications.

- Notify the relevant UNSMS organisation security focal points when their personnel are involved in security or safety incidents, and capture acknowledgements where required.

- Monitor usage of the SCS and enforce adherence to SOPs; guide personnel on appropriate protocols and radio/telephony discipline.

- Verify the operational status and serviceability of SCS equipment and platforms; promptly report anomalies to the designated authority and track remediation.

- Conduct personnel headcounts as instructed by the DO, SA, DSA, and/or FSA or per SOP, ensuring timely and accurate results.

Provide security administrative support

- Maintain contact and residence details of all UNSMS personnel and eligible family members (and, where applicable, implementing partner contacts), as well as contact details for premises and vehicles, in accordance with data protection requirements.

- Maintain current UN warden lists and distribution trees, ensuring regular validation and version control.

- Maintain contact details for response teams, emergency services, host-government counterparts, local authorities and contracted private security providers, direct personnel to the nearest appropriate service during incidents.

- Maintain records and logs of actions and communications in relation to incidents and other critical communications, ensuring accuracy, completeness and retrievability.

- Prepare and submit accurate, timely reports as directed by the Senior Security Professionals (SA/DSA).

- Perform other duties within the functional profile as directed by the Supervisor and/or Security Adviser/Deputy Security Adviser/FSAs.

Support knowledge building and knowledge sharing

- Participate in training on internal procedures for the project staff and provide support to the organization of training and other capacity building activities as needed.

- Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as directed by the Supervisor and/or Security Adviser/Field Security Associate.

Institutional Arrangement
